The Water (prevention and control) Pollution Act has some major defects. With majority of our rivers drying up and the sorry state of Yamuna shows the incompetence of the Act in the present times. The act still talks about wells and streams as being the sources of water. Wells and streams were the sources of water in ancient times but now we have rivers, lakes, ponds, artificial water bodies which have been totally excluded from the purview of this Act. Shockingly this act does not even define what a ‘water pollutant’ is. Nor does water table levels and potable water etc. find any place in the Act. Whatever amendments have taken place in this act have only been with respect to the Environment Protection Act. Thus the act is a complete failure in itself.

These are only a few glaring examples of some of our legislations that lack competency and are ineffective in today’s fast moving world. There are many many more. But what is important is that these reforms should start immediately. Running away from these problems will only make them pile on one another and make them even bigger. India is still a developing nation and if we have to shift 

from the agrarian economy, I would say it is time that we adopt the reformative approach and make the legislations more dynamic in nature. We need more participation of the citizens in bringing about these changes. All this is necessary because we need a clearer picture of our future.

DR. KULMANI SAMAL (JAGATSINGHPUR): Before shedding my views, I would like to salute the wisdom and foresight of the Constitution makers led by Dr. Bhimrao Baba Saheb Ambedkar for the wonderful peace of document that enshrined fundamental values and aspirations of the people. Constitution is a special legal sanctity, consisting of the basic governing principles of the state where the powers and duties of the state organizational framework and the principle functions of the organs of the government as well as of the nation are described. The source of all peoples' and organisations' power, duties and rights are enshrined therein. It is rightly said that the constitution is the supreme law of our land which cannot be superseded even by the Government, since it is an Umbrella Legislation in itself. 

So my point of view is that in a democratic society where various groups of people having different cultures want to stay together and share views with each other in a positive manner, it is necessary to follow certain rules and procedures in order to maintain unity among themselves. India, our motherland is a glaring example in this regard. Here, our predecessors documented the Constitution which has not only made the citizens of this country to follow the rules and procedures rather it has posed a moral commitment to establish the Government to execute the path of development of nation smoothly and peacefully through the letters of the Constitution. This is the most important reason because of which we are united in spite of having a lot of diversities. The Constitution in a healthy democracy provides an enabling framework for the Government as well as for the people to do certain positive things to meet the aspirations and goals of all the sections, whether rich or poor of our society. 

I would like to state that our Constitution is unique as we have borrowed the ideas from many countries since we are deeply entrenched with inequalities of various kinds. The adoption of ideas from different sources has consequently made us enable and empower to take positive measures to overcome the problems caused by diversities. Simply we can imagine the situation of a country where there is no legal document on Rules and Procedures to run the Government or to rule the people. In the same way we can also visualize the situation of not following the ideas enshrined in the Constitution either by the Government or by the people. So I can say that our Constitution is the watchdog of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity which subsequently ensures certain fundamental rights to the citizens and formulates the Directive Principles according to which the democratic set up of the Government runs. As many states in our country are under one union, we describe our Constitution as the happy blending of the unitary and federal structure and hence it is expected to have good cooperation and coordination among all the States and between the State/States and the Country as well. Our Constitution has also clearly outlined the limits of functioning of the executive, legislature and the judiciary. It appropriately prescribes the framework within which the State has to manage to function and the basic structure of the setup is supposed to be sacrosant. Any violation or deviation which goes against the principle is unthinkable and whenever violation or deviation takes place, it creates a lot of disturbances in every segments of society. 

As we all are aware, the Constitution provides for 'equal rights' through different provisions. For example, under Article 14, the Constitution ensures equality before law and equal protection of law. Equal protection of law suggest that the same law shall apply to all. Article 15 says about the prohibition of discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, sex, caste, creed etc. However, in certain instances, special provisions have been initiated for women and children as well as special protections for groups of citizens who are economically and socially depressed. We have created these provisions in our Constitution expecting to maintain equality of all the individuals of our Country. 

To remain committed to the Constitution especially in India is not at all easy since it is diversified uniquely, though diversification at the other hand has made all of us to understand each other, has made us to be tolerant with each other, has made us to share with each other. So by strengthening the democratic values and democratic traditions in our country, we have to generate conscience and to spread awareness among the people of all religions, sects, castes, languages to stand up against the suppression of civil liberties. We have come across the incidents in our country from time to time where the people of different community and religion have involvement in tussles thereby damaging property and killing each other. Even in certain cases in the past the Government has also failed to show commitment to the words of Constitution. Recently, under the NDA rule in which BJP is the leading party, the sense of insecurity among the minorities and scheduled castes has been felt all over the country since certain Hindu organizations have been using the violent and embarrassing method to dominate over minor religious communities. The trend of supremacy by upper castes has also been evident from the incidents of violence against the dalits in different parts of the country. The increasing incidents of violence against minorities and weaker sections of our country are not at all the characters of a matured and diversified civilization. So, it is the time we have to make ourselves concerned to wipe out the undemocratic and unconstitutional nature of our society and to rise to the highest level of an established civilization as per the letters and spirit enshrined in our Constitution. 

*श्री विद्युत वरन महतो (जमशेदपुर) ः भारतीय संविधान के निर्माता डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर के 125वें जयंती व­ाऩ पर सरकार द्वारा 26 नवंबर के दिन को प्रथम "संविधान दिवस" के तौर पर मनाया गया। इसी दिन 66 साल पहले 26 नवंबर को भारतीय संविधान को स्वीकार किया गया था और अधिकारिक तौर पर इसको 26 जनवरी, 1950 में लागू किया गया था। इसी उपलक्ष्य में इस दिन को संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाया जा रहा है। जैसा कि हमारे माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने प्रथम संविधान दिवस के ऐतिहासिक अवसर पर भारत के लोगों को बधाई देते हुए कहा कि यह दिन आपको हमारे संविधान के बारे में और अधिक जानने के लिए प्रेरित करे। उन्होंने कहा कि यह दिन उन सभी महान महिलाओं एवं पुरू­ााो को श्रद्धांजलि है, जिन्होंने भारत को एक संविधान देने के लिए अथक काम किया। उन्होंने कहा, "संविधान के बारे में कोई भी बात तब तक पूरी नहीं होती, जब तक बाबासाहेब भीमराव अंबेडकर के योगदान को याद न किया जाये। आओ, हम हमेशा हमारे संविधान के विचारों और मूल्यों को बरकराकर रखें और एक ऐसे भारत का निर्माण करें, जिससे हमारे संस्थापक पूर्वजों को गर्व महसूस हो सके।"

भारत का संविधान जीवंत एवं सक्रिय दस्तावेज है जो समय के साथ विकसित होता रहा है। भारत को आज़ाद हुए छह दशक से ऊपर हो गए हैं और अपने गणतंत्र को 66 व­ाऩ। इस संदर्भ में यह देखना उचित होगा कि हम जिन लक्ष्यों को लेकर चले थे उन्हें प्राप्त करने में कहाँ तक सफल हुए हैं। भारतीय संविधान के प्रारंभ में मूल उद्देशिका दी गयी है। जिसमें स्प­ट तौर पर लक्ष्यों का उल्लेख है। कहा गया है कि भारत को एक संपूर्ण प्रभुतासंपन्न, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य बनाया जाएगा। साथ ही, सभी नागरिकों को सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनीतिक न्याय, चिंतन, अभिव्यव्ति, विश्वास, आस्था और हैसियत एवं अवसर की समानता तथा व्यव्ति की प्रति­ठा और देश की एकता और अखंडता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए भाईचारे की गारंटी दी जाएगी।

व­ाऩ 1949 में 26 नवंबर को संविधान सभा में बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर ने एक बात कही थी कि-"" आज इस संविधान की अच्छाईयां गिनाने का कोई खास मतलब नहीं है। संविधान कितना ही अच्छा हो, अगर इसका इस्तेमाल करने वाले लोग बुरे होंगे तो यह बुरा साबित होगा। अगर संविधान बुरा है है, पर उसका इस्तेमाल करने वाले लोग अच्छे होंगे तो फिर भी संविधान अच्छा साबित होगा। ऐसे में जिन लोगों के ऊपर संविधान लागू करने की जिम्मेदारी लागू होती है, यह उन पर निर्भर करता है कि वे संविधान को कितनी ईमानदारी और प्रभावी ढंग से लागू करते हैं।""

आज की सबसे बड़ी जरूरत है कि हम भारत के लोग संविधान को पढ़ें, जाने और उसमें अपना विश्वास प्रगाढ़ करें। यह महज एक किताब नहीं है, यह एक तसव्वुर है कि हम बर्तानिया उपनिवेशवाद यानी गुलामी और गरीबी, जातिवाद से मुव्त होकर किस तरह का मुल्क बनाना चाहते हैं। मैं प्रधानमंत्री के आह्वान को दोहराते हुए अपनी बात को विराम देना चाहता हॅं...........आओ, हम हमेशा हमारे संविधान के विचारों और मूल्यों को बरकरार रखें और एक ऐसे भारत का निर्माण करें, जिससे हमारे संस्थापक पूर्वजों को गर्व महसूस हो सके।

SHRI GANAJAN KIRTIKAR (MUMBAI NORTH WEST): As we all know, Dr. Ambedkar was viewed as messiah of dalits and downtrodden in India. He was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. 

We should not forget the fact that the then Congress Government did not award Bharat Ratna to Dr. Ambedkar in time. Many political parties use Babasaheb's name only for getting Dalit votes. That should not be the motto of the political parties. They shed crocodile tears on his memory. They are not true to the ideals and philosophy of Dr. Ambedkar. After violent and prolonged agitation renaming of Babasaheb Ambedkar's name was fulfilled. Then the change occurred. 

Nowadays, there is a tendency among political parties to use the name of Dr. Ambedkar to attract Dalit votes. They should not use Babasaheb's name for political purposes. Very recently, the NDA Government finally decided to inaugurate the memorial of Babasaheb at Indu Mills, Mumbai. It was inaugurated by the Prime Minister, Mr. Narendra Modi. Subsequently, the Government purchased London-based house of Dr. Ambedkar which was also inaugurated recently. 

But unfortunately for both the functions, representatives of Shiv Sena and other political parties were ignored. There had been a delay in commissioning the project at Indu Mills because of the petty politics and played by the Congress Party. 

I demand from the Government to carry Dr. Ambedkar's photo on future Indian currency notes. This will also be a true tribute to him. 

It gives me pleasure to express on behalf of Shiv Sena Party and on my own behalf my deep obeisance to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar on the occasion of his 125th Birthday Anniversary. 

KUMARI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE (UDUPI CHIKMAGALUR): India salutes Dr. B.R. Ambedkar for his contribution to Constitution of India. He has given voice to voiceless people of India. We should really think on this line. 

SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH (MAVELIKKARA): Now our nation is celebrating the 125th birth anniversary of the Architect of Indian Constitution, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. As a person who toiled throughout his life for the socio-economic development of the people which he belongs to, fighting against all odds of the society in the early half of the 20th Century, it will be a great tribute to him if we discuss the issues pertaining to the socio-economic development of Dalits and tribes in this house comprehensively, apart from discussing other issues pertaining to Constitution and its upkeeping. 

The contributions of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar were sterling not only for the Dalits of India, but for the whole nation. The constitutional safeguards visualized in the Constitution for SC/ST are with an objective to safeguard them from the upper caste chauvinistic elements, to protect them from discrimination, humiliation, for ensuring them education, employment and to enable them to stand in their own feet. 

But it is quite unfortunate and a shame that even after 68 years of independence, the attacks against the Dalits and tribes are increasing and social discrimination and gap between the dalits and other caste groups are widening. Are we the law makers who are responsible for this shame or the law implementers are responsible or the civil society is responsible for it. 

Normally socio-economic development helps eliminate discrimination. Whereas, in India, social discrimination increases with socio-economic development. As some advertisement says, "It happens only in India".

The atrocities against the Dalits are on the increase, which is never heard before in the history of independent India. Whenever the BJP led NDA government is in power, the atrocities and crime against Dalits, Adivasis and people among the downtrodden societies are on the increase. The upper caste chauvinistic elements have no guilt in unleashing terror in the minds of the Dalits and Adivasis. 

Earlier the main culprits indulged in atrocities against Dalits were Upper caste people, but now the OBC groups also are in the forefront in attacking the Dalits. The recent incidents that occurred in Maharashtra in the killing of a Dalit boy for playing caller tune on Babasaheb and the beating of a Dalit girl for falling shadow on a man at Madhya Pradesh are classic example of new found resurgence of atrocities on Dalits by OBC groups. 

Do the OBC people have sanskritised as upper caste and feeling that Dalits are not eligible to live in the society? Did they become Brahminical that they can do whatever they want? Or because they think that now the country is ruled by an OBC Prime Minister and we can do whatever we want and nobody will question us?

Recently the killing of two children and family members from dalit community in Haryana has brought shame to the whole nation. It is not the killing which pains the whole nation, the utterance of certain Honourable Ministers that pains us a lot. They are not even giving the status of a stray dog to the dalit. What a shame to the nation!!

Though the atrocities on the Dalits are increasing nobody from the ruling party, BJP voiced their protest against this. Now in India the majority of the MPs are from BJP. More than 75% belongs to BJP. So far did anyone raise the voice against the crime on SC/ST in India?

The atrocities on Dalits are very high and increasing in BJP ruled states like Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra. The authorities are reluctant to register cases against the culprits and put them behind the bars. The data of Crime Records Bureau and the recent press new says this. 

The age old Sutras and Smritis have not treated the Dalits as human beings. Traditionally they are outcastes and the 'Nitisastra" of present rulers are also ruled by the age old Smritis only. The NDA government is trying to bring in the brahminical cult back into effect. 

Let me ask one small question? Even though the majority of the SC/ST members in the Lok Sabha belong to BJP, how many MPs from among them are in key positions? How many Cabinet Minister are there? How many MOS from among them? How many SC/ST have been appointed as Governors in your tenure? How many Secretaries to Government from SC/ST appointed so far by the present government? How many persons from SC/ST posted in key positions in the government and PSU?

The 23% of our population belongs to Dalits and Adivasis. But how many percent of the Ministers were from that community? How many percent of Secretary to Government from that community? How many percent of Governors from that Community? How many Chief Ministers from that community in BJP ruled states? The statistics in these cases can't tell a lie, as they are obvious. 

BJP has only two Cabinet Ministers from SC/ST. One from SC and one from ST. Two Ministers to represent the 23% of population. There are 5 cabinet ministers in this government from among Brahmins alone, whereas the total population of Brahmins in India is only 4.6%. Is it because BJP don't have qualified persons from among Dalits/ST to appoint as Ministers. 

Compare this with the UPA rule. UPA has 7cabinet ministers from among dalits including Minister of Home, Railways, etc. the Hon. Speaker of the House also was a Dalit. What I want to substantiate here is that the atrocities against the Dalits now a days is reflection of the general attitude of the Government, the ruling party and the philosophy which governs them. 

Hon'ble Prime Minister exhorts the government to organize year long programmes to celebrate 125th birth year of Baba Saheb Ambedkar. If this announcement is with commitment and conviction the first step should be to give justice to this community in government and in governance. Give them the due share in power. Otherwise the entire announcement will only end up as routine sermons. 

If you want to end the atrocities, discrimination and injustice to dalits, mere sermons will not do. Affirmative action is required. Give them their share of power, empower them. As a token of respect to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, I request the government to appoint as many number of Ministers in government from SC/ST communities according to the percentage of population. 

The problem is not only of atrocities against the Dalits, rather it is only one among several other social injustices the community is facing. 

Over the years successive governments have introduced so many positive actions for the development of Dalits. 

There is a special component for SCs and STs in the plan funds, called SCSP and TSP. Funds are being set apart exclusively in all plan heads for SCP and TSP. it started from 1974 onwards by Smt. Indira Gandhi, one of the greatest visionary leaders of India. 

Each and every development departments are supposed to utilize these funds only for the benefits of the communities. Still the fate of the Dalits in India remains the same. It is said that if the funds set apart for the development of Dalits and Tribes in India are deposited in their personal accounts, all of them would have been lakhpathis though not crorepathis. 

Why the funds are not reaching the Dalits? Who is responsible for this? The issues are many. I am not taking this opportunity to discuss this issue in detail, since the subject is different. But if we want to ensure the development of Dalits and ensure social democracy and inclusive democracy, then the act of parliament is required to be passed on the implementation of SCSP and TSP funds. 

Such an Act, should lay down the legislative framework for planning in all parameters of development, security and social dignity for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. 

A specific Act with sufficient safeguards will ensure the accelerated development of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes with emphasis on economic, educational and human development and emancipation, with the goal of promoting equity for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and reducing the gaps between Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and other castes. 

If the funds set apart are diverted, misappropriated or unutilized the persons responsible should be identified and provisions may be given for the action against the erring officers. Only with a comprehensive legislation on planning, implementing and monitoring of SCSP/TSP schemes, the development disparities among SCs and STs can be solved in our country. 

Taking into account of the predicament of the SCSP and STP programmes and to resolve them, UPA Government has taken steps to introduce a bill in the Parliament as per the guidance of Madam Soniaji. Now it is in cold storage of the Government. I strongly urge Government that the bill may be considered now and please introduce and pass the special component plan for the Scheduled Castes and Tribal Sub-Plan for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Authorities (Planning, Allocation and Utilization of Financial Resources) Act immediately. 

I take this occasion to raise another major problem faced by the SC/ST, that is, regarding their promotion in government services. As per the Constitution , the reservation in government jobs for SC/ST is guaranteed during entry in services. Whereas, there is no uniform norms which governs reservation in promotion to the employees belongs to SC/ST communities. Several State Governments are ensuring promotion to Dalit officers, but it is not enforced constitutionally and hence the defaults are not being seriously viewed. 

The employees and officers from SC/ST communities are deprived of their promotions due the apathy of bureaucracy. The mere reason that they are born in SC/ST community, these employees are getting only step motherly treatment. The senior officers very seldom give the Dalit officers high grades enabling them to get promotions. The Dalit Officers are often ill-treated on caste grounds. 

The UPA government had introduced the bill to ensure reservation in promotion to Dalit officers and passed in the Rajya Sabha, Whereas it was defeated in Lok Sabha. 

The effort of State Governments to ensure reservation of Dalits in promotion is jeopardized due to interventions of various courts. Since there is no clear Law enacted by Parliament on reservation in promotion, the intervention by Hon. Courts are bound to happen. 

Recently the hon. Patna High Court has set aside a state Government resolution that provided for reservation with consequential seniority in promotions to government employees belonging to SC/ST categories. 

We need to ensure justice to the employees from Dalit communities. The age old discrimination should be stopped. The social discrimination towards the dalits is not ornamental for a nation thriving to be wealthiest, modern and socially developed one. Mainstreaming dalits by all means is required for peace, amity and development.

I request the Central Government to reintroduce and pass the Bill for ensuring reservation in promotion to SC/ST employees in Lok Sabha at the earliest and ensure natural and social justice to the deprived communities. 

A Central Act to streamline SCSP/TSP programmes and an Act for the reservation in promotion of SC/ST officers is a precondition for elimination of atrocities against the Dalits. They will bring in faster development and reduces development disparities which may positively impact on social discrimination. 

By law we have abolished untouchability. But now the Dalits are getting beaten for falling shadow on a caste Hindu. Recently at village Ganeshpura in Chattarpur in Madhya Pradesh a dalit girl was beaten up by higher caste women after the victim's shadow fell on a muscleman belonging to their family. And that too, when the girl was fetching water from the village hand pump. The news says that it is with great difficulty that the victims got the case registered in the police station. 

In Ansurda Village, Osmanabad in Maharashtra, 13 families are facing boycott, that they are forced to relocate from their village. The reason the Dalits took out a procession to mark the birth anniversary of Babasaheb Ambedkar and played a song praising him. They are not allowed to drink water from public taps and their cattle were barred from grazing in the village. Shopkeepers are asked not to give them groceries. Adding to the woes of Dalits, the police has refused to register the case under SC/ST Atrocities Prevention Act. 

Again, in Maharashtra, a Dalit youth was brutally killed over Ambedkar ringtone. Reason is that the victims' phone rang a ringtone praising Babasaheb Ambedkar. The assailants, who belonged to the dominant Maratha and OBC communities, ran their bike repeatedly over the victim's body, mutilating it. 

While speaking in the Constituent Assembly Babasaheb Ambedkar said and I quote, "Will history repeat itself? It is this thought which fills me with anxiety. This anxiety is deepened by the realization of the fact that in addition to our old enemies in the form of castes and creed we are going to have many political parties with diverse and opposing political creeds. Will Indians place the country above their creed or will they place creed above country? I do not know. But this much is certain that if the parties place creed above country, our independence will be put in jeopardy a second time and probably be lost forever. This eventually we must all resolutely guard against. We must be determined to defend our independence with the last drop of our blood".

The situation across the country and atrocities against the Dalits has forced us to fear that the fear of Babasaheb Ambedkar is going to be true. The attack on the Dalits is increasing day by day, especially by caste Hindus. The intolerance level reached to such a height that the high caste groups can't even hear the word Jaibhim or a song on Babasaheb Ambedkar. Will they ask for the change of Indian Constitution as Dr. Ambedkar is the architect of it.?

Even shadow of a dalit should not touch a non-dalit. Is it not untouchability?

As per Article 17 of the Constitution of India "Untouchability" is abolished. That is when we adopted this Constitution, 65 years back. 12 years before, I was born. In my childhood, on several occasions, I also had the humiliation. Even now our society is not ready to give up this shame, rather it is increasing. Are we not ashamed of it?

We are talking about nationalism. Do the dalits not belong to this nationalistic group? Are they not Indians? Are they migrated along with other migrants? My modesty does not allow me to attack anyone on the basis of caste or creed. But please remember that there is a limit for everything.

If you are not ready to treat them as human beings, then why trying for Ghar Vapasi? Before doing Ghar Vapasi, please try to understand human values and learn to protect it. 

In several states the elected members of local Self Government institutions from among SC/ST are not even allowed to sit in chairs and preside the meetings. There are instances where SC/ST are asked to sit on floor in such meetings. 

Offences against the dignity of the dalits and STs are increasing day by day. Many at times it is being done willfully and not by mistake. But law enforcing authorities are not ready to take action against these crimes. 

As I have already mentioned earlier, even after we have implemented the POA Act 25 years ago, the attitude of the nation towards the Dalits in our society has not improved, rather worsened as is implicated by introducing a more stringent amendment. 

It is not good for the nation. The patience of downtrodden in the country should not be tested. As it is rightly said by Babasaheb Ambedkar, I quote, "These down-trodden classes are tired of being governed. They are impatient to govern themselves. This urge for self-realization in the down-trodden classes must not be allowed to devolve into a struggle or class war. It would lead to a division of the House. That would indeed be a day of disaster". I hope and wish it may not happen. 

Now, the development schemes for Dalits also get sidelined. The funds for their development has been curtailed. The SCSP/TSP introduced by Congress government and the allotment of funds according to the percentage of population is under threat. The reduction of funds for social development schemes have affected the development of dalits and tribes. I urge to government that the plan funds for SC/ST development should be according to population. 

Article 46 of Directive Principles of the Constitution has ensured reservation policy in employment, which has worked positively towards bringing the dalits and adivasis in the public sector. While the reservations is limited only in the public sector, it has restricted the employment opportunities in the private sector. With constant decrease in the public jobs, there is an immediate need for legislation of reservation in the private sector. 

Dalit women have been facing three fold discrimination in the society, with Caste, class and gender dimensions overshadow their access to development. The Dalit women are also usual target to physical and sexual violence in the society. There should be inclusive policies and effective implementation for ensuring that the Dalit women and girls are protected and guided towards holistic development including education, employment, entrepreneurship and health. 

Dalits are often associated with unclean occupations like manual scavenging as well as traditionally forced occupations like devdasi system. The efforts towards abolishing manual scavenging and devdasi system have not found wide appeal in the Indian society. With dalits are often considered for such unclean jobs have blocked their efforts to pursue other jobs. Thus for considerable development of those still involved in manual scavenging and forced occupations like devdasi system, the legislation should be implemented effectively and perpetrators be punished. 

With adoption of Sustainable Development Goals in September, national agenda of implementation should focus on the inclusion and participation of the Dalits and Adivasis. With SDGs giving the developmental importance to the excluded and discriminated communities, the policies should ensure effective and direct engagement of Dalits and Adivasis for real development. With more than 21 crores of Dalits in India, their development should be paramount importance. 

The Constitution guaranteed rights and privileges to tribes and dalits should be protected at cost. There should be stringent action to reduce social discrimination and to ensure social equity in the society and that should be the fitting tribute to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, the architect of our Constitution. 

DR. K. GOPAL (NAGAPATTINAM): Hon. Deputy Speaker, Sir, I would like to express my profound thanks and indebtedness to our beloved leader hon. Chief Minister Dr. Amma for giving me an opportunity to speak on behalf of our AIADMK party in this august house. 

The topic of discussion ‘the commitment to India’s Constitution’ as a part of 125th Birth Anniversary celebration of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is indeed the need of the hour. “Remembering the past and dreaming about the good future while working hard to meet both ends in the present” is an exclusive characteristic of human beings.

This is an occasion to revere and remember the Father of Indian Constitution Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and our commitment to the Constitution of India. It was on the same day (26th November) in 1949 that the 248 members present in the then Constituent Assembly put their assent on the Draft Constitution and got it passed. 

Earlier on the 29th of August 1947, the Drafting Committee was formed under the Chairmanship of Baba Saheb Dr. Bhim Rao Ambedkar comprising of eminent personalities like N. Gopalaswamy Aiyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Syed Mohammed Saadulla, K.M. Munshi, B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan. Later N. Madhav Rao was appointed in B.R. Mitter’s place and T.T. Krishnamachari was appointed in the vacancy caused by the death of D. P. Khaitan. 

Making of Indian Constitution was a Himalayan task. It required the knowledge of Constitutions of various countries, deep knowledge of law and Justice and a thorough understanding of Indian History and Culture. It took two years eleven months and eighteen days to make the Draft Constitution. The Drafting Committee under the chairmanship of Dr. Ambedkar produced such a complete and commendable Constitution which not only succeeded in giving a viable democracy to India but in upholding and maintaining unity in diversity of Indian society and culture. 

Today we have assembled here in this august house not merely to shower our lavish praise on the greatness of Baba Saheb and the Constitution of India. We are here to discuss and evaluate the performance of our Governments, both at present and in the past, their commitment to adhere to the constitutional provisions and what is really expected out of the Governments. One pertinent question arises in our minds today is that whether we are doing enough justice to the commitment to the great man and his great work, the Constitution of India. Here comes the time to think and re-think, to do critical analysis of the performances of the Governments, good or bad, lapses and mistakes made in the past till today and to find a path-breaking solution to the still unsolved problems affecting peace prosperity, progress and development of the Nation. 

It is really painful to see various problems in the society which affect the peaceful co-existence, communal harmony. We need to find a solution to the grave problem of intolerance and communal violence. The solution is very much in our Constitution. In this regard the comment of Dr. Ambedkar on 25th November 1949 is remarkable. He said : “The constitution, I offered may be good or bad, it will depend on how the men in office use it.” These words are true, immortal and holds good forever. It means however good a Constitution may be, if the executors fail to deliver, it may be termed as a bad one. Dr. Ambedkar‘s words are prophetic and that is why, he is considered to be the Modern Manu. 

Without doubt Dr. Ambedkar was a great son of India and as the architect of Indian Constitution, his contribution remains unmatched. He stood against untouchability and oppression in the name of caste and class. This has not only immortalised him, but lifted the deprived, the depressed and the down-trodden from the deep pit of discrimination. Though he was intent upon the uplift of the oppressed people, his core focus was very much on the unity, integrity and glorification of the mother India despite all the contradictions and diversities. He believed that only in unification and not in the disintegration lies the good of all.

The various provisions included in the Constitution stand testimony to ideals and great mind of Dr. Ambedkar. The secular sentiments of the Constitution are refulgent of his liberal and all-assimilative mindset. The posthumous award of Bharat Ratna to him was really most deserved. But no amount of awards or laurels can match his personality, pursuits and performances. The world will remember him as a messiah and as a man of destiny, who designed and defined the destiny of a great nation and its people. 

Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was a multifaceted personality. He was a nationalist, jurist, social reformer, philosopher, historian, orator, prolific writer, economist, scholar and a revolutionary leader. To achieve the very best in all these spheres of life is simply outstanding and that too, from an oppressed Dalit family background, in those times, makes him the most remarkable leader India has ever had. The life and achievements of Dr. Ambedkar are worthy of writing with golden letters in the history of the nation and the entire human history. 

Notwithstanding the caste discrimination and social injustice he went on to achieve the best throughout his brilliant and illuminating academic career. Dr. Ambedkar had strongly believed that political independence cannot assure either social solidarity or national integration in the absence of social justice. He propagated that fundamental rights have little meaning to the people in the absence of social democracy. 

Dr. Ambedkar was one of the very few Indian statesman-politicians who actively participated in the discussions on constitutional matters from the Monsford Reforms (1919) to the Cabinet Mission (1946) proposals. The Round Table Conference was the landmark in the history of the Indian Constitution. Being invited to discuss on constitutional matters Ambedkar demanded independence and hoped that the people of India would be able to redress their grievances by political power and this political power will come to them under the Swaraj constitution.

At the first session of Round Table Conference, he gave a clear warning to the British Government saying, “I am afraid it is not sufficiently realized that in the present temper of the country, no Constitution will be workable which is not acceptable to the majority of the people. The time when you were to choose and India was to accept is gone, never to return. Let the consent of the people and not the accident of the logic be the touchstone of your new constitution, if you desire that it should be worked. …”

He advocated for a Government which was a responsible Government formed by the representatives of the people. Dr. Ambedkar did not want to impose a constitution on the Indians, but he submitted that the opinion of the people about the manner in which they desired to be governed must be accepted. “The best government rests on the people, and not on the few persons and not on the property, not on the authority but on the free development of public opinion”. 

Dr. Ambedkar examined the functioning of a democratic government on the basis of stability and responsibility. As regards the character of the constitution, “it was Federal in form and unitary in spirit.” It established a dual polity with the Union at the Centre and the States at the periphery, each endowed with sovereign powers to be exercised in the field assigned to them respectively by the Constitution.

In his draft Constitution Dr. Ambedkar has advocated for a strong central authority to save minorities from the misrule of majority and also as the centre has the responsibility to work for a common end and for the general interests of the country as a whole. His concept of Federalism meant that the State was a federation in normalcy, but unitary in emergency. But the ground reality today is that the Union Governments at the Centre are trying to overpower the very federal system of Centre-State relationship. Union Governments whether UPA or NDA try only to crush the rights of the States and try to dominate, destabilize and derail the powers entrusted on the State Governments by the constitution of India.

The Goods and Services Tax (GST) proposed by the Centre is one such danger to the developed and productive states. Our Honourable Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma has voiced her concerns about the impact of the proposed GST on the fiscal autonomy of the States and the huge revenue loss it is likely to cause to a manufacturing and net exporting state like Tamil Nadu. Likewise the Inordinate delay in releasing the Central Sales Tax Compensation is yet another hindrance due to autocracy of the Centre.

The Finance Bill 2013 contains an extremely retrograde, anti-federal provision. Clause 7 of the Bill amended Section 40 of the income Tax Act which has made any levy by a State government by way of privilege fee, license fee, royalty etc., on State Public sector Undertakings not deductible for the purpose of computation of income. All such levies are legitimate statutory levies and such were deductible from the income of the State Public Sector Undertakings under section 37 of the income tax act, clause 7 of the Finance Bill 2013 is objectionable because it amounts to an indirect taxation of the income of the State Governments and hence is a violation of the spirit of the Article 289 of the constitution of India.

The National Eligibility Cum Entrance Test (NEET) introduced by the Medical Council of India and Dental Council of India was opposed and objected by our honourable Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma as the NEET for the UG and PG Medical and Dental courses will affect the prospects of Students from rural areas and poorer socio-economic backgrounds and thus will derail the social justice up hold by the Tamil Nadu State by the way of 69% reservation for the SC/ST, MBC and BC candidates. The provisions made in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution of India. The Government of India is under an obligation to take measures for the development of these languages, such that "they grow rapidly in richness and become effective means of communicating modern knowledge. Any candidate appearing in an examination conducted for public service at a higher level is entitled to use any of these 20 languages as the medium in which he or she answers the paper. States within India have the liberty and powers to specify their own official language(s) through legislation 

Recently, Our Chief Minister Dr. Amma had raised her voice against announcement of the Centre to celebrate Sanskrit Week celebrations in schools and wrote a letter to Prime Minister stating that it would be appropriate to have organized a ‘Classical Language Week’ in each state based on its linguistic heritage. “Tamil Nadu has a rich cultural heritage based on the ancient Tamil language. There has also been a strong social justice and language movement in the state and an official celebration of ‘Sanskrit week’ in Tamil Nadu is highly inappropriate. She asked the Prime Minister to advise officials to suitably modify the letter to enable each state, to organize celebrations in tune with the language and culture of the state keeping with the cultural and linguistic sensitivities in a diverse country. 

These are few instances how an Autocratic Centre could crush the federal rights of the states as per the constitution. What Dr. Ambedkar warned while introducing the draft copy of constitution will certainly happen if the Governments at the Centre continue to try and infringe up on the federal powers of the States duly empowered by the constitution.

When the Constitution Makers framed the Indian Constitution, they gave more importance to the States, knowing full well, the practical problems that the States face. At that time, they also kept in mind the principle of 'Unity in Diversity'. Right from that time, all of them recognized that there was diversity in languages that different people spoke, diversity in culture that people followed and also diversity in food habits. At the same time, they preserved unity, by giving the necessary powers to the States. 

During the course of time, one after the other, almost all the powers of the States were taken away by the Centre whichever Party ruled the Centre. Since they monopolized all the powers, what we see today is instead of unity, we are slightly drifting towards unitary States. 

The Constitution makers, very thoughtfully, made three Lists - State List, Central List and Concurrent List - and included relevant subjects in each. For example, subjects like education and others were taken out of the State List and included in the Concurrent List, even without consulting the States. 

In this connection, I want to make a request that if the Centre really wants to have true federalism and preserve unity in diversity, whenever any subject is taken out of the State List, the Centre must take the consent of all the States because it would amount to tinkering with the States' rights. In the Concurrent List, even though the States have the right to enact laws, if the Centre enacts a similar one, then the Central Law supersedes the State's Law. So, in such cases, the Centre should take the consent from all the States, and this is our humble request to the Centre.

Presently, Hindi is made the official language of the country. Our request regarding the language issue is this. If the Centre is supporting federalism, then, it should respect all the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution and make Tamil and all other such languages as "Indian national official languages". Then only, we can say that we have unity in diversity and have national integration. In this connection, I want to remind the House that the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Hon. Amma has been insisting, all along, that the Central Government has to accept that Tamil and other languages included in the 8th Schedule, are "Indian national official languages", and the Centre should take earnest steps and make necessary announcement in this regard. I request that the Centre, taking note of this point, should move in this direction and make such an announcement immediately.

On the issue of reservation, I want to tell the House that it was in Tamil Nadu in 1924, when the Justice Party was ruling Madras Presidency, it introduced 'Reservation Policy', for the first time in India, to make reservation for the suppressed and the oppressed.

Dr. Ambedkar observed “Equality of opportunity” as the most important of Fundamental Rights. For him Article 32 is the soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it. To him, fundamental rights would mean establishment of equality and liberty in order to reform our social system. The Directive Principles of State Policy contained the positive obligations of the State towards its citizens. The Directives were meant to ensure social and economic democracy which was secured by the provisions of fundamental rights in a written Constitution.

The Constitution is a dynamic document and it should grow with the growth of the Nation and should suit the changing needs and circumstances. Dr. Ambedkar urged the necessity of amendments to the Constitution. But these amendments should not affect the federal structure and Centre- State relationship which is vital in good governance and administration. 

Dr. Ambedkar advocated the abolition of privileges on the basis of caste or class chauvinism and vigorously fought for the liberty, self-respect and dignity of the individual. Dr. Ambedkar incorporated in the Constitution provisions strong enough to hold the country together both in peace and war time. He provided special safeguards to the minorities and certain oppressed classes who are socially and educationally backward. Babasaheb urged the importance of ‘one man, one value’ and ‘one man, one vote’. He worked for securing equal protection of laws for every citizen as also the freedom of profession and equality of opportunity.

In Tamil Nadu we were fortunate to have social reformers of highest order, Thanthai Periyar E.V.R., Arignar Anna, Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G.R who held the principles of social justice and good governance as their two eyes. We are blessed to have the dynamic leader par excellence Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma who is the epitome of the three great leaders. 

Thanthai Periyar E.V.R. was considered the Ambedkar of the South. He devoted his entire life to fight against caste and class discrimination and to uphold social justice. He worked for the equality and social justice of oppressed people for seven decades. Arignar Anna gave the philosophy of Kadamai, Kanniyam, Kattuppadu which reflects essence of all good principles of our Constitution in a nutshell. Our Party Founder Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G.R, gave new dimension to Tamil Nadu politics and sowed the seeds for the betterment of socio-economic and educational status of the people. 

Today the Hon. Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma has given her heart and soul for the overall development and upliftment of poor, down-trodden people in Tamil Nadu. 

She has introduced numerous innovative projects and schemes for the benefit of the rural and urban poor, down-trodden people particularly women. The political prowess and achievements of our Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma are simply unmatched. Her political acumen and administrative skills brought tremendous development in the socio-economic – educational status of poor, down-trodden, oppressed women and minorities in Tamil Nadu. 

She is the champion of social justice and women’s rights. She fought bravely against evil forces to uphold 69% reservation in education and advocated for a constitutional amendment to ensure that the weaker sections of society to get 69% reservation. For that great achievement she is hailed by the people of Tamil Nadu as ‘Brave Leader who saved social justice’.

Women in India face myriad cultural challenges that impede their social advancement. Women throughout the world face systematic gender-based discrimination and are regularly denied the right to life and security of person, recourse to legal rights, health care, education, employment, inheritance, and freedom of movement. During the previous tenures as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Dr. Amma introduced a number of novel schemes for women and female children which have won accolades in our Country and abroad. 

The flagship schemes of Amma Government are – the Girl Child Protection Scheme; the 4-gram gold coin for the Thirumangalyam (Mangalsutra) and 50,000 rupees grant for the marriage of impoverished women; Widow Remarriage Assistance Scheme; Orphan Girls’ Marriage Assistance Scheme; Inter-caste Marriage Assistance Scheme; financial assistance to young destitute girls for pursuing higher education; cradle baby scheme for girl children to prevent infanticide 

Amma strongly condemned all kinds of crimes perpetrated against women and sought to improve their livelihood opportunities so that they are empowered financially and socially, in order to stand up against any injustice meted out to them. 

Women Self-help Groups, formed by Amma Government, have emerged as an indomitable force that has transformed the status of women, and liberated them from discriminatory codes and cultural stigma. This is only the beginning - the best is yet to come. 

The establishment of All-Women Police Stations was pioneered by Amma Government in 1992 was specifically aimed at tackling and giving an impetus to investigation in crimes against women, and to respond swiftly to complaints given by women. It has been a landmark achievement in the path of women empowerment in Tamil Nadu and has set the beacon for other States to follow. 

The poor, marginalized and vulnerable live in a parallel world where economic poverty is structurally, politically and socially defined. Amma gave deep thought to this concept, and have been devising Government schemes with pro-poor initiatives and inclusive strategies, to improve their economic well-being. A desire to achieve for people the highest attainable standard of health, adequate housing, education, economic opportunities and social security for a dignified life. It is a collective responsibility to ensure that the cherished constitutional entitlements reach the poorest of the poor. 

With great pride we proudly consider our Idaya Deivam Puratchi Thalaivi Dr. Amma as the Living Ambedkar. Her far-sighted vision has transformed Tamil Nadu into number one State where people could live healthy, wealth, happy life with peaceful co-existence and communal harmony.

Before I conclude, it is high time for all of us here to take a pledge to fulfil the dream, vision and mission of Dr. Ambedkar and meticulously follow the ideals in his immortal work, the Constitution of India.

*डॉ. सुनील बलीराम गायकवाड़ (लातूर) ः जब अंग्रेज भारत छोड़कर जाने को तैयार हुए और इसकी प्रक्रिया शुरू हुई तो इससे पहले कांस्टीटय़ूशनल सेटलमेंट करने की बात उठी। अंग्रेजों ने यह तय करना जरूरी समझा कि भारत की सत्ता के हस्तांतरण के बाद भारत में लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था ही लागू हो। इस पूरी प्रक्रिया में बाबासाहेब डॉ. अंबेडकर की प्रमुख भूमिका रही है।

भारत का संविधान 26 नवंबर, 1949 को स्वीकार किया गया। संविधान के मायने क्या होते हैं? शायद उस समय भारत के लोगों को यह पता नहीं था, लेकिन दुनिया में संविधान का महत्व स्थापित हो चुका था।

संविधान असल में समूह में बंटे लोग जो रा­ट्र बनाना चाहते हैं, को मानवीय अधिकार दिलवाता है, जिसके तहत लोगों के लिए स्वतंत्रता, बंधुता, न्याय और समानता की व्यवस्था का निर्माण करता है। यह सभी मनु­यों को एक समान अधिकार देता है और मनु­यों के बीच भेदभाव को अपराध भी घो­िात करता है। 1950 के बाद विश्व के लगभग 50 देशों ने अपना संविधान बनाया, भारत उनमें सबसे पहला है। हालांकि यह भी साफ करना जरूरी है कि आज़ादी के आंदोलन और भारत के संविधान का आपस में कोई संबंध नहीं है। दोनों अलग-अलग घटनाएं हैं। जब सन 1928 में साइमन कमीशन का भारत में आगमन हुआ तो उस समय कंस्टीटय़ूशनल सेटलमेंट (संवैधानिक) की बात उठी, क्योंकि भारत एक विभाजित देश है और यह कई जातियों, धर्मों, रीति-रिवाजों, समुदायों और क्षेत्रों में बंटा हुआ है। ब्रिटिश लोग और भारत के लोग दोनों इस बात को जानते थे। संविधान निर्माण के जरिए इन बिखरे हुए लोगों के समुदाय को एक रा­ट्र करने की कोशिश की गई, हालांकि भारत इसमें कितना सफल हो पाया है, यह एक गंभीर बहस का मुद्दा है।

अंग्रेजों ने यह तय करना जरूरी समझा कि भारत को सत्ता के हस्तांतरण के बाद भारत में लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था ही लागू हो। इस पूरी प्रक्रिया में बाबासाहेब डाँ. अंबेडकर की प्रमुख भूमिका रही। अगर हम बाबासाहेब के संपूर्ण जीवन को देखें तो यह साफ होता है कि कंस्टीटय़ूशनल सेटलमेंट को लेकर वह कितने गंभीर थे।

बाबासाहेब इस बात को लेकर हमेशा सक्रिय रहे कि भारत में कंस्टीटय़ूशनल सेटलमेंट कैसे हो। उनका मानना था कि देश में सामाजिक क्रांति तभी स्थायी होगा, जब संवैधानिक गारंटी होगी। क्योंकि वह संविधान के जरिए देश में समानता स्थापित करना चाहते थे। वह जानते थे कि जाति और जन्म के आधार पर किसी काम को करने की बाध्यता या फिर न करने की मनाही न हो। डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर संविधान के जरिए इन चीजों को खत्म करना चाहते थे। वह चाहते थे कि संविधान के जरिए भारत से असमानता खत्म हो और समानता आ जाए। लोगों को उनके मूलभूत अधिकार (फंडामेंटल राइट्स) को देकर गारंटी मिले। भारत में सामाजिक क्रांति कामयाब हो रही थी, वहीं दूसरी ओर देश अंग्रेजों की गुलामी से आज़ाद हो रहा था। संवैधानिक तौर पर भारत में जाति और वर्ण जैसी व्यवस्था के तहत बनाए गए कानून के खत्म होने का वव्त आ गया था। साहू महाराज, ज्योतिबाफूले, नारायना गुरू और बाबासाहेब डॉ. अंबेडकर के माध्यम से देश में सामाजिक क्रांति आई थी। उसे अपनी एक पहचान चाहिए थी। इन दोनों स्थितियों में भारत में संविधान की जरूरत थी। भारतीय लोगों को संविधान की जरूरत थी। संविधान की जरूरत इसलिए थी क्योंकि उनको एक रा­ट्र बनाना था। संविधान के निर्माण के लिए कई समितियां बनी थी। इसमें से बाबासाहेब ड्राफ्टिंग कमेटी के चेयरमैन और एडवाइजरी कमेटी, फंडामेंटल राइट सब कमेटी, माइनरोरिटी कमेटी और यूनियन कांस्टीटय़ूशन कमेटी के सदस्य थे। संयुव्त रा­ट्र का जो सपना है कि दुनिया में समता हो, बंधुत्व हो, एकता हो, महिलाओं और दलितों की समस्या खत्म हो जाए तो इसमें वह तब तक सफल नही हो सकते, जब तक कि भारत की समस्या खत्म नहीं हो जाती।

यदि दुनिया को समता, बंधुत्व, गरीबी, भूख, अशिक्षा से मुव्त करना है, दुनिया को अगर मानवतावादी जगह बनानी है तो भारत में भारत के संविधान को सही तरीके से लागू करना होगा। दुनिया में लोगों ने जो सपना देखा है, वह तब तक पूरा नहीं हो सकता, जब तक भारत का संविधान कामयाब नहीं होता। भारत के संविधान की कामयाबी ही दुनिया को कामयाबी के रास्ते पर ले जाने में सक्षम है।

SHRIMATI PRATIMA MONDAL (JAYANAGAR): India gained the status of free and sovereign on August 15, 1947 after a long struggle and countless sacrifices. It adopted the Constitution on November 26, 1949 which came into force on January 26, 1950. It is often considered as one of the gigantic constitutions in the world which establishes a democratic state having 370 articles, 10 schedules in over 300 pages. Under this Constitution citizenship is single notional. No State citizenship is allowed unlike the case in the United States.

As the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, Ambedkar argued that the Constitution needed to be “both unitary as well as federal according to the requirements of time and circumstances. In his speech to the Constituent Assembly while presenting the draft constitution in 1949 where he explicitly notes that the constitution was designed to maintain the unity of India, in short, to hold it together.

The text prepared by Dr. Ambedkar offered a vide range of constitutional safeguards and guarantees to all citizens for instance, socio-economic rights, civil liberties, freedom of religion, the abolition of untouchability and prohibition of all forms of discrimination among others.

Dr. Ambedkar was the man who borne the responsibility to fight against the untouchability and exploitation based on Hindu Caste System and struggled for the untouchables rights carved for them a place in the Republican constitution of India. Though he managed to include certain provisions in the constitution of India for empowering lower castes but the fact was very much known to him that establishing equal human and civil rights for depressed classes was not sufficient in ensuring justice and welfare to them unless it would be accompanied by the legal provisions and safeguards to uphold those rights in the case of its violation and denial. Law, therefore, should provide remedies against the invasion of Indian 

fundamental rights. He said in the Constituent Assembly that all of us are aware that rights are nothing unless remedies are provided whereby people can seek to obtain redress when rights were invaded. Article 32 provides the right to all citizens of the country to approach the Supreme Court, if their fundamental rights and constitutional privileges are violated by any State institution or individual. This is perhaps why Dr. Ambedkar considered this provision as the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it. It is important to note, the Supreme Court later has declared Article 32 is a part of basic structure of the Constitution.

He also suggested safeguards for the minorities are vital. In democracy, minorities must feel safe. He noted that the suppression and exploitation of minorities in any form is the negation of democracy to humanism. If suppression is not stopped, then democracy degenerates into tyranny. Therefore, he gave so much importance to education. He believes that education is essential to moralize and socialize the individuals, especially the backward classes to have a cognizance of self. Article 46 further, as argued earlier, emphasis his vision which directs the State to take steps to promote education of the weaker sections of the society.

The credit goes to Dr. Ambedkar for the illiteracy programmes and free education up to matriculation guaranteed by the Indian Constitution. He raised the voice of those who had been long remained unheard and had an intense commitment for the social cause and upliftment of deprived and downtrodden sections of society. Indian Constitution does incorporate the social and political philosophy of Dr. Ambedkar which is most noticeably evident in the various provisions of the Constitution. The Preamble, Part III, IV and XVI among others are determined to establish a just society by upholding the concepts of liberty, equality, fraternity and safeguarding the unity of the country. There all three principles got significant place in the preamble of Constitution.

Most importantly Article 17 is unique in the sense that it has given a blow to the century old practice of untouchability. It reflects the spirit of the constitution’s determination to restore the dignity of the individual and assure fraternity. Untouchability is not only prohibited but it is made punishable by law. Part IV also reflects the conceptualization of Dr. Ambedkar on democracy that is to say, a political democracy should be accompanied with the social and police democracy. He expressed the view that the untouchables can not develop if they don’t get reservation in the service in the legislature in proportion to their relation. He argued that the social, political and economic upliftment of the untouchables is not possible simply by making provision and passing motions.

In this regard, it is also pertinent to note William Darity’s Comparative estimation when he wrote, “it is Ambedkar’s intellectual and political contributions that lie at the heart of the development of the reservation policy that prevails in India to this day”. 

SHRI MALYADRI SRIRAM (BAPATLA): It is great honour for me to express my views on this auspicious occasion of Constitution Day and during the 125th Birth Anniversary Celebration of Dr. Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar. I am grateful to Hon'ble Speaker for giving me this honour. 

Dr. Babasaheb B.R. Ambedkar, the celebrated author of the Constitution of the modern India, is a celebrity in history, who cast a spell on tens of nations of people by his writings and preaching's. He is a political scientist, economist, legal luminary, social reformer, architect of India's Constitution and a leader of men.

Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is a multifaceted personality. With varied interests, he defies attempts at classification and categorization. But with his singular drive for the uplift of the poor and the weaker sections, he became an inspirational figure during his lifetime and a national icon in the decades thence. 

Not surprisingly, despite his later differences with the Congress, and his opposition to the politics of social hate and communal divides, Ambedkar is now sought to be appropriated by everybody for their political mobilization strategies. 

He not only preached but also worked hard for the upliftment of the "oppressed and suppressed" millions of the society, including women, who constitutes 50% of the society. He understood fully the problems faced by the women in the society and in order to uplift them from oppression, he tried to introduce the "BILL" giving equal right to them in the property of the family, which was called "SARADHA ACT", unfortunately never seen the light of the day. 

Recently the official forum in the AP brought a calendar on Ambedkar with a caption "we are here because he was" which conveys a lot of meaning. There he refers to everyone, not only people like me but also so many others who are present in this august House. It is through his great contribution by way of our constitution the society is safe and secure, compared to our neighbours, excepting a small hiccups here and there. 

It is since 60+ years we got freedom from a long and exploitative colonial rule. After 60+years nothing substantial has been done to dalits to liberate from their socio-economic servitude. It is common occurrence today that we notice increasing atrocities on Dalits. They are subjected to age long economic exploitation coupled with social discrimination and cultural oppression. What Dr. Ambedkar said about and did for Dalits is still relevant today. 

Buddhism, being very dear to the heart of Ambedkar, was the first progressive thought in Indian philosophy which had a break with Brahmanical system. What impressed Dr. Ambedkar in Buddhism was that it did not promise salvation to humanity as all other religions did. Buddha to Dr. Ambedkar was Marga Data (Path finder) and not Moksha Data (giver of salvation). Buddha did not claim divinity for himself or for his Dhamma. Buddhism was discovered by man for man. It is this quintessence of humanism that took Dr. Ambedkar closer to Buddhism. 

Dr. Ambedkar was drawn towards Buddhism because he considered it as a social philosophy but not as religion. As it was an exploitative, casteless and egalitarian philosophy, he found "salvation" of humanity, as a whole and the dalits in particular, in Buddhism. 

A voracious reader Dr. Ambedkar saw education as tool for the liberation of the socially backward from illiteracy, ignorance and superstition. He founded the People's Education Society in 1945 with the aim of advancing the educational interests of weaker sections of society. Dr. Ambedkar was also a crusader for gender equality and fought for equal rights for women in inheritance and marriage. He resigned from the Cabinet in 1951 when his draft Hindu Code Bill failed to receive the support of the Parliament. 

Undoubtedly, Dr. Ambedakr’s biggest and most important contribution was in his role as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India. With tremendous foresight and erudite scholarship, Dr. Ambedkar not only piloted an outstanding draft through the Constituent Assembly but also outlined the philosophy and wisdom behind the various provisions. 

Dr. Ambedkar ensured the inclusion of a well-defined and comprehensive chapter on Fundamental Rights which specifically abolished untouchability, guaranteed equal rights to all citizens and prohibited discrimination of all kinds in social relations. Dr. Ambedkar believed that protection of minorities and their religion was of paramount importance. Thus, the Constitution grants each person and freedom of faith, religion and worship and gives the minorities freedom to manage their religious affairs. Dr. Ambedkar justified such protection on the following grounds: 

"It is wrong for majority to deny the existence of minorities. It is equally wrong for the minorities to perpetuate themselves. A solution must be found which will serve a double purpose. It must recognize the existence of minorities to start with. It must also be such that it will enable majorities and minorities to merge someday into one. The solution proposed by the Constituent Assembly is to be welcomed because it is a solution which serves this twofold purpose." 

Dr. Ambedkar played a crucial role in laying down the Directive Principles of State Policy, a unique feature of the Indian Constitution. These principles mandate that the State shall strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a just order. These principles lay the foundation for social democracy. In Dr. Ambedkar's words "We must make our political democracy a social democracy as well. What does social democracy mean? It means a way of life which recognizes liberty, equality and fraternity as principles of life. These principles of liberty, equality and fraternity are not to be treated as separate items in a trinity. They form a union or trinity in the sense that to divorce one from the other is to defeat the very purpose of democracy. .................. Without equality, liberty would produce the supremacy of the few over the many. Equality without liberty would kill individual initiative. Without fraternity, liberty and equality would not become a natural course of thing. It would require a constable to enforce them. .............On the social plane, we have in India a society based on the principles of graded inequality which means elevation for some and degradation for others. On the economic plane, we have a society in which there are some who have immense wealth as against many who live in abject poverty............... How long shall we continue to live this life of contradiction? We must remove this contradiction at earliest possible moment or else those who suffer from inequality will blow up the structure of political democracy. ........"

I think we have already deviated from the Directive Principle of State Policy by subsidizing LPG and here also lies different problems which we are facing and this also needs correction. 

The Directive Principles of State Policy were criticized by some and termed mere "pious declarations". Responding to this criticism, Dr. Ambedkar said: "Whoever captures power will not be free to do what he likes with it. In the exercise of it, he will have to respect these instruments of instructions which are called Directive Principles. He cannot ignore them. He may not have to answer for their breach in a Court of Law. But he will certainly have to answer for them before the electorate at election time."

Dr. Ambedkar was firm in his belief that our judiciary must both be independent of the executive and must also be competent in itself. He did recognise however that tussles between the executive and the judiciary were inevitable, and were in fact necessary to ensure that each acted as a check and balance on the functioning of the other. He observed: "For myself, I cannot altogether omit the possibility of a Legislature packed by party men making laws which may abrogate or violate what we regard as certain fundamental principles affecting the life and liberty of an individual. At the same time, I do not see how five or six gentlemen sitting in the Federal or Supreme Court examining laws made by the Legislature and by dint of their own individual conscience or their bias or their prejudices be trusted to determine which law is good and which law is bad."

Dr. Ambedkar called upon the socially and economically disadvantaged to 'educate, agitate and organise'. Nevertheless, his commitment to constitutional methods was unwavering and he advocated a path of informed and reasoned public engagement. He said: "We must abandon the bloody methods of revolution. ............ When there was no way left for constitutional methods for achieving economic and social objectives, there was a great deal of justification for unconstitutional methods. But where constitutional methods are open, there can be no justification for these unconstitutional methods. These methods are nothing but the grammar of anarchy and sooner they are abandoned, the better for us. "

Dr. Ambedkar believed that strong independent institutions constituted the fundamental pillars of a democracy and it is they who would ensure its survival. He ensured that the Constitution provided for an independent judiciary and that the right to Constitutional Remedies was a fundamental right.

Speaking about Article 32 -Right to Constitutional Remedies, Dr. Ambedkar said: "If I was asked to name any particular article in this Constitution as the most important - an article without which the Constitution would be a nullity - I could not refer to any other article except this one. It is the very soul of the Constitution and the heart of it."

It must be noted in the above regard that in practice our political system has been innovative and flexible. Dr. Ambedkar's commitment to the building of strong institutions and constitutional methods has resulted in many interesting modern day manifestation. For example, the Right to Information Act is a unique and powerful instrument created by law to empower people and enable them access information from any department of Government on any subject advancing thereby openness and transparency. Similarly, the Supreme Court of India through Public Interest Litigation has enabled the common man access the highest courts of justice by just sending a post card. High Courts and Supreme Court have also taken suo motu cognizance of violation of fundamental rights and initiated action on their own setting aside the conventional notions of locus standi. All the above reflect the strength of Indian democracy and dynamism of the Constitution. 

In this connection, I would like to highlight certain issues pertaining to the under privileged sections of the society. For example, even today reserved post are not filled in full in the SC/ST category. Only 8 to 9% are filled in category 'A' post, 10-12 in category 'B' post and category 'C' is 15-16, where as category D is to the tune of 23-24%, same is the case in ST also. I request the government to see that all the post meant for the reserved sections are to be filled. I also urge upon this government to provide reservations in promotions. Not only that these groups are brought into the main stream by considering them for good posting in the case of officials and also portfolios for some political leaders, other than Tribal welfare, Social Justice, etc. 

SHRI DHANANJAY MAHADIK (KOLHAPUR): Dr. Ambedkar's role in the Constituent Assembly was to write about the history of the evolution of free India's Constitution. 

In a remarkable speech, on the problems of the Scheduled Castes, delivered in the Conference held by the All India Scheduled Castes Federation at Kanpur (UP) on 29th January 1944, Dr. Ambedkar suggested the Scheduled Caste people that they should share political power with the Hindus and Muslims to improve their condition. Only then they will become masters. 

At another occasion held at Lucknow on 25th April, 1948, he, while addressing the Scheduled Castes, aptly warned them that they can achieve their salvation if they capture the political power by organising into a third party holding the balance of power between the rival political parties - Congress and Socialists. 

The similar feeling he expressed at his election to the Drafting Committee in 1946. He said: "I came into the Constituent Assembly with no greater aspiration than to safeguard the interest of the Scheduled Castes." 

This statement clearly explains the idea behind his interest for Scheduled Castes. But when he was elected the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, he left all his initial interests and contributed himself whole heartedly for giving a constitution to the newly born nation. He gave up all his personal wishes only for the general interest of the nation. 

The true Constitutional philosophy of Ambedkar has been fully reflected in the course of Round Table Conference in England and in Memorandum which he submitted to the Constitutuent Assembly on behalf of All India Scheduled Caste Federation. 

Appreciating the great services rendered by Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, T.T. Krishnamachari, one of the Members of the Constituent Assembly, said in the Assembly, "... the House is, perhaps, aware that of the seven members nominated by you, one had resigned from the House, and was not replaced. One dies and was not replaced. One was away in America and his place was not filled up and another person was engaged in State Affairs and there was void to that extent. One or two people were far away from Delhi and, perhaps, for reasons of health did not attend. So, it happened ultimately that the burden of drafting the constitution fell on Ambedkar and I have no doubt and we are grateful to him for having achieved this task in a manner which is undoubtedly commendable."

It is universally accepted that Ambedkar has made an immense contribution to the philosophy of our Constitution and to the constitutional jurisprudence. But this has led to the belief that Ambedkar was the sole guiding force of the Constitution. He was the chief architect of the Constitution to define the will, goal and vision of India. He is regarded as the father of the Constitution and the Constitution is his brainchild. Therefore, whatever principles have been incorporated in the Constitution, Ambedkar is regarded as a source of it. Prime Minister Nehru, while paying a tribute to Dr. Ambedkar in the Lok Sabha said that Dr. Ambedkar had played a most important part in the framing of India's Constitution. He told two facts, firstly he said that Dr. Ambedkar has played a very constructive role in making of the Constitution even before his election to the Drafting Committee and secondly he hold that no one took greater trouble and care over the Constitution making than Dr. Ambedkar. 

He was chosen among other equally available members of the Constituent Assembly simply because of the treasure, the treasure of his intelligence, the treasure of his keen knowledge of his subject, his treasure, of his interest in constitutionalism and the treasure of his professionalism of being an advocate. 

The work done by Dr. Ambedkar in various sub-committees of the Assembly was considered very useful and convinced the Congress bosses beyond doubt that the legislation and solidification of freedom would not be easy without the services of Dr. Ambedkar. 

It is rightly said that the Indian Constitution was the product of Dr. Ambedkar. It was fully influenced by the philosophy of Dr. Ambedkar. He had a vision for future India. When he was elected the Chairman of the Drafting Committee he forgot his personal anxiety and joined hands with the Congress in general and Pandit Nehru in particular as both were ready to sink their differences and agreed to work together for the betterment of the newly born nation. But this does not mean that he had the greed for the position he was offered by the Congress. He was very firm and bold in his demands and whenever he got chances he criticized the Government also. 

There is also a need to examine his role for the upliftment of minorities in connection with the members of the Constituent Assembly. Why, because he had to take into consideration their provisions and their reservations on certain issues, as he observed many a times in the Assembly and the attitude of other members for him. There are reasons for that, firstly he was non-congress man and secondly he was not a staunch follower of Gandhi. There were other members who were jurists, scholars, statesmen, social activists and political leaders in the Assembly but he was given this stupendous task of piloting the Draft Constitution. 

Ambedkar, the true rebel and rationalist, played a major role in creation of new India. He has shown to the Indians that the goal under the fabric of Constitution is nothing but to establish social economical and political democracy for the betterment of all Indians.
