SHRI KALYAN BANERJEE (SREERAMPUR): Sir, I consider myself today to be one of the privileged persons. I thank you and my leader, Kumari Mamta Banerjee, for giving me this opportunity to speak on this subject. 

Sir, if it is considered in the world that Lord Denning was the best judge, in our country Dr. Ambedkar was and is still the best jurist. Dr. Ambedkar was an illustrious leader and was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution. A good and virtuous constitution having moral foundation, protects not only fundamental freedom and rights but also creates a bridge between conflicting interests and becomes a harbinger to the social needs. It produces good legislatures and good citizens. The constitutional courts are sentinel on the qui vive therefore, it functions objectively and dispassionately to correct imbalances and keep check on every wing of the State without trespassing upon the field assigned or powers conferred on the other wing. At the same time, it maintains a delicate balance. 

A Constitution is a documentation of the founding faiths of a nation and the fundamental directions for their fulfillment. The written Constitution of a country is a document which defines the regular form or system of the Government containing the rules that directly or indirectly affect the distribution exercise of the sovereign power of the State. It is thus mainly concerns with the creation of three organs, i.e., the Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary as also the distribution of governmental powers among them and the definition of their mutual relation. We have to work in letter and spirit of the Constitution itself. 

The founding father of the Constitution cognizant of the reality of life wisely engrafted the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles in Parts III and IV for a democratic life for everyone in Bharat Republic. This significance of the perception that Parts III and IV together constitute the core of commitment to social revolution of the society and they together are the concerns of the Constitution and is a deep understanding of the Indian Constitution itself.

Sir, India is a secular country. Secularism has been inserted in the Preamble by reason of the 42nd Constitution amendment of 1976. The object of insertion of this word was to spell out expressly the high ideals of the secularism and the integrity of the nation. Secularism does not mean the constitution of the theocratic society. It merely means equal status of all religions without any preference in favour of or of discrimination of any of them. It is clear from the constitutional scheme that it guarantees equality in the matter of religion to all individuals and groups irrespective of their faiths. Emphasis in that is there is no religion of the State. Preamble of the Constitution read particularly with article 25 to 28 indicates that the concept of secularism is embodied in the Constitution scheme itself. Article 29 of the Constitution speaks of protection of interest of minorities. Article 30 speaks of right of minorities to establish and administer an educational institution. 

The concept of secularism is one facet of the right to equality woven as central golden thread in the fabric depicting the pattern of the scheme of our Constitution. Secularism has been given a pride of place in the Constitution itself. Dr. Ambedkar said, “I like the religion that teaches liberty, equality and fraternity”. Dr. Ambedkar said, “Religion is for men and not men for religion”. Dr. Ambedkar said, “The basic idea underlying the religion is to create an atmosphere for the spiritual development of the individual”. Our Constitution has secured independence to the Judiciary and zealously guarded the independence of the Judiciary. Independence of Judiciary is doubtless a basic structure of our Constitution. But the said concept of independence has to be confined within the four corners of the Constitution and cannot go beyond the Constitution. Our Constitution is liberal, democratic, egalitarian, secular and federal in character. Dr. Ambedkar said, “Our object in framing the Constitution is to two-fold – to lay down the form of political democracy and to lay down the idea of economic democracy and also to prescribe that every government whoever is in power shall strive to bring about economic democracy”. Since our Constitution is federal in character, likewise Central Government every State Government is elected by the people. Relations between the Union and the States have been engrafted under part XI of the Constitution. Powers of enactment of laws made by the Parliament and the Legislatures of the States have been provided under article 246 of the Constitution. Our Constitution does not permit the Central Government to interfere with the State subjects and thereby any attempt to destroy the federal character of the Constitution. 

Recently the Government of India has issued a directive that all Central Schemes will be monitored by a Deputy Secretary level officer of the Government of India. These officers have a part in overseeing the Central schemes. They will travel to different States to monitor the progress of the schemes on the ground. This move of the Government of India tantamount to mistrust of the official machinery of the State Government. As is the present practice, all schemes under the State Plan under the Centrally-sponsored schemes are implemented and monitored by the State machinery. The Government of India releases the funds to the State Governments on the basis of physical and financial progress of the scheme and after due submission of the Utilisation Certificate by the State Government. This system has been in vogue since the introduction of the Central schemes and is functioning well. The new system will severely impact the autonomy of the State Government and is against the spirit of cooperative federalism. 

14.00 hours

Sir, Dr. Ambedkar fought for the protection and reservation of SCs and STs. Now, an attempt is being made to take away such a protection and reservation. It is surprising that the hon. Prime Minister and other Ministers are holding video conferences with the Chief Secretary under the guise of development and to know the development programmes. This amounts to direct interference with the State administration. If the hon. Prime Minister and any of the Ministers wishes to know the development of a State itself, he is free to talk with the concerned Chief Minister. 

I am saying this today with great respect to the hon. Prime Minister. Please do not take me amiss. Like the hon. Prime Minister, all the Chief Ministers of the country are also good administrators. They are also honest persons. They are also political persons. They have fought for 30 to 40 years in the field. They have not been sent to the State as a Chief Minister from Delhi office for running their State itself. I am saying this with great respect to the hon. Prime Minister. Do not undermine any Chief Minister. Do not undermine any State Government. 

Law and order is a State subject. The Government of India has taken up the Plan schemes aimed at creating a comprehensive and integrated system for enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of policing, and creation of an IT-enabled State-of-the art tracking system around “investigation of crime and detection of criminals”. The ostensible objective of the programme is to improve Police functioning in various areas such as law and order, traffic management, etc. And what is being done? Under the guise of this, every case has to be reported to them and from Delhi, the Home Ministry will be monitoring all the law and order cases which are registered under the State Government and which is the subject matter of the State. Does it not betray the cooperative federal system of the country? What are you trying to achieve which you cannot achieve under the provisions of our Constitution? 

The Central Government is trying to achieve it in an indirect method for the purpose of keeping record and indirectly monitoring the cases. This is not permissible under the Constitution itself. 

The IAS officers and IPS officers of the State cadres are sent here for training for two years. After two years of training, these officers are required to be sent to the States. My question today is, why, after this training, are you keeping these officers in the various Ministries in Delhi? For what purposes are you keeping them? The Union Government is consisting of various Ministries. Under what law, under what provisions is this being done? Are you trying to brainwash the IAS and IPS officers before sending them to the States? Under what constitutional provisions are these things done by the hon. Prime Minister and other Ministers? 

During this current financial year, the Centre has unilaterally structured a large number of Centrally sponsored schemes without consulting the State Governments. The State Governments ratio has been decreased. 

I fully support my friend from AIADMK who just now spoke. In matters of Concurrent List, if a law has to be legislated, why are you not consulting the State Governments? It cannot be an idea and concept of only the Central Government. No doubt, the Concurrent List is for the Central Government and the State Governments. No doubt that the Central Government is having its powers. Do not try to be the big brother or the elder brother of the country itself. All are not small people. It is said under our Constitution itself that the State Governments are not juniors to the Central Government at all. Like the Central Government, the State Governments have their own independence. They are not under anybody’s control. But schemes are there; relationship is there, which I referred to as stated in part 11 of the Constitution itself. 

The Central proceeds on account of collection of cess and surcharge do not form part of the divisible pool of Central taxes shared with the States. The share of cess and surcharge in gross tax revenue of Central Government has increased substantially over a period of time from 3.51 per cent in 2001-02 to above nine per cent in 2015-16. The States have been demanding that the proceeds on account of cess and surcharge should be shared with them. The Government of India has not acceded to this demand. Instead, despite sluggish economy and other challenges being faced by the country and the States to spur the economic growth, the Centre has imposed 0.5 per cent cess on service tax for its Swachh Bharat programme. The States were not taken into confidence while imposing this burden on the common man and the economy. This is against the spirit of cooperative federalism.

The non-tax receipts of the Central Government have steadily grown by 11 per cent over the last decade. A substantial amount of non-tax receipt is accruing from auctioning of licence fees and disinvestment in the Central PSUs. While the States have equal claim on the proceeds accruing from auctioning of licence fee for exploitation of natural resources, it also has a major role in the development of the Central PSUs which are located in the States. As such the Centre should share part of its proceeds with the State Governments. 

Inter State Council is a constitutional entity created under article 263 of the Constitution. Although constitutionally mandated, several of these Councils are virtually inactive. A large number of regional issues which could have been easily discussed and resolved in these Councils either lie unattended or allowed to assume serious proportions of prompt Central interventions. Both these situations are undesirable in a federal set-up like ours. Therefore, Inter State Council should be strengthened and made effective. 

The Central Government passes Central legislation and many legislation overlap with the State legislation. The burden of implementing the Central legislation, like the Right to Education Act, 2010 and National Food Security Act, which are often passed without any effective consultation with the State Governments, falls on the State Governments. These legislation put enormous financial burden on the State Governments and forces the State Governments to redefine its development priorities in order to provide necessary financial allocation for the statutory liabilities arising out of the Acts. 

The Constitution itself envisages Planning Commission. It was really a concept of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. Now, Planning Commission has been substituted with Niti Aayog. But no plan size has yet been informed to anyone. In Niti Aayog not a single discussion has been held by the hon. Prime Minister excepting the Land Bill. What is being done by Niti Aayog? Planning Commission has gone. Six months are already over. There is no work done by the Niti Aayog. 

In recent days a new trend has come to our notice. As you know, Governors cannot act without the advice and consultation with the Cabinet. Very recently, few Governors have been appointed. What are they doing? These Governors, without consulting the State Government, the Chief Minister and the Cabinet, are asking for security to the political party leaders. I do not want to name that political party. This Governor some times, when such political party leaders are coming, without asking the Chief Minister and without consulting the Cabinet, asks for CRPF protection for holding local municipality election. Is it not a breach on the part of the Governor? Is it not a contravention of a constitutional mandate? … (Interruptions) I will just take three minutes. 

I would like to refer to page 975 of Volume 10 of Constituent Assembly debate.

“However good a Constitution may be, it is sure to turn out bad because those who are called to work it, happen to be a bad lot. However bad a Constitution may be, it may turn out to be good if those who are called to work it, happen to be a good lot. The working of a Constitution does not depend wholly upon the nature of the Constitution. The Constitution can provide only the organs of State such as the Legislature, the Executive and the Judiciary. The factors on which the working of those organs of the State depend are the people and the political parties they will set up as their instruments to carry out their wishes and their politics. It is, therefore, futile to pass any judgement upon the Constitution without reference to the part which the people and their parties are likely to play.”

Sir, Mother Teresa said:

“God has not called me to be successful, but God has called me to be faithful.”

Therefore, Sir, the three organs of the State should be first faithful to the Constitution and discharge their constitutional duties. This is not the time to see how successful we are during these 65 years, this is the time to give answers as to how much faithful we are to the Constitution itself. For the last two days, this debate is going on in this House and many leaders have said many things. But I would like to say this. If we are really faithful to the Constitution, all the organs of this country, the Legislature, the Judiciary, the Executive and all the people of this country itself, if they are faithful to the Constitution, then we will really pay respect to Dr. Ambedkar and other great leaders who were instrumental to make our country as the largest democratic country in the world.

Sir, with these words, on behalf of my party and on behalf of my leader Mamata Banerjee, I pay respect to Dr. Ambedkar and other great leaders who gave us the Constitution and I conclude with a prayer today in this House that today and also in future, let us take a promise that we would be faithful to the Constitution itself. Thank you.

*श्री सदाशिव लोखंडे (शिर्डी) ः परम आदरणीय डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर जी की 125वीं व­ाऩगांठ संविधान दिवस के शुभ अवसर पर सदन में चर्चा चल रही है। बाबासाहेब ने 26 नवंबर, 1949 में देश को एक संपूर्ण प्रभुत्वसंपन्न, समाजवादी, पंथनिरपेक्ष, लोकतंत्रात्मक गणराज्य बनाने के लिए तथा देश के सभी नागरिकों को सामाजिक, आर्थिक और राजनैतिक न्याय, विचार अभिव्यव्ति, विश्वास, धर्म और उपासना की स्वतंत्रता, प्रति­ठा और अवसर की समता प्राप्त कराने के लिए तथा उन सब में व्यव्ति की गरिमा और रा­ट्र की एकता और अखंडता सुनिश्चित करने वाली बंधुता बढ़ाने के लिए दृढ़ संकल्प होकर संविधान सभा में संविधान को अंगीकृत, अधिनियमित और आत्मार्पित किया था।

डाँ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर साहब दलित, आदिवासी और कमजोर तबके के मसीहा थे। वे जीवनपर्यन्त देश के निचले तबके के लोगों की सेवा में लगे रहे। उन्होंने दलितुं के उत्थान हेतु भारतीय संविधान का निर्माण किया।

वे दलित, आदिवासी और कमजोर तबके के लोगों की पीड़ा को समझते थे। उन्हीं के सतत प्रयास से आज देश की विधानसभाओं, संसद, ग्राम पंचायतों एवं सरकारी नौकरियों में दलितों को आरक्षण मिल रहा है।

डॉ. बाबासाहेब का नारा था- शिक्षित बनो, संगठित रहो और संघ­ाऩ करो। यह इस देश का दुर्भाग्य है कि आज़ादी के 67 व­ााॉ के बाद भी दलितों का उत्थान नहीं हो रहा है।

आज भी महारा­ट्र चैम्बर ऑफ कॉमर्स, जिसका गठन 10 व­ाऩ पूर्व हुआ था तथा जो दलित उद्योगपतियों से संबंधित है, पांच करोड़ की अल्प राशि निधि के तौर पर जमा नहीं कर सकी है। यह देश के दलित उद्योगपतियों की स्थिति है।

देश के सभी निजी स्कूलों, कॉलेजों, मेडिकल संस्थान इत्यादि में शो­िात वर्ग के छात्रों के लिए 25 प्रतिशत आरक्षण की व्यवस्था होनी चाहिए। दलित, शो­िात वर्ग पर होने वाले अत्याचारों पर रोक लगनी चाहिए।

बाबासाहेब ने कठिन परिस्थितियों में विदेश में शिक्षा प्राप्त की थी। वे चाहते तो अच्छे पद पर रहकर अपना जीवन व्यतीत करते। मगर उन्होंने ऐसा नहीं किया। वे बड़े पदों से सदैव दूर रहे और दलित, आदिवासी एवं कमज़ोर वर्ग के लोगों के लिए संघ­ाऩशील रहते हुए उनके कल्याण हेतु अनेक योजनाएं तैयार करवायीं।

*श्री श्रीरंग आप्पा बारणे (मावल) ः भारत का संविधान विश्व के किसी भी गणतांत्रिक देश का सबसे लम्बा लिखित संविधान है। इसमें अब तक 465 अनुच्छेद तथा 12 अनुसूचियां हैं और यह 22 भागों में विभाजित है। भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना के अनुसार भारत एक संप्रभुतासंपन्न, समाजवादी और धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य है।

हमारे संविधान को बनाने में 2 व­ाऩ, 11 माह और 18 दिन का समय लगा तथा डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर जी को संविधान की प्रारूप समिति के अध्यक्ष के रूप में नियुव्त किया गया और डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद जी को संविधान सभा केअध्यक्ष के रूप में चुना गया। बहुजन हिताय जैसा शब्द और साहित्य की देन डॉ. अम्बेडकर जी द्वारा ही दी गयी है। 26 नवंबर, 1949 को संविधान सभा ने संविधान को अपना लिया और अपने काम को पूरा करने के बाद बोलते हुए अंबेडकर जी ने कहा- "" मैं महसूस करता हॅं कि संविधान साध्य (काम करने लायक) है यह लचीला है और साथ ही साथ इतना मजबूत भी है कि देश को शांति और युद्ध दोनों समय में जोड़कर रख सके। वास्तव में मैं कह सकता हॅं कि अगर कुछ भी गलत हुआ तो इसका कारण यह नहीं होगा कि हमारा संविधान खराब था बल्कि इसका उपयोग करने वाला मनु­य अधम था।""

इसी परिपेक्ष्य में आज देश के हालात को दर्शाया जा रहा है, देश में सब जगह शांति और भाईचारे का माहौल है, लेकिन कुछ लोग देशभर में असहि­णुता का राग अलाप रहे हैं, कुछ लोगों तथा बुद्धिजीवियों द्वारा रोज राग अलापा जा रहा है कि देश में शालीनता की कमी है। मैं पॅंछना चाहता हॅं कि जिन कश्मीरी पंडितों को उनके घरों से निकाल कर हत्या कर दी गई, जब उनको बेघर कर दिया गया, जब देश में अलग-अलग जगहों पर पिछले समय में अनेकों सांप्रदायिक दंगे हुए, जब देश में विभिन्न जगहों पर आतंकवादी घटनाएंì हुई, जिसमें हज़ारों लोगों की जानें चली गयी तब क्या असहि­णुता नहीं थी। अतः अंत में मैं कहना चाहॅंगा कि कृपया देश की जनता को गुमराह करने की कोशिश न की जाए।

हमारे संविधान की विशे­ाता है कि इसमें सभी धर्मों, जातियों और संप्रदायों को एक समान रखा गया है। किसी भी धर्म, जाति या संप्रदाय के साथ कोई भेदभाव नहीं किया गय है। हमारा संविधान विश्व के लिए प्रेरणादायक संविधान है और हमारा संविधान विश्व के सभी देशों को भाईचारे का संदेश भी देता है।

मैं डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर, डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद, सरदार बल्लभ भाई पटेल, डॉ. श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी, डॉ. गोविंद बल्लभ पंत, एस.एच. गप्पी, डॉ. नीलम संजीव रेड्डी, शेख गालिब साहिब तथा अन्य संविधान निर्माता और संविधान सभा के समस्त सदस्यों को नमन करता हॅं। भारत एक लोकतांत्रिक देश है और हमेशा रहेगा।

*श्री राकेश सिंह (जबलपुर) ः 26 नवंबर हम और हमारे देश के लोकतंत्र के लिए एक पर्व का दिन है। इसी दिन 1949 को हमने स्वतंत्र भारत के संविधान को अंगीकृत, अधिनियित और आत्मार्पित करने का संकल्प लिया था और तबसे ही हम इस दिन को प्रतिव­ाऩ संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाते हैं। हम जब भी भारत के संविधान की बात करते हैं तो हमेशा एक ऐसा नाम मानस पटल पर उभर आता है, जिसके बिना इस देश के संविधान की मूल आत्मा की कल्पना ही नहीं की जा सकती। वह नाम है बाबासाहेब भीमराव अंबेडकर जी का। जिन्होंने बहुत ही वि­ाम परिस्थितियें में कठोर संघ­ाऩ करते हुए जीवन जिया। लेकिन शे­ा सारा जीवन इस देश की अखण्डता और एकता के लिए समर्पित किया।

बहुत से वव्ताओं ने श्रद्धेय बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर जी तथा भारत के संविधान के प्रति वचनबद्धता, इस वि­ाय पर विस्तार से काफी कुछ कहा है। मैं तो केवल संविधान सभा में दिए गए बाबासाहेब के अंतिम भा­ाण और उसके उद्देश्य की ओर सदन का ध्यान आकृ­ट करना चाहता हॅं। बाबासाहेब ने कहा था कि देश का संविधान कितना भी अच्छा क्यों न हो, लेकिन उसे लागू करने वाले यदि अच्छे नहीं है तो संविधान की भावना ठीक से स्थापित नहीं होगी और यदि संविधान कितना भी खराब क्यों न हो, लेकिन यदि उसे लागू करने वाले लोग अच्छे हों तो संविधान की भावना अच्छे रूप में ही स्थापित होगी। इसलिए संविधान केवल उसके स्वरूप पर ही निर्भर नहीं होता बल्कि इसे लागू करने वालों की सोच महत्वपूर्ण होती है। यदि इसे लागू करने वालों की सोच इससे अपने लिए किसी लाभ या स्वार्थ की कामना की है तो उससे जनकल्याण नहीं हो सकता, लोकतंत्र की गरिमा और मर्यादा की रक्षा नहीं हो सकती।

भारत जैसे देश में संवैधानिक अधिकार रखने वालों के भीतर यह दृढ़ संकल्प होना चाहिए कि हम लोकतंत्र के माध्यम से ही देश की समस्याओं का समाधान करेंगे ताकि देश को दुबारा कभी आपातकाल जैसे काले अध्याय का सामना न करना पड़े।

अंबेडकर जी का यह भी मानना था कि केवल राजनैतिक लोकतंत्र से ही समाधान ढूंढना उपयुव्त नहीं है बल्कि राजनैतिक लोकतंत्र को सामाजिक लोकतंत्र के साथ जोड़ना होगा। क्योंकि यदि राजनैतिक लोकतंत्र के मूल में सामाजिक लोकतंत्र का आधार नहीं होगा तो देश का लोकतंत्र टिकेगा नहीं और न ही परिपक्व होगा।

अंबेडकर जी मानते थे कि सामाजिक लोकतंत्र वह मार्ग है जो समाज में स्वातंत्र्य, समता और बंधुता, इन जीवन तत्वों को मान्यता देता है। इन तीनों को हम अलग-अलग नहीं देख सकते। बाबा साहेब यह भी मानते थे कि इनको एक दूसरे से अलग करना हमारे लोकतंत्र के मूल उद्देश्य का ही पराभाव है। इसलिए सभी को यह समझना होग कि स्वातंत्र्य, समता और बंधुता से ही सामाजिक समरसता का निर्माण होता है और यही लोकतंत्र की सबसे बड़ी आवश्यकता है और इस सामाजिक समरसता का निर्माण हम सभी के भीतर ही होना चाहिए। आज अधिक आवश्यकता इस बात की है कि राजनैतिक रूप से ही यह प्रयास निरंतर होना चाहिए कि हम समरसता को सामने रखकर ही सामाजिक जीवन की कल्पना करें। यह स्प­ट है कि बाबासाहेब की यही कल्पना थी कि भवि­य में देश संभालने वाले संविधान की इस मूल भावना को सामने रखकर सामाजिक समरसता के निर्माण में आने वाली कमियों को दूर करके चलेंगे। हमें गर्व है कि इसी रास्ते पर आगे बढ़कर श्रद्धेय अटल बिहारी वाजपेयी जी की सरकार ने पंडित दीनदयाल उपाध्याय के दर्शन जिसमें समाज की अंतिम पीढ़ी में बैठे हुए व्यव्ति को हाथ पकड़कर बराबरी के भाव के समाज की मुख्य धारा में लाने के कार्य की बुनियाद रखी थी और देश ने विकास के मार्ग पर एक लंबी छलांग लगाई थी। हमें इस बात पर भी गर्व है कि माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में यह सरकार सामाजिक समरसता की बुनियाद पर ही ""सबका साथ-सबका विकस"" के मूल मंत्र पर कार्य कर रही है।

आज आवश्यकता इसी बात की है कि हमारे देश में विभिन्न प्रकार की मत भिन्नता होने के बाद भी हम सब मिलकर अंबेडकर जी के उस स्वपन को साकार करने की दिशा में आगे बढ़े कि देश मजबूत किए बिना देशवासियों का आर्थिक और सामाजिक उत्थान नहीं हो सकता और इसलिए उन सभी विचारों और ताकतों को कमज़ोर करे जिससे देश कमजोर हो सकता है और तमाम राजनैतिक मतभेदों के बावजूद भी उन विचारों और नीतियों को मजबूत करें, जिनसे देश मजबूत हो सकता है।

मैं देश के संविधान के प्रति अपनी नि­ठा और श्रद्धा व्यव्त करते हुए देश के संविधान निर्माताओं और विशे­ा रूप से डॉ. बाबासाहेब भीमराव अंबेडकर जी के प्रति कृतज्ञता व्यव्त करता हॅं जिन्होंने हमारे संविधान के माध्यम से हमें एक ऐसे संप्रभु व स्वतंत्र रा­ट्र में सांस लेने का अवसर दिया है, जो संपूर्ण विश्व में हमें विलक्षणता प्रदान करता है।

DR. KIRIT SOMAIYA (MUMBAI NORTH EAST): I thank Hon'ble Speaker and Hon'ble Prime Minister to have these special sittings to commemorate 125th Birthday Anniversary celebration of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and to remember and pay homage to the Father of the Indian Constitution. 

I thank hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi and Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Shri Devendra Fadnavis who in this 125th Birth Anniversary Celebration year had bought the House in London where Dr. B.R. Ambedkar use to reside. Government of Maharashtra bought this House few months back and the converted this House into Ambedkar Samarak. Hon'ble Prime Minister, this month, inaugurated the Ambedkar Samarak and Research Centre in London.

I neither participated in the freedom struggle nor witnessed the debates of Constituent Assembly, as I was not born. This is a great opportunity I got here to respect and pay homage to our Constitutional Fathers. 

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): Mr. Deputy Speaker, Sir, I thank you very much for giving me this opportunity. I stand here today to participate in the discussion that we are having on ‘Commitment to India’s Constitution as part of 125th Birth Anniversary Celebration of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’ which was initiated by the Home Minister Shri Rajnath Singh. Subsequently, a number of leaders of respective political parties have given their suggestions and opinions relating to the functioning of our Constitution and relating to the merits of our Constitution, the uniqueness of our Constitution.

Sir, Babasaheb Ambedkar was an illustrious leader, a nationalist, a jurist, a philosopher, a thinker, a historian, a great orator, a prolific writer, an economist, a scholar and a social reformer. At times, I wonder how could a single person, who comes from a humble background, achieve such heights of eminence during a very short span of time. Yesterday, I think, Sudipda was saying that Dr. Ambedkar was not only a Post Graduate in Arts, he was also a D.Sc. in Science, he was also a Barrister, he was also a jurist and he went to England and USA to study. He had achieved these things during a very short period of time. That shows the intellect and what he has repeatedly written and said in his speeches. He said that given an opportunity, a person can excel. It is the lack of opportunity that has actually put large sections of our society in backwardness. In that sense they are deprived of opportunity and that is the reason why we have such a large section of our society who are depressed, deprived and outcast. It is only by denying them the opportunity, some people excel and others are just there to serve them. 

Odisha had representative in the Constituent Assembly. They were elected by the then limited electorate which was elected in 1946 to the Odisha Provincial Assembly. Nine members were elected to the Constituency Assembly in 1946. Three years from 1946 till December 26, 1949 when the Draft Constitution was adopted, those two years 11 months and some days were the formative years of our Independent country. Those were very turbulent times of our sub-continent. Turbulent in the sense when the Constituent Assembly was formed we had the whole Indian sub-continent minus Sri Lanka and today’s Myanmar, Nepal and Bhutan; the rest which was called Indian British Empire that had formed the Constituent Assembly. That is why Dr. Ambedkar was elected from Jessore and Khulna Constituencies to the Constituent Assembly. When Partition took place, a large part of our country went away to Pakistan. But during that period, there was a large part in the nation which was not part of the Constituent Assembly. They were 500 odd Princely States. They were not part of the Constituent Assembly. When the Drafting Committee was formed – the Constituent Assembly elected the Drafting Committee which had elected Babasaheb Ambedkar as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee – that time also those 500 odd Princely States were not part of the Constituent Assembly. A large section, which was then called the Muslim dominated areas, went to Pakistan. The Princely States considering themselves as independent and the onus came on the then Deputy Prime Minister and the then Home Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to amalgamate them with the Indian union. But there was a rider from the Father of the Nation: ‘Do not use force. Do not compel them to come and join us.’ That was the rider that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel kept till the end. He practiced it till the end. There was upheaval within the Princely States to join the Union and to be a part of the progress of the nation. That is why the first amalgamation took place on 14th November, 1947 in my State in Odisha, a small Princely State called Nilgiri. Subsequently, it was on 1st January, 1948 when 26 Princely States joined the Union. At that time Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel had said: ‘We were all wondering how could we make this happen.’ That so-called undeveloped State prepared the key to unlock the lock of our problem? Subsequently, in 1948, Representatives from the Princely States were elected or nominated to the Constituent Assembly.

Sir, there were nine Members – Dr. Harekrushna Mahtab, Shrimati Malati Devi Choudhury, Shri Bishwanth Das, Shri Bodhram Dubey, Shri Laxminarayan Sahu, Shri B. Das (His is the only portrait which we find in this edifice of our Sansad Bhavan), two portraits are there in the Committee Rooms upstairs in the first floor, Shri Nanda Kishore Das, Shri Rajkushna Bose, Shri Santunu Kumar Das. Sir, I remember these nine Members today because they participated vigorously in the making of the Constitution. 

The task that was before the Constituent Assembly can be gauged from some lines, which the Chairman or the President of the Constituent Assembly then was called, Dr. Rajendra Prasad had said on 26th November, 1949. He said:

“I would like to mention some facts which will show the tremendousness of the task which we undertook some three years ago. If you consider the population with which the Assembly has had to deal, you will find that it is more than the population of the whole of Europe minus Russia, being 319 millions as against 317 millions. The countries of Europe have never been able to join together or coalesce even in a Confederacy, much less under one unitary Government. Here, in spite of the size of the population and the country, we have succeeded in framing a Constitution which covers the whole of it. Apart from the size, there were other difficulties. ”

He goes on to narrate what are the other difficulties. While deliberating on this issue, I may be allowed to say that.

“When the British decided to leave this country, they transferred power to us (to the Constituent Assembly); but at the same time, they also declared that all the treaties and engagements they had with the Princes had lapsed. The paramountcy which they had so long exercised and by which they could keep the Princes in order also lapsed. The Indian Government was then faced with the problem of tackling these States which had different traditions of rule, some of them having some form of popular representation in Assemblies and some having no semblance of anything like that. ”

Sir, with the amalgamation of the States, the major problem that came up was that all sections of the society were empowered. Democracy empowered all sections of society. Those fissiparous activities that were prevalent before the British came, also became very active; and it was a challenge not only to the Administration but also to look at a future and frame a Constitution to that effect so that it will test the time. But the best thing which I consider, what has been done through this Constitution, is that every individual has a vote. All individuals are equal in this democratic temper. 

Here, I would quote Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who said:

“At first we were able to get rid of separate electorates which had poisoned our political life for so many years...”

Reservations of seats for the communities which enjoyed separate electorates before, had to be conceded, although on the basis of their population and not as had been done in the Act of 1919 and the Act of 1935 of giving additional representation on account of the so called historical and other superiority claimed by some of the communities. Constitution does not provide for reservation of seats on communal basis but for reservation only in favour of two classes of people of our population namely, the depressed classes who are Hindus and the tribal people on account of their backwardness in education and in other respects. Something has been forgotten to be told. I think Leader of the major Opposition has mentioned to a great extent. It was Jawaharlal Nehru who had moved the preamble of our constitution. He had framed the preamble of the constitution on which practically everyone of us has been deliberating upon. Dr. Ambedkar mentioned the names of these Committees. Several of these Committees were chaired either by Jawaharlal Nehru or Sardar Patel. Thus, goes the credit for the fundamentals of our constitution. 

Sir, I would now come to another aspect. It is not that during the framing of the constitution, it was not being criticized. If someone goes through the newspapers of those days, a number of articles, a number of statements even inside the Constituent Assembly, a number of resolutions were also moved and amendments were also moved. But what did Dr. Ambedkar had said. I quote: 

“The condemnation of the constitution largely comes from two parties – the Communist Party and the Socialist Party.”

That explains most of the case. I need not elaborate on that. But when one says about fundamental rights, here is Baba Saheb’s version. 

“I do not say that fundamental rights can never be absolute and the limitations set upon them can never be looked at. What I do say is that the principles embodied in the constitution are the views of the present generation of if you think this is to be over-statement.” 

Then, he goes on to refer Jafferson, the great American statesman, who played a very great role in framing the American constitution and he quotes: 

“We may consider each generation as a distinct nation with a right by the will of the majority to bind themselves but none to bind the succeeding generation more than the inhabitants of another country”.

This is what Jafferson had said. This was quoted by Baba Saheb Ambedkar. So, what has been there in the constitution cannot be changed is a fallacy. That is what Dr. Ambedkar has said. Let us read what has been propounded during the discussion and what the founding fathers have said and further he has also expressed his anguish. 

While concluding his speech, he said:

“Here I could have ended but my mind is so full of the future of our country that I feel I ought to take this occasion to give expression of some of my reflections thereof. On 26th January, 1950, India will be an independent country.”

There were cheers all around. 

“The point is that she once lost the independence she had. Will she lose it second time? It is this thought which makes me most anxious for the future. What bothers greatly is the fact that not only India has once before lost independence but she lost it by the infidelity and treachery of some of our own people.”

I need not go into the names that he had mentioned. His question was, “Will history repeat itself?” It is because this he was delivering in 1949. Already partition had taken place. Communal riots have taken place. A large number of people had migrated from one country to another. A lot of bloodshed had taken place. During that time he is saying,

“It is this thought which fills me with anxiety. This anxiety is deepened by the realisation of the fact that in addition to our old enemies in the form of castes and creeds we are going to have many political parties with diverse and opposing political creeds. Will Indians place the country above their creed or will they place creed above the country? I do not know. But this much is certain that if the parties place creed above country, our Independence will be put in jeopardy a second time and probably be lost for ever. This eventuality we must all resolutely guard against. We must be determined to defend our Independence with the last drop of our blood.”

These were resounding words which must have reverberated in the Constituent Assembly, the Central Hall that we call today. 

“It is not that India did not know what is democracy. There was a time when India was studded with republics, and even where there were monarchies, they were either elected or limited. They were never absolute. It is not that Indian did not know Parliaments or Parliamentary Procedure. A study of the Budhist Bihkshu Sanghas discloses that not only there were Parliaments—for the Sanghas were nothing but Parliaments—but the Sanghas knew and observed all the rules of Parliamentary Procedure known to modern times. … ”

He was talking about ballot, voting, censure motion and about regularization.

“This democratic system India lost. Will she lose it a second time?” That was his anxiety and his question. I do not know. 

Again I quote,

“If we wish to maintain democracy not merely in form but also in fact what must we do? The first thing in my judgement we must do is to hold fast to Constitutional methods of achieving our social and economic objectives. It means that we must abandon the bloody method of revolution. It means that we must abandon the method of civil disobedience, non-cooperation and Satyagraha. When there was no way left for Constitutional methods for achieving economic and social objectives, there was a great deal of justification for Unconstitutional methods. But where Constitutional methods are open, there can be no justification for these Unconstitutional methods.”

It is because today in free India, Satyagraha and non-cooperation have become the rule of the day. Everyday, every time when we see, this House is assembling and there are people who are capable enough to jump to the Well and get the House adjourned. At least, our Party is not that competent enough and we would not like to do it because we know jumping to the Well and coming out alive in one piece is also a Herculean task. But that is what is happening not only inside the House but also outside. If I want to get my things done, if I want to get something from the Government, then this is what we have learnt forcefully during the last 67 years. We are not indulging in any Constitutional activity. It is all unconstitutional activity that we suddenly jump into. Is this the way? Very forcefully we say that this is the freedom that we have achieved, this is how we achieved Independence and that is how we will achieve our rights and we can meet our demand.

Sir, I need not go into all other aspects, that I had thought that I would be saying, relating to the Constitution - how it was amalgamated from different constitutions and what the reply of Baba Saheb to that was. But I would like to mention here that there is a crisis of parliamentarism today in our country. Instability was the rule of the day for more than 15 years, irrespective of the party in power. Today, we have a Government which has absolute majority in this House of People, but Treasury Benches consider Rajya Sabha a stumbling bloc. Not letting Parliament function is a cross-party phenomenon. We should not forget that representative nature of any Parliament rests on intellectual foundations. Since the European Revolution of 1848, the core principle of parliamentarism has been the search for truth by discussion and debate. This is how Bentham, Burke, Guizot and Mill imagined Parliament. Prior to that date, Governments were run by monarchs and the decision-making process was in secrecy. 

Before 1947, the country had an unbroken history of Government untouched by any public opinion. After attaining Independence, all sections, all classes and all sects are enjoying freedom. All are aspiring to achieve benefits for themselves. It is only our Constitution which ensured the rule of law. At a time when there are so many ideological classes, rising intolerance among the people of various communities, growing inequalities, and suppression of women’s right, it is only the Constitution of our country that can bind everyone together and help find solutions to various problems. 

In these difficult times, it is important to have knowledge and better understanding of the Constitution. That is why, during the last Session from our party, a suggestion was given that as we are observing the 125th Birth Anniversary of Baba Saheb Ambedkar and as November 26 always invariably falls in the Winter Session, it is in fitness of things that we should observe the Constitution Day and also observe the 125th Birth Anniversary of Baba Saheb Ambedkar. Of course, since 1979, November 26 is being observed as the Lawyers’ Day. Yesterday the Supreme Court Bar Association observed it in a fitting manner. 

Sir, I have only three suggestions to make for the Government and for the House to consider. Today’s students are tomorrow’s leaders. It is the responsibility of the teaching community to educate students about the Constitution and make them informed citizens. Constitution Day is a one day affair, but Constitution education is a process leading to right thinking and noble behaviour. Reading out the preamble, conducting quiz will not help students become patriotic citizens. There is a need to develop a proper understanding of the Constitution, right attitude towards it, ability to interpret it to the current situation and the willingness to keep its spirit alive will make them patriotic. Are we striving in that regard? I would hope that the Government will take that step. 

Secondly, during last 18 months, we have heard about cooperative federalism. One guessed it meant cooperation between Centre and the States in running the country. It is actually derived from Right Wing Republicans of the United States of America who have coined competitive federalism. Since adoption of the Constitution, it was essential for all regions to flourish under the watchful eyes of the helpful Union Government. Unfortunately, the colonial system of centralisation of power only grew with passage of time, making a travesty of our Constitution. Maintaining colonial style bureaucracy and top down devolution has not got much changed. There is a need to introduce fiscal federalism. Some States have larger population than the major countries of Europe. Germany has an exemplary federal structure that can be followed for devolution of funds to District Headquarters. Our problem today is of democratic deficit in our Districts. 

The third and last suggestion would be on a uniform civil code. Hon. Member Satpathy from our party has mentioned about it. The Supreme Court of India has already asked the Union Government to take a quick decision in accordance with Article 44 of the Constitution, Directive Principles of State Policy. BJP has been demanding for a uniform civil code. I am sure they are not demanding for imposing the Hindu code. 

We had separate electorates. That was done away with. In today’s world, Islam is the most modern religion. There is codification. When separate electorates were there, we had Myanmar, we had Sri Lanka, we had the whole Bangladesh, Pakistan, India, Princely States altogether. At that time a separate code was being prescribed for different sections for the benefit of the colonial powers. Once the Constitution has come into force, Constitution has enough safeguards for protection of religious and linguistic minorities and their rights. After Supreme Court’s prodding, the Government is duty bound to act on it. My suggestion would be that the Government should begin discussions with people of all shades of opinion on this subject. There is a need to hold inclusive consultations for a uniform civil code with all stakeholders. 

I conclude by saying what Swami Vivekananda had said long back. We had heard from our saints, ‘Ekam sat, vipra bahudha vadanti’. Paths may be many but the Almighty is one. Similarly Swamiji said that our religion, the Hindu religion, not only tolerates other religions but also believes, also respects other religions. That is why in India we have all religious activities which can be performed according to their rights. Yet our independence, our freedom is till at the tip of our nose, not beyond. It should not hit the other person. That should be the spirit. 

With these words, I pay my respects to Babasaheb Ambedkar. Thank you.

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: Hon. Members, please do not take more than five or ten minutes. Prime Minister’s reply will be at 4:30 pm today and we have to conclude the discussion before that. 

DR. TAPAS MANDAL (RANAGHAT): At least the treasury bench now realised that Ambedkar is a wonderful worthy tool for exploitation to run the winter session of parliament without disruption at beginning and opposition did not show its intolerance to that sensitive issue of debate. It is the fate of Dr. Ambedkar in Indian politics to be used by poor politicians for ill intensions since Independence simply because the caste factor does not lose its hold on Indian politics. 

It is a fact that majority of the people including middle class know too little about Ambedkar. They only seem to know that Ambedkar had criticized Hinduism throughout his life and that he was responsible for the policy of reservation. Somebody knows he was the architect of the Constitution of India, that he had PhD degree in economics from Columbia University, that he was D.Sc, D.Lit, Bar-at Law, that the Reserve Bank of India and Finance Commission of India is based on his idea, that he fought for the employment of women and that he wrote many scholarly books on various topics. Ambedkar had also insisted on the word 'scientific temperament' in the Constitution and may other things. More importantly, despite all this, we still criticize him or any one of his stature because democracy is one of the biggest gifts he has given to every Indian. 

The BJP's stand on Ambedkar has always been dubious. On one hand, the BJP's parent organisation RSS and its wings act contrary to the ideology of Ambedkar and on the other hand, they keep praising him. It was the Jan Sangh's strong opposition to the Hindu Code Bill which led to the resignation of Ambedkar from the Law Ministry. It was Guru Golwalkar, the second sarasanghachalak of the RSS who pitched for the continuation of 'Chaturvarnya Vyavastha' and it is the same RSS family that still dreams about the formulation of a 'Hindu Nation'. Despite all these differences, the RSS seem to have one strong reason to praise Ambedkar in its morning prayers -that he with his followers converted to Buddhism and not Islam. In fact, some members of the RSS dare to say that Gautam Buddha was an avatar of Vishnu, which has gone down very well in comic literature. Hence, the BJP's love and respect for Ambedkar is nothing but political opportunism and inefficiency to create a leader of his stature. The BJP's strategy is clear, let's not discuss Ambedkar ideology but keep praising him. And they have succeeded in this in many ways, which is one kind of defeat for the legacy of Ambedkar. 

The BJP and Congress are two sides of same coin. If the BJP is dubious, then the Congress is shameless. The Congress's policy towards Ambedkar was different at the Centre and the State level. Their Central Leadership had always been so busy in the glorification of one family, that they did not get time to understand the legacy and contribution of other leaders. So Ambedkar always remained neglected by the Congress Government. In fact, he was awarded with the Barat Ratna only after the Congress lost power and V.P Singh became Prime Minister. 

It is not the BJP and Congress, but leaders from his own Republican Party of India who are trying their best to insult him and his ideology in every possible way. Ambedkar had named his party 'Scheduled Castes Federation' but at one point he wanted to change the name to make it inclusive and reach out to every caste and religion. He dreamt of a day when the caste system and inequality would be eradicated from our society. As per his wish, after his sad demise, his followers changed the name of the party to the Republican Party of India. But they failed drastically to fulfill his dream. Their internal confrontations and political opportunism led to the destruction of the 'Ambedkar movement' and his values. 

Fortunately, despite all kinds of injustice, his true followers hope for change and till that day, no one can defeat Ambedkar. 

I express my profound respect and regards to a great man of the world and masiha of depressed classes, Dr. Ambedkar on the occasion of special session of Parliament as a part of celebration of his 125th birth anniversary on Constitution day. I think we can express our gratitude and regards to Dr. Ambedkar by upholding each and every words of the holy Constitution as drafted by him. We should work hard to reach a destination he dreamt of, a day, when the caste system and inequality would be eradicated from our society. 

SHRI SANKAR PRASAD DATTA (TRIPURA WEST): On the occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar the Lok Sabha is debating on commitment to India's Constitution. Now I like to draw the attention on the practice of untouchability and different form of violence against Scheduled Caste communities. Still it is continuing. The conviction rate of people accused in such cases continues to be low. Laws such as The Scheduled Castes and the Schedules Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act need to be strengthened and fully implemented the Manual Scavengers Act is also yet to be implemented. Large sections of dalits in rural India are landless workers without assets. There is huge backlog in filling up reserved posts. Development schemes lie unimplemented. Dalit Christian and Muslims have been denied recognition as Scheduled Castes, and are consequently excluded from benefits to which Scheduled Castes are entitled. 

In this circumstances, being a citizen of India and peoples representative from Tripura, I like to draw attention that on behalf of the people of Tripura, "Tripura Scheduled Castes Co-ordinate Committee" and the "Dalit Soson Mukti Manch" collected more than a lakh signature from the people of Tripura in general and Scheduled Castes community in particular. These signed papers are now with us and to be submitted to the Central Government. They have demanded that the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act amendment be passed immediately. Sufficient money should be allocated in the SC/ST sub plan. Reservation should be implemented in private sector also and for this a new Act is to be enacted. 

Hence, if we sincerely like to pay homage to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar we have to fulfill the aspiration of the Dalit people and to bring them at the lightened part of the society otherwise these discussions will be vague one. I hope that the country will stand on this point the advancement of the country. 

*श्री नित्यानन्द राय (उजियारपुर) ः ""संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता"" वि­ाय पर महत्वपूर्ण चर्चा हो रही है। बाबासाहेब भीमराव अंबेडकर जी द्वारादिया गया संविधान अधिकारों के साथ कर्त्तव्यों की भी पहचान करता है। यह संविधान लोकतंत्र को संरक्षित तथा एकता और अखंडता एवं स्वतंत्रता को बल प्रदान करता है। संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता हम सबके लिए धर्म है। भीमराव अंबेडकर एवं प्रारूप समिति के सदस्यों ने संविधान में जो व्यवस्था दी है, उसका मूल उद्देश्य है- सामाजिक न्याय, सामाजिक समरसता, आर्थिक उन्नति, धार्मिक स्वतंत्रता, नारी उत्थान एवं सम्मान, मजदूरों का हक, श्रम का सम्मान एवं किसानों की उन्नति। छुआ-छूत का का कोढ़ जड़ से समाप्त हो। वंचितों को, दलितों को, पिछड़ों को उत्थान का अवसर मिले तथा उनका आर्थिक, सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक उत्थान हो और उसमें कोई व्यवधान न आये, इसका प्रावधान भी अपने संविधान की विशे­ाता है। इस हेतु आरक्षण की व्यवस्था दी गई है। आरक्षण का लाभ जिन-जिन जातियों को प्राप्त है, उसे ही व्यापकता से मिले, परंतु इसका लाभ उन्हीं जातियों के शी­ाऩ परिवारों तक ही सीमित न रहे, उन्हीं जातियों के अब तक आरक्षण के लाभ से वंचित परिवारों तक पहुंचे, इसका भी ख्याल रखना चाहिए। तभी भीमराव अंबेडकर जी और पंडित दीनदयाल उपाध्याय जी के सपनों का समरस एवं सुदृढ़ समाज निर्मित होगा। यह सोच वर्तमान के रा­ट्रवादी विचारकों के विचारों से परिलक्षित होता है। यही उनका भाव है, इसे समझना पड़ेगा तथा इस पर अमल होना चाहिए।

सब अधिकारों एवं कर्त्तव्यों को मात दे दी जाती है तु­िटकरण से। जहां तु­िटकरण होगा वहां कभी न्याय नहीं होगा। तु­िटकरण की नीति, भारत को अपने जेहन से मिटा देनी चाहिए। तु­िटकरण ही हमारे देश के बंटवारे का कारण भी बना। विभाजन का आधार ही गलत था और विभाजन के कारणों से हम सभी अवगत है। यह सदन कक्ष महान भगत सिंह की अमर गाथा का गवाह है। हज़ारों बलिदानियों ने कभी सोचा भी नहीं होगा कि अपना देश आज़ाद होने से पहले विभाजित होगा। भारत स्वतंत्र हुआ पर स्वतंत्रता के पहले ही विभाजित हो गया। कौन जिम्मेदार है इस विभाजन का?

माननीय सोनिया जी ने कांग्रेस के कराची अधिवेशन चर्चा की थी। कहाँ हैं करांची आज? इसका अफसोस कांग्रेस को है की नहीं? माननीय खड़गे जी द्वारा सदन में आर्य और अनार्य की बात की गई। यह बातें भारत की विरासत, संस्कृति, एकता एवं पहचान को कमज़ोर करने वाली हैं, इसकी चर्चा करना अनुचित है। भारतवासी होते हुए भी पाश्चात्य प्रवृत्ति के इतिहासकारों द्वारा रचित यह साजिश है। इसका विरोध होना चाहिए।

अंबेडकर जी के ही शब्दों में-"" हमारे पास ये स्वतंत्रता इसलिए है ताकि हम अपनी सामाजिक व्यवस्था जो असमानता, भेदभाव और अन्य चीजों से भरी है, जो हमारे मौलिक अधिकारों से टकराव में है, को सुधार सकें।"" इस सुधार को एक गरीब का बेटा ही संभव कर सकता है। एक गरीब का बेटा अंबेडकर जी ने संविधान रचा और दूसरा गरीब का बेटा माननीय प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी संविधान की सोच न्याय और विकास का इतिहास रचेंगे।

कवि वृन्द के शब्द मे भीमराव अंबेडकर की सोच समावेशित है-

दान दीन को दीजिये, मिटै दरिद्र कि पीड।

औ­ाध वाको दीजिये, जाके रोग शरीर।।

DR. BHAGIRATH PRASAD (BHIND): Preamble of Constitution of India reflects the goals and aspirations of the people of India. It evinces the commitment of the Constitution to ensure and promote the principles of Justice, Liberty, Equality and fraternity. The Fundamental Rights are designed to remove social and economic inequality to make equal opportunities available to all citizens of India. The social, economic and political justice is supposed to be secured through enforcement of fundamental rights and Directive Principles of State Policy. 

But the ideals enshrined in the constitution were in conflict with socio-economic reality in India at the time of our independence. Hence our Constitution was to confront with a tremendous task of leveling hierarchical society finally forgoing bonds of brotherhood among the socially and economically unequal citizens of India. The chief architect of our constitution Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1949 aptly remarked. "In politics we will be recognizing the principle of one man one vote and one vote one value. In our social and economic life, we shall, by reason of our social and economic structure, continue to deny the principle of one man one value. How long shall we continue to live this life of contradictions?"

Even after the elapse of 66 years, the contradiction persists. Without the social democracy how can we have genuine political democracy? At the time of independence without creating a level playing field, we commenced the game of democracy. Power-hungry socio-economically dominant groups assumed power reinforcing the unjust and essentially undemocratic social infrastructure. This hampered the growth of democracy in all its formations: social political and economical. This systemic deformity vitiated democratic process of social upliftment and poverty elevation programs. Far from the constitutional assurance of justice, the girls of weaker sections of our society are raped, their houses are burnt, the bridegrooms riding on horse are violently attacked and innocent people are murdered. These crimes are generally committed unilaterally by the high caste social groups. 

In these circumstances, social democracy in India as envisaged under the Constitution still seems a distant dream. In fact the low position in the social hierarchy coincides with poverty resulting in reinforcing economic inequality. The poor in general depend more on the dominant caste of their locality which controls land, economy and political power. Stringent provisions against caste and its practice could not eradicate it. It more or less remained a facade to justify the commitment to the constituent without effective action on the ground. The will power and sincerity to enforce law was missing. The vested interests in hierarchical society nullified the legal provisions. 

What is progress? Whether Indian Constitution was committed only to highways, grand hotels, luxurious malls and mega cities? We are competing with the cities of the world, while common man is left out. People-centred development is missing or it stands with poor achievements. Even in 21st century some people are bound to live in dehumanized conditions. What we have done to our ten crore of tribals? All forest, excise and mining laws were enforced indiscriminately in tribal areas. The innocent triblas were exploited, looted and devasted by the government machinery and their contractors. Governors of State having special powers did not intervene to protect tribal people and their culture. 

I commenced my career in IAS from Bastar district of Madhya Pradesh. Four decades ago, it was extremely, peacefully, socially and culturally very rich areas. Bastar District was geographically larger than the Kerala State. Now you could see the difference and compare the development of both the areas. While Kerala is competing with the global standards of development and Bastar may be the worst ruined place on Earth. Utter disregard to the tribal development has ruined the area. We have not only failed in our constituent commitment, we deceived the innocent people. As a result we have earned the wrath of the peaceful people in the form of most violent left-wing terrorism in India. 

The welfare measures to help the poor failed to yield result due to exploitative system working on the ground. Lacs of acres of barren land was allotted to SC/ST and to below poverty line families during the post independence period. After making the land cultivable and fertile, they could not retain it due to pulls and pressures of the dominant class. As a result, today more than 56% of rural population is landless. Above 90% of the landless belong to SC/ST. They are rendered homeless for want of employment. They are deprived of voting rights, schooling of their children, safety and dignity of their women. You may find them hanging on the construction of high rising buildings in cities, working in deep mines or seasonal crop-cutting far from their home lands. On the other hands, concentration of wealth and black money has blocked the road of economic democracy. 

This is evident from the fact that only 3 crore out of 125 crore people of India are income tax payers. This serves to show that the middle class could not grow to sustain our economic democracy in India. The common man is grateful to our leader Shri Narendra Modi and the finance minister who have initiated the stringent measures to curb black money. For the first time in history, financial democracy in the country was introduced in the form of Jan Dhan Yojana. Every citizen of our country is entitled rather facilitated to have account in the bank. All benefits will accrue to the citizen through their account. The entry of the common man into the financial system of the country is a vehicle to achieve ultimately economic democracy as visualized in the Constitution. 

Dr. Ambedkar emphasised upon educating the masses. He considered education as a means of emancipation for the weaker sections of society. This was a difficult task to achieve in a society where traditionally an attempt made by the common man to acquire knowledge was punishable as a crime. Even in an adverse social background, India has made significant progress in promoting universal education. But the ignorance and poverty still impede the flow of benefits of education in tribal areas and to Dalits in our society. 

Extension of school education is our appreciable achievement but quality education is still far away. In this globalised world, quality is prerequisite for real employment. The growing privatization and so called public schools are monopolizing the claim of quality education. And it is true to a great extent. Entire education system is now a market place. Those who have money can purchase. Education is now a commodity. The rich purchase education and claim to be meritorious while the talented poor reconcile with their fate for they cannot afford it. Many toppers in IIT and in other coveted centres of learning fail to join the institutions for want of fees. If a meritorious poor goes back from the doors of the temple of knowledge for want of funds, we fail to protect equality of status and of opportunity as enshrined in our constitution. 

The most topical issue relating to our Constitution is the reservation in services for the Scheduled Castes/Tribes and other backward classes. Most of the Governments were committed formally to the provisions of reservation. An effective implementation would have ended the reservation by now. This is a fact, despite constitutional provisions the government has not yet enacted a law for reservation in services. How can we punish those responsible for non-implementation of reservation? Central Act for reservation must take place by this 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. 

Rationale for reservation was settled originally in the Poona pact of 1932. The Constitution of India followed the provisions of the pact. Why Army and the higher judiciary were left out of reservation? Are we still pursuing the policy of the marshal and non-marshal races which resulted in our slavery for sanctuaries? If we accept the principle of human equality then the discrimination in reservation must end. If certain sections are not up to the standards, then who is responsible? The erstwhile regimes for more than six decades must take responsibility for dereliction of duty under the Constitution. They failed to provide quality education and support to the weaker sections to make them succeed in general competition. 

Issue of reservation in promotion has arisen because of initial level of reservation was not implemented. If assistant engineers and assistant professors are appointed in adequate number initially then at higher level, they will not require out turn promotion. They will have qualification and experience to be promoted normally. This is an irony that simple regulations of reservation in promotion are implemented without any difficulty in the USA but in India, express constitutional provisions fail to materialize. Are we really committed to the spirit of the Constitution? 

Several Communities recently, launched mass movements for reservation in services. We are confronting an alarming situation where these demands of reservation cannot be conceded. On the other hand, counter movements against reservation are on the rise on Social media. Even we witness processions on the streets for and against the reservation of Scheduled Caste and Tribe. Most of this animosity is based on misinformation. Firstly, the unemployed youth feel that they are out of job because of reservation. Secondly, their understanding is that the reserve category candidates are without merit. But truth is that the gap of percentage of marks is narrowing and some of the reserved candidates are in general list on the basis of merit. 

The policy of reservation emerged to compensate the social deprivation not alone poverty. In due course, the scheme of reservation got politicised on the part of governments. On the other hand, the reservation was to be served as a medicine but we have made it a food for the beneficiaries. The medicine must have been effective with proper diet. The Governments did not bother to improve the merit of the candidates. They watered the leaves not the roots. Educational facilities in the best institutions were extended to the weaker sections of society on a large scale. The candidate from Bastar was put against the academically groomed candidates from Saint Stephen, Delhi School of Economics or IITs. Where is the competition? I suggest to the Government to establish model residential colleges in all the districts of the country. Give them exposure to the best institution. Provide them liberal scholarship, hostels and conducive environment on a large scale. The merit of the common man will flourish. You will see all of them in the general merit list. The stigma of reservation will vanish. This way, reservation may not suddenly end, but it will wither away. 

We have with us our great leader as Shri Narendra Modi who will certainly make this dream true. He entered parliament - the temple of democracy vowing his head with utmost commitment to the Constitution. I am sure, the vision and mission of Baba Ambedkar and the aspirations of the people of India will be realized under his leadership. 

PROF. A.S.R. NAIK (MAHABUBABAD): The discussion in Parliament on Constitution Day as a part of 125th birth anniversary celebrations of Bharat Ratna, towering personality, the chief architect of Indian Constitution Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is welcoming decision. It is appropriate for this august body to pay tributes to the Chief Architect and main instrumentality, the Chairman of Drafting Committee of Indian Constitution, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. 

This august body consists of 137 representatives belonging to oppressed communities of the country. It would be our bounden duty to see that the idea of social justice and empowerment of the people in getting appropriate share in social, political and economic areas is still a myth. Reservations in private sector could not be achieved. In addition to other issues, these issues also should be on the agenda of the honourable members, which is nothing but making the vision of Dr. Ambedkar into reality as according to Babasaheb Ambedkar "Political power is a master key which can open each and every lock of the society".

This day is a tribute to all those great framing fathers who worked excellently to give India a Constitution we are very proud of. While appreciating the discussion in this Parliament on "Constitution and its framer, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Commitment to India's Constitution as part of the 125th birth anniversary of B.R. Ambedkar", I submit that celebration of such a kind should not be mere formality but continuous process whereby we may inform the citizens of this country that the contribution of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, who in spite of all hardship in the life contributed the socio-political and economic justice to all. It is to be rightly held that Dr. Ambedkar should not be associated with downtrodden communities but his understanding and vision for future India for all should be remembered for decades to come. However, one cannot forget about the historical socio-economic background of the poor and downtrodden communities of this country who were being oppressed and suppressed for centuries. It is invariably essential to provide favourable treatment and treat with protective discrimination. Here I wish to draw the attention that if reservations are only solution for social justice and empowerment, Dalits and other backward classes in this country are more than 75 percent. Vision of Dr. Ambedkar is not to provide communal reservation for ever but to provide equality of opportunities and equitable empowerment to all, hence provision in the Constitution for protective discrimination. Today the downtrodden population is more than 75 percent but reservation in education and employments are restricted to 50 percent only in all States except one or two. It is time to rethink of enhancement of reservation to these classes depending upon their population. Further, the corporate world is enjoying many benefits from the Governments but there are no reservations in corporate business houses. This aspect also needs to be thought. These are the aspirations of Dr. Ambedkar in achieving socio-economic justice. 

Indian Constitution incorporate the social and political philosophy of B.R. Ambedkar which is most noticeably evident in the various provisions of the Constitution. There are certain instances in the history of independent India that at times attempts were made to tamper the spirit of Constitution. Here it is pertinent to look into the vision of Dr. Ambedkar in future working of this Constitution. "However good a Constitution may be, it is sure to turn out bad because those who are called to work it, happen to be a bad. However bad a Constitution may be, it may turn out good if those who are called to work it, happen to be a good lot".

The real purpose of celebrating this Constitution Day is to rededicate ourselves and making just as aspired by the framing fathers of our Constitution with all concern and commitment in bringing desirable socio-economic change in the country and social justice to all on which cardinal principles solid foundation constitutional edifice is erected and strive hard in getting appropriate share in respect of the downtrodden and oppressed communities of the country. 

*श्री ए.टी. नाना पाटील (जलगांव) ः सर्वप्रथम मैं प्रधानमंत्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के संविधान अंगीकार करने के दिन 26 नवंबर को संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाए जाने के निर्णय का तहेदिल से स्वागत करता हॅं। इस निर्णय का ही परिणाम है कि हम यहां आज संविधान दिवस के पावन अवसर पर लोकतंत्र के इस मंदिर में इकट्ठे हुए हैं। निश्चित ही संविधान के मुख्य निर्माता बी.आर. अंबेडकर के जीवन के बारे में जागरूकता फैलाने की दिशा में यह एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है। आज़ादी के 65 सालों में यह पहला अवसर है कि हमारी सरकार ने 26 नवंबर को संविधान दिवस घो­िात कर हम सांसदों को इसके निर्माताओ के प्रति अपनी भावभीनी श्रद्धांजलि तथा कृतज्ञता प्रकट करने का अवसर प्रदान किया है।

यह निर्णय निश्चय ही महत्वपूर्ण है कि इसी दिन प्रत्येक व­ाऩ स्कूली बच्चों को संविधान एवं डॉ. अंबेडकर के बारे में बताया जाएगा। इससे हमारी भावी पीढ़ी को डॉ. अंबेडकर तथा संविधान सभा के अन्य महत्वपूर्ण सदस्यों के बारे में जानने का अवसर मिलेगा। यह अत्यंत ही प्रशंसनीय है कि भारत सरकार के इस प्रयास के तहत डॉ. अंबेडकर के जीवन से जुड़े पांच महत्वपूर्ण स्थलों को पंच तीर्थ के रूप में विकसित किया जाएगा। इनमें मध्य प्रदेश, दिल्ली का अलीपुर हाउस, इंदु मिल स्मारक, मुंबई में डॉ. अंबेडकर का आवास तथा लंदन में हाल में खरीदा गया भवन शामिल है। मोदी जी ने ठीक ही कहा है कि ये पंच तीर्थ भारत के लोगों के लिए पवित्र स्थल हेंगे तथा वे सामाजिक एकता के लिए काम करने के प्रेरणा स्थल बनेंगे। आदरणीय मोदी जी के इस सराहनीय कदम के लिए मैं उनके प्रति अपना तथा इस सदन का आभार प्रकट करता हॅं।

भारत का संविधान दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा लिखित संविधान है। यहां मैं हमारे संविधान की कतिपय विशे­ाताओं का उल्लेख करना चाहूंगा। भारत का संविधान कोई मौलिक दस्तावेज नहीं है। हमारे संविधान निर्माताओं ने दुनिया के सभी संविधानों का गहन अध्ययन कर उनमें से अच्छी बातों को हमारे संविधान में शामिल किया। चाहे वह इंग्लैण्ड की संसदीय प्रणाली हो अथवा अमेरिका का संघीय ढांचा प्रणाली। कनाडा की अर्ध-संघीय प्रणाली अथवा आयरलैण्ड के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत। इस प्रकार भारतीय संविधान पर ब्रिटिश, अमेरिका, आस्ट्रेलिया, कनाडा, जर्मनी, जापान, आयरलैण्ड, द. अफ्रीका तथा फ्रांसीसी संविधान का संयुव्त प्रभाव है। कुल मिलाकर कहें, तो हमारी संसदीय सरकार का ढांचा एकात्मक विशे­ाताओं के साथ-साथ संघात्मक है।

इस पावन अवसर पर मैं संविधान सभा के उन सभी सम्मानित सदस्यों को भी नमन करता हॅं जिन्होंने पार्टी अनुशासन से ऊपर उठकर संविधान निर्माण में अपना सार्थक योगदान दिया। डॉ. अंबेडकर ने उनके योगदान की सराहना करते हुए कहा भी था, ""यदि इस संविधान के सभी सदस्य पार्टी अनुशासन के आगे घुटने टेक देते तो उसकी कार्रवाइयां बहुत फीकी होती। अपनी संपूर्ण कठोरता में पार्टी अनुशासन सभी को जी-हुजूरियों के जमावाड़े में बदल देता। सौभाग्यवश, उसमें विद्रोही थे। वे थे कामत, डॉ.पी.एस. देशमुख, सिधवा, प्रो. सक्सैना और पं. ठाकुरदास भार्गव। इनके साथ प्रो. के.टी. शाह और पं. हृदयनाथ कुंजरू का भी उल्लेख किया जाना चाहिए। उन्होंने जो बिंदु उठाए, उनमें से अधिकांश विचारात्मक थे। उनके सुझावों की महत्ता बहुत अधिक थी तथा उससे सभा की कार्रवाइयों को जानदार तथा सार्थक बनाने में भारी योगदान दिया। मैं इस अवसर पर उन सभी के प्रति अपनी कृतज्ञता प्रकट करता हॅं। उनके बिना सभा को संविधान के मूल सिद्धांतों की व्याख्या करने का अवसर न मिला होता, जो संविधान को यंत्रवत् पारित करा लेने से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण था।

आजकल हमारे देश में असहि­णु होने के बारे में बड़ो शोर मचाया जा रहा है। वहीं दूसरी ओर, हमारी रा­ट्रीय अखंडता पर कई तरह के कुठाराघात प्रतिदिन की दर से होते हैं। रा­ट्रीय गीत का कुछ लोगों द्वारा बार-बार अपमान किये जाने से हमारे लोकतंत्र को शर्मसार करदिया है। ऐसे रा­ट्रद्रोही लोग इस तरह के निंदनीय कृत्य बार-बार करने का दुस्साहस कैसे कर पाते हैं? फिर भी कुछ तथाकथित धर्मनिरपेक्षतावादी हमारे देश को असहि­णु होने का दावा करते हैं। इस निंदनीय कृत्य के लिए अब तक किसी को भी किसी प्रकार की सजा नहीं दी गई थी। जहां तक प्रश्न है वंदे मातरम् गीत का, तो इसकी किसी भी लाईन में किसी भी धर्म का मान या अपमान नहीं किया गया है। ये गीत हमारी मातृभूमि को हमारे नमन से जुड़ा है। ये गीत हमारी रा­ट्रीय अखंडता का प्रतीक है। ये गीत हमें हमारे रा­ट्रीय धर्म का बोध कराता है। इस सब के बावजूद हमारी रा­ट्रीय भावनाओं पर कुठाराघात का दुस्साहस कैसे जुटा पाते हैं ये चरमपंथी? क्या यह हमारे देश की सहि­णुता का प्रतीक नहीं है? यहां प्रश्न ऐसे व्यव्तियों के दुस्साहस का नहीं वरन् हमारे सेक्युलर कर्णधारों की नपुंसकता का है। धर्म निरपेक्षता के ठेकदार इस मुद्दे पर जुबां खोलने से कतराते हैं। इस सब के बावजूद मैं कह सकता हॅं कि रा­ट्र की अखंडता सदैव रही है और रहेगी। डॉ. अंबेडकर ने जा चेतावनियां दीं थीं- एक प्रजातंत्र में जन आंदोलनों का स्थान, करिश्माई नेताओं का अंधानुकरण और मात्र राजनीतिक प्रजातंत्र की सीमाएं- वे आज भी प्रासंगिक हैं।

PROF. RICHARD HAY (NOMINATED): In fact as a new parliamentarian, I wanted to speak on the subject matter related to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s 125th Birth Anniversary.

Since, I did not get an opportunity I may be permitted to submit a text of my speech.

First of all, I pay my tribute to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Constitution, an erudite scholar, an eminent jurist but also a revolutionary who fought for the cause of the Dalits and the weaker sections of the society. His deep knowledge and enviable flair for English language and oratorical skills made him recognised all over the nation and world as a leader par excellence. He was a democratic socialist who propagated that fundamental rights have no value without social democracy. An intellectual giant of moden India, indeed.

The greatness of Bharat is not only her commitment to democratic principles and values but also her strong belief in Dharma.

Tolerance, acceptance, justice are the main pillars of Indian ethos and parliamentary democracy. From times immemorial, Bharat accepted, received with all the warmth, all the religions that came to Bharat through her extensive shores that is secularism of an high order!

Tolerance has been and will be the way of life of Bharat. All the religions survived and flourished in the Indian soil and every religion enjoys the freedom to profess, conduct and follow their doctrines. We respect every religion and cherish the most valuable trait of ‘Unity in Diversity’ principle. I believe the strength of our country lies in her pluralistic and multi-ethnic and multi-lingual people, which reflect its beauty and uniqueness.

We have been practicing secularism from ancient times. We had the best of universities in the world, when the West were living in darkness. Everything said and done, India is a peaceful country, and the spirituality of the country attracts millions from different parts of the world. 

In the Constitution, the word, Secular, has not been defined. People interpret it according to their whims and fancies.

I think, in the Constitution, it (secular) has been used to mean - a sense of absence of any discrimination on the grounds of religion. It means equal respect for all religions.

The greatest contribution of Dr. Ambedkar is to the Constitution and Institution building aside, but to democracy itself as a way of life and about citizens’ rights. He detested hereditary dynastic rule and one- party system.

Wisdom

Sympathy

Friendship
