*श्री अजय टम्टा (अल्मोड़ा) ः यह बहुत खुशी की बात है कि आज हम भारत के संविधान निर्माता डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर जी और भारत के संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता व्यव्त करते हुए सदन में चर्चा कर रहे हैं। यह निश्चित रूप से आवश्यक था। भारत में रहने वाले लोग व भारतवासियों को भारत के संविधान के बारे में जानने का अधिकार है।

डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर जी ने भारत का संविधान लिखने में अहम भूमिका निभायी। 26 नवंबर, 1949 को उनकी अध्यक्षता में संविधान पूरा हुआ और उन्होंने तत्कालीन सरकार को यह संविधान सौंपा। देश की एकता, अखण्डता, सार्वभौमिकता, सामाजिक समरसता, आर्थिक-सामाजिक-बौद्धिक दृ­िट से एक अच्छा वातावरण बने। इतने महत्वपूर्ण व्यव्ति के चित्र को सेन्ट्रल हॉल में लगाने में कठिनाई हुई, साथ ही अंबेडकर जी को ""भारत रत्न"" मिलने में इतना समय लगा, यह आश्चर्य है। श्रद्धेय अटल बिहारी वाजपेयी जी ने 1989 में भारत रत्न का सम्मान दिया। यह देशवासियों की आशाएंì व हक दिलवाया।

यह देशवासियों के लिए बड़ी खुशी की बात है कि प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने 125वीं व­ाऩगांठ धूमधाम से मनाने का निर्णय लिया है। कमेटी बनी 14 अप्रैल, 2015 से 14 अप्रैल, 2016 तक यह चलेगा। देशभर में कार्यक्रम का आयोजन होगा। राज्य मुख्यालयों, स्कूलों एवं महाविद्यालयों में मनाने का निर्णय अत्यंत ह­ाऩ का वि­ाय है।

यह और भी अत्यंत ह­ाऩ का वि­ाय है कि माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी ने 26 अलीपुर रोड, अंबेडकर जी के निवास को भव्य स्मारक बनाने का निर्णय लिया है। साथ ही, 15 जनपथ जहां अंबेडकर फाउंडेशन का कार्यालय है, उस स्थान पर अंबेडकर स्टडी सेंटर व अनुसंधान केंद्र के निर्माण के लिए 195 करोड़ रूपए की स्वीकृति का निर्णय लिया है।

मैं निवेदन करना चाहता हॅं कि देश में सामाजिक समरसता लाने के लिए आर्थिक वि­ामता को दूर करने के लिए एकता, अखंडता को मजबूत करने के लिए भारत के संविधान के अनुरूप चलाने का दायित्व हमारा व देशवासियों का है।

SHRI BALKA SUMAN (PEDDAPALLI) : I am very much happy to be part of the debate to commemorate the Constitution on the eve of Dr. Ambedkar's 125th Birth Anniversary. Whole world has recognised intellectual contribution of Ambedkar and he is listed among the top intellectuals of the world. As Chairman of the Indian Constitution, he put all his efforts in shaping the Indian Constitution as one of the best Constitution in the world. But it is very unfortunate that there are some section who branded him as leader of untouchables and trying to damage the image of the great philosopher through some writings. Ambedkar's philosophy and his writing are subject for research in social sciences in all top universities of the world. 

DR. B.R. AMBEDKAR SPEECH -1953, AURANGABAD. "Politics is not the BE-All and END All of the nations life". He urged them to study diligently Indians problems in all its aspects, politics, social, religious and economics and fight with own accord for the salvations of the downtrodden. "This statement of Ambedkar is a guiding force for my political career. This remains always at the back of my mind and in all my political activities and thinking." 

So long as the Indian Constitution survives the name of Dr. Ambedkar remains immortal. He lives forever in the hearts of every Indian, particularly the downtrodden. 

AMBEDKAR'S WARNING TO NATIONS ON 26TH NOVEMBER, 1949: On the 26th of January, 1950, we are going to enter into a life of contradictions. In politics, we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality. 

How long shall we continue live this life of contradictions? How long shall we continue to deny equality in our social and economic life? 

We must remove this contradictions at the earliest possible or else those who suffer from inequality till blow up the structures of political democracy, which this assembly has so laboriously built up. 

The Constitution of India established a Welfare State and a very detailed agenda for promotion of social welfare and justice was mentioned in the chapter on the Directive principles of State Policy. The underlying philosophical orientation of the Indian Constitution Makers was that an activist state through positive action could promote the quality of life of the underprivileged, deprived and vulnerable sections of society. 

The philosophical postulates of new vocabulary of liberalisation, privatization and globalization (LPG) are fundamentally different from that of the worldview of our Constitution and its makers. The current process of liberation envisages a minimum state rather than providing the state with all-pervading functions. In other words, in the context of liberation, role of the state is visualized as facilitator of market forces rather than broader functions of overall welfare of the masses. 

In the context of liberalisation and privatization the Dalit Bahujan movement is raising new questions such as demand for extending reservation from government services and public sector to private sector. Along with the reservation for dalits in private sector, the Dalit movement is raising an issue of access to resources in the emerging market economy and thus seeking to have a share in the market-sphere. Dr. Ambedkar the founding father made genius efforts to constitutionally guarantee equality to the disadvantaged section of the populations.

Constitution provision aimed at preventing discrimination and promoting social justice are -Article14, Article 15, Article 16, 17 & 23. These provisions made concerted efforts "to abolish social equality, social stigma and social disabilities in our society. 

"If I fail to do away with the inhuman injustice to the class, into which I was born, I will put an end to my life with a bullet". This was glorious vow taken by Ambedkar. Untouchability was abolished under the Constitution of free India. The vow was fulfilled, the dream realized and the ambition materialized. The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines or principles given to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies. These provisions, contained in Part IV of the Constitution of India, are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, making it the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws to establish a just society in the country. The principles have been inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland and also by the principles of Gandhism; and relate to social justice, economic welfare, foreign policy and legal and administrative matters. 

Uniform civil code for the citizens - The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India."

Legislative Competence - Concurrent List Vide entries 5, 6, 7, 9, 13.

Uniform civil code in India is the proposal to replace the personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in the country with a common set governing every citizen. These laws are distinguished from public law and cover marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption and maintenance. Article 44 of the Directive Principles in India sets its implementation as duty of the State.

Divergence between personal laws has led to controversies such as the Shah Bano case in 1985.

By the 42nd Amendment of 1976, India was declared a secular nation. As a result of this, and the understanding of Article 25, the State and its institutions have not interfered with religious practices, including in relation to various personal laws. There is a view that this principle runs contradictory to the idea of secularism which requires the State to be inert of religious considerations - and not tacitly support them by following a practice of non-interference, no matter what. Clause (2) of Article 25 empowers the State to frame any law to regulate or restrict "secular activity which may be associated with religious practice " -therefore, it is argued, Article 25 is no bar to having a Uniform Civil Code. The inconsistency in personal laws has been challenged on the touchstone of Article 14, endangered by personal laws that put them at a disadvantage.

The first prominent case founded on Article 14 was Shah Bano (1985) in which the apex court ruled that a Muslim woman was entitled to alimony under the general provisions of the CrPC, like anybody else. Following protests from Muslim leaders, Rajiv Gandhi's government in 1986 got the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act passed in Parliament, which nullified the ruling. The Act allowed maintenance to a divorced woman only during the period of iddat, or for 90 days after divorce, according to provisions of Islamic law, but in stark contrast to general provisions under the CrPC. In Daniel Latifi vs Union of India(2001), the Supreme Court upheld the Act in so far as it confined the time period of maintenance to the iddat period, but held that the quantum of maintenance must be "reasonable and fair" and therefore, last her a lifetime. In effect, the verdict did a balancing act between the Shah Bano judgment and the 1986 law. 

In Githa Hariharan Vs RBI (1999), the top court adjudicated upon the constitutional validity of certain provisions of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and the Guardian Constitution and Wards Act, on a petition claiming they violated Articles 14 by treating the father as the natural guardian of a child under all circumstances. The court held that the interest of the child was paramount and that the letter of law would not override this aspect. It ushered in the principle of equality in matters of guardianship for Hindus, making the child's welfare the prime consideration.

The Supreme Court examined the aspect uniformity again in two cases in 2015. The first pertained to seeking the court's recognition to the Ecclesiastical court, which operates under the Canon Law for Catholic Christians and not under India's civil laws. The apex court was upset- wondering angrily whether India would remain secular in the present circumstances, and calling for stamping out religions from civil laws. This case remains pending. In the second case, the court dealt with the issue of guardianship of a Christian unwed mother without the consent of the child's father. While ruling in the woman's favour, it said : "it would be apposite for us to underscore that our Directive Principles envision the existence of a uniform civil code, but this remains an unaddressed constitutional expectations." It has stated that is "total confusion" owning to personal laws governing religious practices, and has enquired as to whether a uniform civil code is in the offing.

And yet, framing a Uniform Civil Code, or any law for that matter, remains the exclusive preserve of Parliament.

Goa has a common family law, thus being the only Indian state to have a uniform civil code. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 permits any citizen to have a civil marriage outside the realm of any specific religious personal law.

Personal laws were first framed during the British Raj, mainly for Hindu and Muslim citizens.

The first President of the country, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, opposed reforms to personal laws; others included the Congress party president Vallabhbhai Patel, a few senior members of the Congress and the Hindu parties. As a delaying tactic, they demanded a uniform civil code. The women members of the Parliament, who previously supported this, in a significant political move reversed their position and backed the Hindu law reform; they feared allying with the fundamentalists would cause a further setback to their right.

Thus, a lesser version of this Bill was passed by the Parliament in 1956, in the form of four separate acts, the Hindu Marriage Act, Succession Act, Minority and Guardianship Act and Adoption and Maintenance Act. It was decided to add the implementation of a uniform civil code in Article 44 of the Directive principles of the Constitution.

These amendments disregarded the majority views while not affecting or empowering the minorities. 

The principal that all are equal in the eyes of the law must also be upheld and hence it is important to move towards a Uniform Civil Code in line with the thoughts of the framers of the Constitution that was to be implemented as society developed. 

"Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry - The State shall endeavour to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and shall, in particular, take steps for preserving and improving the breeds and prohibiting the slaughter, of cows and calves and other milch and draught cattle."

Organisation of Agriculture

Improvements in agricultural output have been key to India, with 'Bharat' still residing and relying on the field. Special programmes were undertaken to improve food and cash crops supply. The Grow More Food Campaign (1940s) and the Integrated Production Programme(1950s) focused on food and cash crops supply respectively. Five-year plans of India-oriented towards agricultural development- soon followed. Land reclamation, land development, mechanisation, electrification, use of chemicals-fertilizers in particular, and development of agriculture oriented 'package approach' of taking a set of actions instead of promoting single aspect soon followed under government supervision. The many 'production revolutions' initiated from 1960s onwards included Green Revolution in India, Yellow Revolution (oilseed : 1986-1990), Operation Flood (dairy : 1970-1996) and Blue Revolution (fishing: 1973-2002) etc. Following the economic reforms of 1991, significant growth was registered in the agricultural sector, which was by now benefiting from the earlier reforms and the newer innovations of Agro-processing and biotechnology. 

Due to the growth and prosperity that followed India's economic reforms a strong middle class emerged as the main consumer of fruits, dairy, fish, meat and vegetables - a marked shift from the earlier staple based consumption patterns led to a 'revolution' in 'high value' agriculture while the need for cereals is experienced a decline. The per capita consumption of cereals declined from 192 to 152 kilograms from 1977 to 1999 while the consumption of fruits increased by 553%, vegetables by 167%, dairy products by 105% and non vegetarian products by 85% in India's rural areas alone. Urban areas experienced a similar increase. 

Agricultural exports continued to grow at well over 10.1% annually through the 1990s. Contract farming - which requires the farmers to produce crops for a company under contract- and high value agricultural product increased. Contract farming led to a decrease in transaction costs while the contract farmers made more profit compared to the non-contract workforce. However, small landholding continued to create problems for India's farmers as the limited land resulted in limited produce and limited profits.

The 1991 reforms also contributed to a rise in suicides by indebted farmers in India following crop failures (e.g. Bt cotton). Various studies identify the important factors as the withdrawal of government support, insufficient or risky credit systems, the difficulty of farming semi-arid regions, poor agricultural income, absence of alternative income opportunities, a downturn in the urban economy which forced non-farmers into farming, and the absence of suitable counseling services. 

Since independence, India has become one of the largest producers of wheat, edible oil, potato, spices, rubber, tea, fishing, fruits and vegetables in the world. The Ministry of Agriculture oversees activities relating to agriculture in India. Various institutions for agriculture related research in India were organised under the Indian Council of Agriculture Research (est. 1929). Other organisations such as the National Dairy Development Board (est. 1965), and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (est. 1982) aided the formation of cooperative and improved financing. 

The contribution of agriculture in employing India's male workforce decreased from 75.9% in 1961 to 60% in 1999-2000. Studies hold that 'there were about 45 million agricultural labour households in the country in 1999-2000. These households recorded the highest incidence of poverty in India from 1993 to 2000. The green revolution introduced high yielding varieties of crops which also increased the usage of fertilizers and pesticides. About 90% of the pesticide usage in India is accounted for by DDT and Lindane (BHC/HCH). There has been a shift to organic agriculture particularly for exported commodities.

During 2003-04, agriculture accounted for 22% of India's GDP and employed 58 per cent of the country's workforce. India is the world's largest producer of milk, fruits, cashew nuts, coconuts, ginger, turmeric, banana, sapota, pulses and black pepper. India is the second largest producer of tobacco and rice, the fourth largest producer of coarse grains, the fifth largest producer of eggs, and the seventh largest producer of meat.

Animal Husbandry

India till recently had the largest number of animals in the world and it is one of the largest producer of milk in the world. But the number of animals is going down rapidly along with milch animals. As such there is a mismatch between the production of milk and per capita consumption of milk in the country. Whereas the population of the country is increasing manifold, the population of milch animals is on the decline. This mismatch has resulted in short supply of milk and its prices have increased manifold in the recent past making this commodity out of the reach of the poor people and the worst sufferers are children who are getting milk resulting in their malnutrition. Taking advantage of shortage of milk in the country the unscrupulous and anti-social people are producing synthetic milk on a very large scale and endangering the health and the lives of the unsuspecting people. This situation has to be tackled on priority and one way to do this is to impose a blanket ban on the slaughter of milch animals in the country which are slaughtered to consume their meat and also to export the meat to earn foreign exchange at the cost of poor children who are not getting milk essential for their health.

From the ancient times cow, 'Goumata' is worshipped particularly by the Hindus in the country. Not only is the cow's milk consumed by the people and more so by the children even the cow's urine is used for medical purposes in various parts of the country. Its progeny once grown as bull helps the farmers in cultivating their fields and grow cereals for the human consumption and the industry. Cow dung is used to make manure in rural India. Since the cow is worshipped there is a long pending demand of most of the Hindus in the country to impose a blanket ban on the slaughter of cows and its progeny in the country. Religious leaders, sadhus, saints and various political parties have consistently demanded ban on slaughter of cow and its progeny. Hence, it has become necessary to ban the slaughter of cows and its progeny throughout the country showing respect to the sentiments of majority of the people. Of late, cruelty against animals in the country has risen manifold. People do not hesitate kicking and inflicting injuries on animals and more so on stray animals. Even the owners of milch animals after extracting their milk leave them to roam on the streets and roads and these hungry animals can be seen searching food in garbage and loitering on the roads causing road accidents in which they too are hurt and wounded. Cruelty against animals must be stopped with a heavy hand by imposing tough penalties and fines on the offenders and humane approach should be adopted towards the animals.

मेरा आग्रह है कि ""भारत के संविधान"" की प्रतियां देश के प्रत्येक स्कूल, कॉलेजों एवं आमजन तक पहुंचानी चाहिए। आज देश में अधिकारों के प्रति ज्यादा उम्मीद है जबकि कर्त्तव्यों के प्रति उदासीनता है। ""भारत के संविधान"" के साथ आम नागरिक में कर्त्तव्यों के प्रति भी जागरूकता और जिम्मेदारी पैदा करने की बहुत जरूरत है। मैं धन्यवाद देना चाहता हूं आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी को जिन्होंने देश में पहली बार ""भारत के संविधान"" पर संसद में चर्चा करायी और ""संविधान दिवस"" मनाया। मैं आशा करता हॅं कि प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी के नेतृत्व में संविधान की आत्मा और मजबूत होगी, देश का दलित, जनजाति गरीब वर्ग उनके नेतृत्व में तरक्की करेगा।

*श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य (फूलपुर) ः भारतीय संविधान के निर्माण के अग्रणी पुरू­ा बाबासाहेब डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर ने समाज के वर्गीकरण एवं जाति विभाजन को पहली बार तार्किक रूप से भारतीय संदर्भों में परिभा­िात किया। डॉ. अंबेडकर का सामाजिक दर्शन यह मानता है कि समाज अनेक वर्गों के समावेश से बनता है। उसका आधार अलग-अलग हो सकता है। वह वर्गीकरण आर्थिक, बौद्धिक अथवा सामाजिक हो सकता है। समाज के वर्ग ही कालांतर की विभिन्न स्थितियों में जाति का रूप लेते गये हैं।

भारत में आज भी दलितों एवं अति पिछड़ी जातियों में यदा-कदा जो सामाजिक वि­ामताएंì एवं उनकी स्थितियों पर चिंता अभिव्यव्त होती है, यदि उसके मूल में अध्ययन किया जाए तो शैक्षिक एवं आर्थिक रूप से उनका पिछड़ापन ही कारण के रूप में सामने आता है। डॉ. अंबेडकर ने अपने सामाजिक दर्शन में भारतीय समाज को विश्व के सभ्यतम समाज के रूप में स्थापित करने के दृ­िटकोण से जिन सामाजिक चिंताओं का उल्लेख किया, उनके निराकरण के उपाय प्रस्तुत किये, वह आज भी प्रासंगिक हैं। किंतु दुर्भाग्यवश बाबासाहेब के सामाजिक दर्शन को रा­ट्र की आज़ादी के व­ााॉ में वैसी राजनैतिक, सामाजिक प्रतिबद्धता में समाहित नहीं किया गया है, जिसकी देश को जरूरत थी। संविधान निर्माण की प्रक्रिया में बाबासाहेब ने शो­िातों और वंचितों को शैक्षिक और आर्थिक रूप से आगे लाये जाने की दिशा दी और ऐसे प्रावधान किये जिससे कार्यगत वर्गीकरण और जाति की परस्पर संबद्धता का अंतर कम हो सके। डॉ. अंबेडकर के सामाजिक दर्शन की ग्राहयता को माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में बनी केंद्र की सरकार ने पहली बार एक स्प­ट सोच को स्वीकार किया। माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी की पहल पर शुरू की गयी ""प्रधानमंत्री जन-धन योजना"" के अंतर्गत खोले गये 19 करोड़ बैंक खाते वास्तव में शो­िात एवं वंचित वर्ग के लोगों को आगे लाने का शुभ संकेत हैं। जिन्होंने आज़ादी के बाद आज तक बैंक का रास्ता भी नहीं देखा था।

माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने ""स्वच्छ भारत"" अभियान की जिस परिकल्पना को साकार करने का सामाजिक अभियान प्रारंभ किया है, उससे निश्चित रूप से यह संदेश जाता है कि स्वच्छता का कार्य समाज के किसी वर्ग विशे­ा अथवा उव्त वर्ग विशे­ा की पहचान कराने वाली जाति से जुड़ा हुआ नहीं है, वरन् यह एक सामाजिक भागीदारी का कार्य है। और इस भागीदारी में लोकतांत्रिक व्यवस्था के अति उच्च पद प्रधानमंत्री से लेकर समाज की निचली पंव्ति तक के लोगों की सामाजिक भागीदारी है।

आज यह रा­ट्र बाबासाहेब डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर की 125वीं जयंती मना रहा है, तो हमें उनके राजनैतिक दर्शन का भी कुशलतापूर्वक स्मरण करना होगा। 1991 की गणना के अनुसार देश में 16 प्रतिशत आबादी अनुसूचित जाति एवं 8 प्रतिशत अनुसूचित जनजाति की थी। देश में 100 जिले ऐसे हैं जहां 51 प्रतिशत से अधिक आबादी अनुसूचित जनजाति के लोगों की है, इसी प्रकार 27 प्रतिशत आबादी देश में अति पिछड़े वर्ग के लोगों की है। देश में आज़ादी से पूर्व भारत में शो­िातों एवं वंचितों की दयनीय स्थिति पर ब्रिटिश हुकूमत के हुक्मरानों की इच्छा विभाजनकारी थी ऍर वे अपने इस दु­प्रयास में डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर का सहयोग चाहते थे, लेकिन डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर ने विपरीत परिस्थितियों के बाद भी ब्रिटिश सरकार को दृढ़तापूर्वक बता दिया कि उनके लिए देश प्रथम है और देश की समस्याओं का समाधान वे देशहित के लिए अपने देशवासियों के मध्य ही चाहते हैं। निश्चय ही सामाजिक वि­ामताएंì शिक्षा के स्तर में सुधार के साथ काफी कम हुई हैं, लेकिन अभी भी भारतीय समाज इन वि­ामताओं से पूरी तरह उबर नहीं पाया है। यदा-कदा छोटी-बड़ी घटनाएंì हो जाती हैं, लेकिन इन पर बौद्धिक एवं आर्थिक रूप से समृद्ध समाज के कुछ लोग जिस प्रकार रा­ट्र की प्रति­ठा को शर्मसार कर देने वाले बयान देते हैं, उन्हें बाबासाहेब के गौरवशाली अतीत से कुछ सीख लेनी चाहिए।

भारतीय जनता पार्टी की अगुवाई में रा­ट्रीय जनतांत्रिक गठबंधन की वर्तमान केंद्रीय सरकार ने डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर के सामाजिक एवं राजनैतिक दर्शन को कार्य रूप मे परिणित करने के लिए सार्थक प्रयास शुरू किये हैं, जिनसे भारतीय समाज का जीवन स्तर निश्चय ही ऊंìचा होगा। आवश्यकता इस बात की है कि सामाजिक पुनर्जागरण और सर्वांगीण विकास के प्रयासों को सभी स्तरों पर सामाजिक प्रतिबद्धता के साथ ही राजनैतिक प्रतिबद्धता का संबल प्राप्त हो। यदि ऐसा हो सका तो डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर के 125वीं जयंती व­ाऩ में यह उनके प्रति कृतज्ञ रा­ट्र की सच्ची श्रद्धांजलि होगी।

SHRI C.N. JAYADEVAN (THRISSUR): Madam Speaker, on the 66th anniversary of adopting the Constitution of India, as we, the Members of the 16th Parliament of India, gather here to mark its anniversary, I find it extremely spirited to remind the House that the very idea of a Constituent Assembly was put forward by Shri M.N. Ray, a pioneer communist in India and an advocate of radical democracy. This was then taken up by the national leaders and through the process of deliberation, conclusion, adoption, implementation and subsequent amendments finally culminated in a form today that has made this very meeting possible.

The Constitution of India has its very birth from an assemblage of all sections of society, that is, Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, Anglo-Indians, Christians, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and also women. The Constituent Assembly has imbibed tolerance, secularism and nationalism in the very blood and breath of the Constitution from day one.

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Constitution, who devoted his entire life to fight against casteist tyranny, has played a leading role in keeping the Constitution an all encompassing, rational, liberal and forward thinking text of guidelines and rules. The Indian democratic set up that he envisaged did not bear the elements of blind faith, discrimination, unwarranted restrictions and a constricted thinking.

During the last 66 years of its adoption, we have enacted about 100 amendments to our Constitution with respect to social justice, agrarian reforms, re-writing the map of Indian federalism by creating more and more States, extending the period of reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies. There are also amendments with regard to reservation of quota for OBC in Government and private educational institutions etc., enriching the quality and contents of the Constitution. 

The 42nd Amendment of 1976 was an important one curbing some fundamental rights and imposing some fundamental duties and also adding the words ‘secular’ and ‘socialist’ to the Preamble. Likewise 73rd and 74th Amendments in 1992 provided for direct elections in panchayats and urban local bodies thereby strengthening the Panchayati Raj System. 

Unfortunately, there have been concerted attempts from different quarters to deny the fundamental rights to various sections of society and to change the Preamble of the Constitution. For example, on the occasion of the Republic Day celebrations this year, the original Preamble was given in a Government advertisement which does not include the words ‘secular’ and ‘socialist’. Instead of owning the mistake, a Union Minister said that there should be a debate on this issue, giving an impression that the Ruling establishment does not accept the amended Preamble of the Constitution. One political party of the Ruling alliance went further saying that if Pakistan was carved out after partition for Muslims then, the rest of the country is a Hindu Rashtra. Yesterday, our hon. Home Minister himself has suggested that the word ‘secular’ should be removed from the Preamble. Such a move should be opposed at any cost.

*श्री राजेन्द्र अग्रवाल (मेरठ) ः सबसे पहले मैं संविधान सभा के सभी माननीय सदस्यों तथा विशे­ाकर डॉ. बाबासाहेब अम्बेडकर को अपनी विनम्र श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित करता हॅं।

66 व­ाऩ पहले 26 नवंबर, 1949 को भारत को यह संविधान समर्पित किया गया था, ऐसा कहें कि भारत की जनता ने भारत के संविधान को आत्मार्पित किया था। स्वाभाविक रूप से 26 नवंबर, हमारा संविधान दिवस है तथा इस नाते इसे समारोहपूर्वक मनाने का निर्णय करने वाली आदरणीय नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व वाली वर्तमान सरकार का मैं अभिनदंन करता हॅं। आज "संविधान दिवस" के अवसर पर हो रही यह चर्चा पूज्य बाबासाहेब की 125वीं जयंती पर हो रहे आयोजनों के भाग के रूप में की जा रही है।

बाबासाहेब का व्यव्तित्व अद्भुत था। उनके व्यव्तित्व के विभिन्न आयामों को देखकर आश्चर्य होता है। हृदय उनके प्रति अगाध श्रद्धा से भर जाता है। आश्चर्य एवं श्रद्धा तब और भी गहरी हो जाती है जब अस्पृश्यता के महारोग से ग्रस्त समाज के वंचित वर्ग में जन्म लेने वाले बालक भीम की अखंड संघ­ाऩगाथा का हम स्मरण करते हैं।

आपातकाल के दौरान मैं जेल में रहा। धनन्जय कीर द्वारा लिखी गई बाबासाहेब की जीवनी मैंने जेल में पढ़ी। पढ़ते समय मैं व्यथित हो जाता था। हिंदू समाज में व्याप्त अस्पृश्यता के कारण पग-पग पर होने वाले उनके अपमान से मैं विचलित हो जाता था। अपने समाज बंधुओं के ही द्वारा दिया गया अपमान का जितना वि­ा बाबासाहेब ने पीया, यदि बाबासाहेब भगवान शिव के समान अपने कंठ में न रोककर उसे उगल देते तो यह समाज, यह देश टूट जाता।

माननीय खड़गे जी ने अपने भा­ाण में इस बात का उल्लेख किया था कि समाज की व्यवस्था तथा उसके द्वारा दी गई पीड़ा से आहत बाबासाहेब ने घो­ाणा की थी कि मेरा हिंदू के नाते जन्म अवश्य हुआ है पर मैं हिंदू रहकर मरूंगा नहीं। निस्संदेह उन्होंने हिंदू धर्म छोड़कर बौद्ध धर्म स्वीकार किया, परन्तु यह भी सत्य है कि अनेक प्रकार के प्रलोभनों के बाद भी बाबासाहेब ने मुस्लिम अथवा ईसाई होना स्वीकार नहीं किया। बाबासाहेब ने जहां हिंदू नहीं रहने के कारण बताये, वहीं मुस्लिम अथवा ईसाई न होने के कारणों का भी उल्लेख किया है। मैं उसके विस्तार में नहीं जाना चाहता परंतु मैं यह अवश्य दोहराना चाहता हॅं कि यदि बाबासाहेब ने अपमान के वि­ा को मुस्लिम अथवा ईसाई होकर उगल दिया होता तो यह समाज, यह देश टूट जाता। वस्तुतः बाबासाहेब संविधान निर्माता तो हैं ही, साथ ही समाज को संभालने वाले, बांधने वाले तथा सबको साथ लेकर चलने वाला बाबासाहेब इस युग के "शिव" भी हैं। मैं उनकी 125वीं जयंती के इस समारोह में उनको शतशः प्रणाम करता हॅं।

यह चर्चा भारत के संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता पर हो रही है। कल यू.पी.ए. की अध्यक्षा श्रीमती सोनिया गांधी ने बाबासाहेब को उदधृत करते हुए कहा कि संविधान का व्यवहारिक अमल केवल संविधान की अपनी प्रकृति पर ही निर्भर नहीं करता, संविधान की भावना का भी उतना ही महत्व है जितना उसके शब्दों का। संविधान पर अमल करने वाले लोगों की नीयत कैसी है, यह भी महत्वपूर्ण है। संविधान की इस आत्मा (स्पिरिट) की अवमानना तो निरंतर कांग्रेस द्वारा की गई है। माननीय मंत्री श्री थावर चन्द गहलौत द्वारा कल अपने भा­ाण में कांग्रेस द्वारा संविधान की अवमानना के अनेक उदाहरण दिए गए थे, मैं उन्हें दोहराना नहीं चाहता, लेकिन एक बात मैं आग्रहपूर्वक कहना चाहता हॅं कि संविधान के प्रति हमारी प्रतिबद्धता का अर्थ है प्रत्येक नागरिक को समान अवसर की उपलब्धता। वोट बैंक की राजनीति ने इसे बहुत नुकसान पहॅंचाया है। अल्पसंख्यकों की बात की जाती है, उनके अधिकारों की चिंता की जाती है, परंतु क्या वास्तव में यह चिंता की जाती है? यदि यह चिंता की जाती है तो सभी अल्पसंख्यकों की, की जाती। चर्चा एवं चिंता केवल उन अल्पसंख्यकों की होती है, जो वोट बैंक के रूप में राजनीतिक सत्ता तक पहॅंचा सकते हैं। जातीय समूहों की बात भी प्रायः समान अवसरों के निर्माण के लिए नहीं, राजनैतिक स्वार्थ की पूर्ति के लिए की जाती है। वोट बैंक की यह राजनीति अत्यंत घातक है, संविधान की आत्मा का उल्लंघन है। यह सबको समान अवसर नहीं देती केवल समाज को जातीय व धार्मिक गुटों में बांटती है। इसे रोके जाने का उपाय होना चाहिए। "सबका साथ-सबका विकास" यही ""संविधान के प्रति हमारी प्रतिबद्धता"" का प्रमाण हो सकता है।

लोकतंत्र के सबसे बड़े मंदिर में आज हम यह चर्चा कर रहे हैं। लोकतंत्र के संचालन में वाद-विवाद तथा संवाद का बड़ा महत्व है। यहां वाद-विवाद तो होता है परंतु संवाद नहीं होता। संसद के बाहर अनेक प्रकार की बातें हम कहते हैं- वहां भी सामाजिक, राजनीतिक मर्यादा का पालन आवश्यक है, परंतु संसद में बोलते समय हमारी जिम्मेदारी बहुत अधिक होती है। मैं देखता हॅं तथा इसकी मुझे चिंता होती है कि संसद में वाद-विवाद तो है संवाद नहीं है। अभी कल ही हुई चर्चा के मैं एक-दो उदाहरण देता हॅं। चर्चा का आरंभ करते हुए माननीय गृह मंत्री जी ने संविधान के प्रियेम्बल की चर्चा की तथा आपातकाल के दौरान 1976 में किए गए 42 वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा इसमें सेक्युलर तथा समाजवादी शब्दों के जोड़े जाने का उल्लेख किया। उनका भा­ाण यदि पढ़ें तो स्प­ट है कि उन्होंने कहीं भी "सेक्युलरिज्म" का विरोध नहीं किया। उन्होंने इस संबंध में केवल दो बातें कहीं- एक, सेक्युलरिज्म का वास्तविक अर्थ धर्मनिरपेक्षता नहीं पंथनिरपेक्षता है तथा दो, यह पंथनिरपेक्षता हमारे देश के स्वभाव में है जिस कारण संविधान निर्माताओं ने इस शब्द को प्रियेम्बल में लिखना जरूरी नहीं समझा। मैं समझता हॅं कि बात बड़ी स्प­ट है परंतु संसद के अनेक माननीय सदस्यों ने विशे­ाकर अत्यंत वरि­ठ सदस्यों श्री तारिक अनवर तथा श्री मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे ने अपने भा­ाण में इसका उल्लेख इस प्रकार किया जैसे कि श्री राजनाथ जी तथा यह सरकार पंथनिरपेक्षता अथवा उसके अनुसार धर्मनिरपेक्षता या सेक्युलरिज्म के खिलाफ है। संसद मे संवाद का यह अभाव मुझे प्रायः ध्यान में आता है। हम अपनी बात कहें परंतु दूसरों की बात भी समझें-अन्यथा संवाद कैसे होगा। स्थायी समितियों की बैठकों में यह संवाद थोड़ा बहुत दिखाई देता है, परंतु इसे संसद की बहस में भी दिखना चाहिए। आज इस ऐतिहासिक चर्चा में भाग लेते हुए मेरा आपसे यह अनुरोध है कि आवश्यक नियम बनाकर अथवा नियमों में परिवर्तन/संशोधन करके संसद के वाद-विवाद में इस संवाद तत्व का समावेश किया जाना चाहिए। लोकतंत्र की यशस्विता के लिए तथा संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता के लिए यह बहुत आवश्यक है।

*श्री दिलीपकुमार मनसुखलाल गांधी (अहमदनगर) ः आदरणीय डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर जी अर्थात् बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर की 125वीं जयंती के उपलक्ष्य में संविधान पर कल से चर्चा का आरंभ हुआ। अपने चर्चा की शुरूआत करते हुए संविधान के वि­ाय पर बहुत ही सशव्त शब्दों का, सजृनशीलता के साथ सामर्थ्यवान शब्दों का चयन करके डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर और उनके सभी साथियों के योगदान की सराहना करके इस देश की एकता एवं अखंडता के साथ देश दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा लोकतंत्रिक देश बनने पर गर्व महसूस किया। इसी के साथ ही आदरणीय श्री राजनाथ सिंह, श्री वैंकेया नायडु, श्रीमती सोनिया गांधी, श्री मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे, श्री रामविलास पासवान, श्री थावर चंद गहलौत जैसे अनेकानेक गणमान्य वव्ताओं का संविधान संबंधी विचार सुनने का अवसर मिला। इससे हमारे संविधान से संबंधित ज्ञान में वृद्धि हो गयी है और अपने देश के उज्ज्वल भव­य के लिए हम किस प्रकार जिम्मेदारी का पालन करना चाहिए इसकी जानकारी मिली। पूरा देश हमारे संविधान की चर्चा देख रहा है। अलग-अलग राजनैतिक दलों के सांसद होते हुए भी हम संसद में किस प्रकार विवेकपूर्ण आाचरण कर रहे हैं। अपनी प्रतिभा का कैसा उपयोग कर रहे हैं। हमारे संविधान पर हर एक सांसद का चिंतन और गरीबों के उत्क­ाऩ पर चर्चा चली है। हम इस संविधान पर चर्चा करते हुए क्या हम एक नया विचार कर सकते हैं? क्योंकि हमारे देश में ग्राम पंचायत से लेकर रा­ट्रपति चुनाव तक सभी चुनाव हर पांच साल में एक ही साथ कर सकते हैं क्या? अगर ऐसा किया तो देश के विकास के लिए गति मिलेगी और तो बार-बार आचार संहिता के कारण देश के विकास में बाधा आती है। उससे हमें निजात मिलेगी। संविधान के दायरे में रहते हुए अगर हमने ऐसा निर्णय लिया तो देश में एक नया पर्व शुरू हो जाएगा, इसलिए इस सुझाव पर गंभीरता से विचार किया जाये।

संविधान में न्यायपालिका, चुनाव आयोग और मीडिया इन सभी की सुरक्षा की बात की है और इसका उपयोग भी अच्छी तरह से हो रहा है। इसका आदर करते हुए मैंने एक प्रस्ताव दिया था कि सन् 1955 से जिन-जिन लोगों का नाम वोटर लिस्ट (मतदाता सूची) में था लेकिन समय के चलते उनकी मृत्यु हो गयी, उनका नाम जानकारी लेकर मतदाता सूची में से हटाया जाये ताकि ग्राम पंचायत/नगर पालिका/महानगर पालिका/पंचायत समिति/जिला परि­ाद/ विधायक चुनाव तथा संसद सदस्य चुनाव सुचारू रूप से हो और तत्कालीन चुनाव आयुव्त श्री टी.एन. शे­ान ने इस प्रस्ताव को स्वीकार कर, पूरे देश में लागू कर दिया। संविधान के अनुसार हमने जो लोकतंत्र की व्यवस्था स्वीकारी है, इसी कारण यह संभव हो सका।

इस संदर्भ में, मैं दूसरा एक उदाहरण देना चाहता हॅं कि देश में अलग-अलग क्षेत्र से 542 सांसद चुनकर आते हैं। अलग-अलग राज्य से सांसद चुनकर आते हैं और वे देश के प्रतिनिधि जैसा माना जाता है। लेकिन 542 सांसद को नंबर 1 से 542 तक नंबर बांटिए ताकि हम देश का चुनाव कर रहे हैं और हमारी प्राथमिकता देश की एकता और अखंडता कायम रखना है। मेरे प्रस्ताव से इस प्राथमिकता को कायम रखने का प्रयास होगा और मुझे यह कहने में प्रसन्नता हो रही है कि वर्तमान चुनाव आयुव्त ने हमारे सुझाव को स्वीकार करके मुझे लिखित रूप से आश्वस्त किया है कि देश के 17वीं लोकसभा का चुनाव इसी प्रकार से होगा। आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के नेतृत्व में डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर जी की प्रासंगिकता की बात की चर्चा समाज के उत्थान के लिए की गयी है। उसी आधार पर प्रधानमंत्री जी स्वच्छ भारत अभियान,शौचालय सुविधा,जन-धन योजना, जीवन सुरक्षा बीमा, अटल पेंशन योजना, स्किल इंडिया और प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना के माध्यम से समाज के निचले स्तर के आखिरी आदमी के जीवन में भी परिवर्तन लाये ताकि वह स्वाभिमान के साथ देश का नागरिक बने। पीड़ित/दलित तथा गरीबी रेखा के नीचे जीवन यापन करने वाले और अपनी स्वयं की प्रतिभा रखने वाले अलग-अलग क्षेत्रों से बाहर पढ़ाई करके आने वाले युवाओं को अपने पैरों पर खड़ा करने के लिए रूपए 50,000/- (पचास हज़ार) से रूपए 10 लाख (दस लाख) तक का कर्ज देकर उनके मन में यह विश्वास पैदा कर दिया कि देश आपके साथ है। देश के पिछड़े नागरिकों को अपने पैरों पर खड़ा रहने का लाभ मिलेगा। देश की गरीबी हटाने की यह एक अच्छी योजना हो सकती है और मुझे पूरा विश्वास है कि आन वाले दिनों में गरीबों को उनके उत्क­ाऩ के साथ ही देश का सम्मान बढ़ाने का अवसर मिलेगा।

हमने आपके शुभ कर कमलों द्वारा तथा नेतृत्व में अहमदनगर में प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना का मेला लगवाकर चेक वितरण भी करवाया। उस समय आपने जनता को संबोधित करते हुए कहा था कि आप अकेले नहीं है। पूरा देश आपके साथ है। यहां ऋण लेने के लिए कोई भी गारंटी नहीं है। प्रॉपर्टी भी गिरवी नहीं रखनी पड़ेगी, लेकिन यह मत भूलिए कि आपके कर्ज की गारंटी पूरे देश ने ली है और देश का ऋण वापस करने में आपका पद और प्रति­ठा बढ़ेगी। 

संविधान के दायरे में रहकर एन.डी.ए. सरकार ने डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर को तथा उनके सहयोगियों का विनम्र अभिवादन करते हुए आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने दूरदृ­िट दिखाई है, उसके साथ-साथ अपने सशव्त संविधान को अभिवादन करता हॅं।

SHRI B. SRIRAMULU (BELLARY) : It is an honour for me participate in this special discussion while we are also celebrating the 125th Birth Anniversary of Baba Saheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Chief architect of our Constitution.

The life of Dr. Ambedkar is a saga of struggle for dignity, rights and equality. He had to confront the curse of caste discrimination right from his childhood and continued to suffer the ignominy all through his life due to the prevailing caste prejudices in our society.

"The way he will be remembered most will be as a symbol of the revolt against all the oppressive features of ...society. He rebelled against something against which all ought to rebel."

While we celebrate the Constitution Day it is obvious to remember all those luminaries and visionary statesmen involved in the Constitution making process. Foremost among all of them was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Being the Chairman of the drafting Committee, he took every care to ensure that the voice of the poorest of the poor and underprivileged are heard. He didn't bother for his indifferent health. With devotion and dedication he could see through the arduous task of drafting the Constitution in two years, eleven months and seventeen days.

To him education make one understand the society, individual rights and add dignity and honour to ones' life. The call is relevant for our society even today and for all of us. One of the members of the Constituent Assembly was Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee who made sterling contributions to the drafting of the Constitution. 

Similar emphasis on role of education in society could be seen from Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee delivering his second Convocation address at the Calcutta University on 12 February, 1936, he said, our ideal is to provide extensive facilities for education from the lowest grade to the highest, to mould our 'educationalist' purpose and to draw out the best qualities that be hidden in our youth and to train them intellectually, physically for devoted service in all spheres of national activity, in villages, in towns and cities. 

Dr. Ambedkar not only piloted an outstanding draft through the Constituent Assembly but also outlined the philosophy and wisdom behind the various provisions. Our Constitution did not just created a republic but kept in place one of the finest basic laws guiding the destiny of our nation and set ourselves on the path of "justice, equality and fraternity" in the Preamble.

The chapters on Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State policy delineates the role of state for the welfare of the people as well as the unfettered rights of the citizens. The Fundamental Rights guaranteed equal rights to all citizens including freedom to the minorities to profess, preach and practice their religion.

To Ambedkar the parliamentary form of government was the best suited to meet the needs and aspirations of the people ensuring social justice and political recognition. Speaking about Parliamentary democracy, Dr. Ambedkar said and I quote :

"It is workable, it is flexible and it is strong enough to hold the country together both in peace time and in war time. Indeed, if I may say so, if things go wrong under the new Constitution the reason will not be that we had a bad Constitution. What we will have to say is that man is vile."

Today when we look back, our heads bow down to the visionary leaders who crafted the Constitution of which we are so proud of. We are proud of our unity in diversity. We must try to defend these values at all costs.

Our commitment to the Constitution and the underlying philosophy behind it is the greatest tribute we can pay to its chief architect Baba Saheb Ambedkar.

Our Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modiji have paid the tribute to Baba Sahib when he said, " I am here because of Baba Saheb". He is a national icon and citizens of this country will remember him as long as we have this Constitution.

SHRIMATI MEENAKASHI LEKHI (NEW DELHI) : I would like to quote the great Allamalqbal, who was quoted by Dr. Sachinanand Sinha on the first day of the first session of the Constituent Assembly of India and whose words serve as a constant reminder of the resilience of this great nation. 

"Yunan-o-Misr-p-Roma sab mit gaye jahan se,

Baqi abhi talak hai nam-o-nishan hamara.

Kuch bat hai ke hasti mit-ti nahi hamari,

Sadion raha hai dushman daur-e-zaman hamara"

These are not mere words but the reflection of the journey that our country has undertaken to date. India has survived the ravages of time and cataclysms of age, in spite of the fact that the heavens themselves had rolled and revolved for centuries, in a spirit of hostility and enmity towards us.

Today, after 68 years of Independence, I am proud and honoured to be a part of this Parliament that is working tirelessly to transform India into the ideal nation that this great Constitution had envisioned.

Any expression of commitment to the Constitution of India would be incomplete without acknowledging the effort and brilliance of the members of the constituent assembly who sat for 141 days to compile the voluminous document.

The Constitution is an embodiment of the vision of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar whose birth anniversary is being commemorated today. His thought provoking suggestions and sufficient summaries used to evoke admiration of the entire house. While speaking on the floor of the house he used to touch upon issues like a true statesman and firmly placed the interests of the nation above anything else.

The contributions of B. N. Rao, the constitutional advisor to the constituent assembly who prepared a rough draft of the Constitution for the consideration of the drafting Committee must also be acknowledged, along with the contribution of all members of the constituent assembly who put in tremendous effort and dedication to give to the nation a strong and meticulously drafted Constitution, with elements from various Constitutions.

The versatility and brilliance of Dr. Ambedkar combined with his humility and ability to integrate divergent opinions was essential to the framing of our Constitution. His burning passion to fight against injustice made him a natural leader of the oppressed, downtrodden and women of the Indian society. 

The chief architect of the Indian Constitution was also one of the greatest intellectual and social reformers of India, whose work in the upliftment of Indian women deserves special recognition. Dr. Ambedkar argued for extensive economic and social rights for women and emphasized the importance of these rights in maintaining and protecting the dignity and modesty of women.

His service as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and the Law Minister proved to be an asset to all oppressed classes and the women of India as this gave him an opportunity to translate his visions into specific policies and institutions.

The efforts of the members of the constituent assembly and Dr. Ambedkar's persistence on the matter led to the inclusion of women's rights in the Constitution of India. In addition to the rights applicable to all citizens of India, special rights were conferred upon women to protect them from societal exploitation and help them achieve an equal status in society.

Articles like 15(3), 51(A) (c) and 16 which enabled affirmative discrimination in the favour of women, added the renouncement of practices derogatory to the dignity of women as a fundamental duty and prevented discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth and residence in any employment under the state ensured that the status of women would improve in an independent India.

The Constitution also provided for equal rights for all citizens and several other articles which would establish a state based on equality and justice. Article 14 provides for equal rights and opportunities in political, economic and social spheres. Article 15 prohibits discrimination on the ground of sex. Article 39 provides for equal means of livelihood and equal pay for equal work. Article 42 for just and human conditions of work and maternity relief. 

Article 46 directs the state to promote with special care, the educational and economic interests of the weaker section of the people and to protect them from social injustice and all forms of exploitation while Article 47 directs the state to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health. 

Dr. Ambedkar looked upon law as an instrument for creating a social order in which the development of an individual would be in harmony with the growth of society. He incorporated the values of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Indian Constitution, which have proved invaluable in maintaining the unity and integrity of this diverse and vast nation.

His most important contribution to the rights of women in India was perhaps the common Civil Code for the Hindus. As the Law Minister of free India he championed the Hindu Code Bill in Parliament on 11th April 1947. Though this bill could not be passed at that time, it was later split into four separate bills and passed in 1955-56. These bills gave Hindu women rights in the sphere of marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption and maintenance; rights which are integral to the empowerment and dignity of women. Unfortunately, similar rights were denied to the women of minority communities in India, who can still be divorced unilaterally and be subjected to a polygamous marriage. Even worse is the fact that even though the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgment in the Mohd. Ahmed Khan V. Shah Bano Begum case of 1985 gave Muslim women the right to alimony the Congress government of the time, with its absolute majority, decided to pass the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 which tried to do everything but protect the rights of divorced muslim women. It attempted to dilute the judgement of the Supreme Court and denied even utterly destitute Muslim divorcees the right to alimony from their former husbands.

According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, society must be based on reason. The principle that were extended to Hindus under the Hindu Code Bill are equally beneficial for the upliftment of other sections of the Indian society, and especially the women of such sections of society. The Constitution under Article 44 envisioned that there would someday be a Uniform Civil Code in this country, which guarantee equal rights on matters of personal laws to all citizens. Such a code would be a true embodiment of the Constitution, which is based on the principles of equality, secularism and women's rights.

Dr. Ambedkar's dream of a society based on equality for all is yet to be realised. The condition of women in India remains poor even after 68 years of Independence. It ranks 101 out of 136 on the Global Gender Gap Index, with a sex ratio of 943 and only 26.6% women completing secondary education, this country has a long way to go.

This Government is fully committed to the task of women empowerment and has enacted multiple schemes like 'Beti Padhao, Beti Bacho'. The policy commitment to ensuring the safety, security and dignity of women is being streamlined through programme like NAVDISHA - National Thematic Workshop on best practices for women and child development, organised by the Ministry in January 2015. Over 28 lakh accounts have been opened in post offices across the country under the girl child savings scheme - Sunkanya Samriddhi.

The Union Cabinet on 20 March 2015 approved 33 per cent reservation for women in police forces of all seven Union Territories (UTs) including Delhi Police.

Successful linkages between SHGs and Micro-Finance institutions such as RMK, NABARD, SIDBI and other private microfinance institutions are being harnessed to help in generating additional income, jobs and in creating small enterprises for women. 

The Juvenile Justice Bill, 2014 and revision of the adoption guidelines with simplified and online processes and fixed timelines is also being implemented for the protection of young girls, and a new National Nutrition Mission is being formulated. Under Mission Indradhanush the Government also plans to achieve full immunization coverage for all children.

The Preamble to the Indian Constitution is the vision of its founding fathers. The objectives of the document are enumerated in the preamble. The values that form the foundation of the Constitution were originally justice, liberty, equality, fraternity and a democratic form of government and socialist and secular elements were added eventually. These objectives form the basic structure of the Constitution and any law violating the basic structure is pro-tanto void.

If we don't look back at history, we end up repeating the same mistakes. Today, after 68 years of independence it is almost necessary to examine the progress we have made in fulfilling the dreams and aspirations that were bestowed upon us as parliamentarians.

Numerous writers, filmmakers and intellectuals have returned their awards in the past few weeks to protest against the growing 'Intolerance' in the country. I am sure that there are a lot of people who are truly worried about the growing intolerance and have not returned their award out of any political considerations but there is absolutely no data to support that India is becoming intolerant. The entire narrative is an attempt to malign a pro development and corruption free government. 

The Prime Minister has reiterated his commitment to holistic development time and again, and spoken out against violence of any kind. This is in accordance to the vision of the Constitution of promoting a fraternal concord in the country. On the contrary the opposition that was at the helm of affairs for almost 60 years has failed to govern and lead the nation on the path illuminated by the Constitution of this country. 

India is a secular nation. Though 'Secularism' has not been explicitly defined in the Constitution and may be interpreted as being opposed to religion and the state being anti-religious, India being a tolerant nation which strives to respect all religions has chosen to interpret 'Secularism' in an inclusive manner, and the state protects and fosters all religions and religious sentiments. The right to freedom of religion is a guaranteed fundamental right. Having said that, it is pertinent to note that this freedom is not absolute in nature but is subjected to reasonable restrictions.

As an example of the growing intolerance in the country a lot of people have brought forth the issue of the 'recent' ban on cattle slaughter. Many still, challenge the legitimacy of the same and in the process of doing so have accused the Government of being intolerant. The question that arises is that, if this is proof of the Government's intolerance? The framers of our Constitution thought it fit to put in the banning of slaughter of milch and drought cattle as one of the Directive Principles of State Policy under Article 48 of the Constitution; Principle, which any government in power in this country should endeavor to implement. 

Moreover, a ban on slaughter of cattle has existed in 21 of the 29 Indian states since before this Government came to power and Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister. The Andhra Pradesh prohibition of Cow Slaughter and Animal Preservation Act was passed in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1977, banning the slaughter of cattle at a time when 219 of the 287 seats in the assembly were held by the Opposition whereas, the state of Jammu and Kashmir has had a ban on cattle slaughter and the possession of cattle flesh since 1932.

In fact, state governments in 13 states have enacted legislation banning the slaughter of cattle while the Congress party was in power. The atmosphere of intolerance and fear is only an illusion being created by an opposition who is savvy at media management. 

India is a diverse country that integrates various cultures, languages, religions and traditions. In order to keep its unity intact while maintaining a strong regional administration capable of fulfilling local aspirations and needs, the Indian Constitution has based the governance of the country and the varied sentiments of the population in various states, the Constitution authorizes each state to make its own laws on the banning of slaughter of animals. State governments in 21 states deem it fit to enact legislation banning cattle slaughter while 8 states have felt that such legislation is not needed. The Constitution has divided the power to legislate on subjects into three distinct categories. Matters of public order fall under List II, which lies under the exclusive jurisdiction of states. The Constitutional division of power makes this criticism against the Prime Minister for a State's law and order problem, superfluous. In furtherance of this cause, I would like to submit that all state governments that have come forward in retaliation have the power to amend their state law and can choose to amend it.

Converting a failure of law and order into a matter of caste and community is a reprehensible act and should be treated as a crime against the unity and integrity of India. No amount of condemnation is enough for such an act, and the ones engaging in such an act, and the ones engaging in such behavior must be prosecuted. For the 60 years that the Congress Party has ruled the country, it has failed to uphold the values of the Constitution. One of the pillars on which the Constitution of India rests on, is fraternal concord. The statements made to exacerbate communal divisions are clearly against the values the Constitution espouses.

The Directive Principles of State Policy are meant to be a guiding light for any Government that comes to power. They are meant to enumerate the goals and objectives that every Government that comes to power must strive to achieve. Though the Directive Principles don't have legal force behind them and can't be enforced by courts, their importance to the constitution is immense. The framers of the Constitution firmly believed that even without legal force these principles were integral for our Constitution as they were the ideals towards which the nation must strive. They believed that their implementation would be a benchmark to measure the success of a ruling Government and the people of the country would ensure that Governments make progress towards these goals through the power of their vote, granted to them under Article 326 to the Constitution.

The people of this country have shown unparalleled faith in this Government and elected it with a sweeping mandate. It is therefore the duty of this Government to hold due allegiance to the Constitution and work with all its might towards fulfilling the vision enshrined in the Constitution.

Even though there has been some progress towards a few directive principles, the country still has a long road ahead. The inclusion of a Uniform Civil Code as a Directive Principle in the Constitution clearly shows the commitment the framers of our Constitution had towards equal treatment for all under law.

At the time of Independence the Muslim League argued that the personal laws of the Muslims could only be effectively implemented and protected in a new nation. A separate nation, Pakistan was made to incorporate the supremacy of Muslim personal laws. The Constitution of India envisioned a secular nation based on uniform laws for all. Matters of marriage, succession and inheritance in a secular nation should not be dependent on religion. As a nation of equals, all laws must apply equally to all citizens. This goal is something that this Government had resolved to implement in it's election manifesto and is fully committed to implementing in the earliest timeframe possible. 

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mudgal V/s Union of India, 1995 observed that it was altogether unjustifiable for the government to discriminate between Hindus and Muslim. Personal laws of all religions are sacramental in nature. The Hindu personal laws were codified by various enactments and the sacramental laws were replaced n 1955-56. There is no reason for keeping Muslim personal laws. The court added "there is no justification to ignore article 44 in deference to Muslim sentiments in particular" and "article 44 is based on the concept that there is no necessary connection between religion and personal law in a civilized society. Article 25 guarantees religious freedoms whereas Article 25 aims to divest religion from social relations and personal laws. " 

When it comes to the freedom of expression, I would like to highlight that the Government has banned over 35 books throughout the country between 1950 and 2014. Out of these, 31 book bans were enacted by the Congress government. The only book ban enacted after this Government coming to power was done on the orders of a Pune Court. If the banning of books is done to preserve harmony and public order, it can still be justified, but instances like the banning of MO Mathai's book 'The Reminiscence of the Nehru Age' , Javier Moro's 'The Red Sari', Arthur Koestler's 'The Lotus and the Robot' and Salman Rushdie's 'The Moor's Last Sigh' show that some bans were enacted to preserve the image of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty, something that is purely an act of silencing criticism. 

The opposition has manufactured the entire discussion on intolerance in an effort to belittle a government working on nation building and development and to hide their failures. I would like to conclude by quoting the poet Iqbal:

'Nations are born in the hearts of poets, they prosper and die in the hands of politicians.'

It is the resolve of my Government that we will bear due allegiance to all provision of the Constitution of India and strive to build a nation envisioned by our founding fathers, base on the principles enshrined in the Constitution of India.

They have failed to find real issues to raise. This Government is committed to development and ending corruption, and is making strides towards leading the nation to prosperity. We must all as citizens of this nation ensure that no one polarizes us in the name of secularism, just to further their political agendas and secure their vote banks. We must commit to not let divisive political forces derail us from the path of development that we have embarked upon.

भारत आज विश्व में संभावनाओं के नए केंद्र के रूप में उभर रहा है तथा संपूर्ण विश्व का भारत की तरफ देखने का नज़रिया बदल रहा है। इन संभावनाओं को हकीकत में परिवर्तित करने का एक मात्र रास्ता यही है कि हम सभी भारतीय संक्रमण (ट्रांसफॉरमेशन) के इस काल में केवल और केवल संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्ध होकर अपने आपको रा­ट्र के प्रति समर्पित करें।

यही समर्पण हमें न केवल देश को विकसित देशों की पंव्ति में खड़ा करने के यशस्वी प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी के संकल्प को पूरा करने में सहायक होगा अपितु देश की स्वतंत्रता के आंदोलन में अपना सर्वस्व समर्पण करने वाली हुतात्माओं को सच्ची श्रद्धांजलि होगी।

भारत की उत्कृ­ट बौद्धिक सम्पदा का लोहा आज पूरा विश्व मान रहा है और इस सम्पदा को पहचानने के लिए, प्रेरित करने के लिए जाति व्यवस्था का पीढ़ियों तक दंश झेलने वाले हमारे सर्वहारा समाज को बराबरी तक लाने के लिए, देश को एकता के सूत्र में बांधने के लिए विश्व के सबसे बड़े लोकतंत्र को सबसे विस्तृत संविधान देने के लिए सारा देश महामना बाबासाहेब को कृतज्ञ भाव से श्रद्धासुमन ज्ञापित करता है।

DR. RAVINDRA BABU (AMALAPURAM) : Thank you very much for allowing me to express my views and concern at the historic occasion in this special sitting of this august House to the discussion on commitment to Constitution of India to commemorate the 125th Birth Anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

It is noteworthy that on 26th November 1949, 66 years before, the Constituent Assembly had adopted the Constitution of India and now this day is being celebrated as the Constitution Day in India.

Our country's Constitution is one of the best Constitution in the world as it grants every citizen Right to Equality, Right to Speech, the freedom of faith, religion and worship. Through Constitution, we have a liberal polity which ensures Liberty, Equality and Justice.

We are blessed by our great leaders, this grand and independent nation called the Republic of India. Most importantly, each citizen of the state is fundamentally given rights that are secured by the very sacred book, which we all celebrate as the Constitution of India. And, today we celebrate our Ist Constitution Day. I take the privilege to quote a few words from our preamble:

"WE THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens : JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; " 

I am proud to account that India is a nation with 22 scheduled languages, 06 major religions, 29 states and 07Union Territories. With so much diversity, I am amused and wondered when I go through the history as to how unified we are, in this diversity. In another word, "we are unity in diversity".

We have successfully been dodging the communal and economic frictions with such growing and dynamic structure. India is the only country in the world which is divided to the level of caste, and yet people are harmoniously living together.

I am happy to quote that as per the records of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation, more than 275 inter-caste marriages have been applied for financial aids this year. This shows that people are developing empathy towards each other. 

Compared to many country's histories and current unrests, India is credited with such profound and humane tolerance. Our great nation accounts for one of the major diversities and yet given the circumstances of current global economic dynamics and civil revolutions; we are in consensus of resolving instead of revolting. 

Neighbouring countries like Pakistan, face social and educational discrimination against women, while we being a secular nation enjoy the liberty and are making change possible. 

Countries like Syria, Iraq, Iran, Afghanistan, Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, Saudi Arabia and Yemen are facing political crisis, while our great nation has more religious and castistic groups, yet we are all togetherly aiming to resolve our problems. 

As a befitting tribute to the memory of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, I suggest the following :

1. Passing of Reservation Act : So far the provisions of reservation have been made through executive orders; I demand that the provisions of reservation should be made as Act. 

2. Reservation in Private Sector : Now it's a high time to introduce reservation in private sector because the Government share as an employer has shrunk after the introduction of liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation and corporatisation, in early 90's, of all the industries including Health and Education.

3. In order to build confidence among the oppressed educated youth, employment generation is a need of the hour. I also urge upon to move an amendment in Constitution of India to nullify the ruling of Supreme Court of India in Nagraj Case.

I conclude that since Parliament reflect the will of the people, the law made by the Parliament should be made beyond the judicial review and Parliament should be made supreme over any other organs. I would like to mention that Supreme Court of India has introduced a new concept i.e., basic structure which was never there in original Constitution.

I strongly feel that nothing is more important than the mandate given by the people of the country, in any election, to any elected representation. Since, legislature is accountable to the people as any wrong doing on part of the legislators can be replaced by the people in next election.

MOHAMMED FAIZAL (LAKSHADWEEP):To ensure constitutional rights to all citizens is the prime concern of the Government.

I would limit my debate to the fundamental rights which are deprived of even after 62 years of our independence and our great democracy i.e. my constituency Lakshadweep.

It’s the constitutional right of the citizen to choose the people to govern them. But in my Constituency Lakshadweep, we the people’s participation is not there in any form or the final decision making authority is not people’s representative till now. I have raised this issue in this august House to start a legislative set up in Lakshadweep and I also requested this House to form a Committee to visualize what I have expressed. But so far nothing had happened on this till now. We are geographically isolated and our great constitution gives us the right to live with equality. Till today, we have to spent extra money for our existences. Constitution gives us the right so that the advantageous enjoyed by the fellow citizens of India should also be extended to us also. With an example I would like to explain it. 

The dream of having a house or a dwelling unit in island cost almost double than that of in other part of India. There is no subsidy granted to equalize the additional cost incurred on transportation and other over heads.

When the north eastern states are given 90% coverage under NFSA, based on their geographical isolation, scheduled tribe status and climatic condition to grow any crop. Similar condition is in existence in my constituency Lakshadweep. But Lakshadweep is given a coverage of only 33% NFSA.

*श्रीमती अंजू बाला (मिश्रिख) ः भारत रत्न बाबासाहेब डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर जी की 125वीं जयंती व­ाऩ में रा­ट्र निर्माण में उनके उल्लेखनीय योगदान को सही मायने में सम्मानित करते हुए हमारी सरकार के सामाजिक न्याय एवं अधिकारिता मंत्रालय ने इस व­ाऩ से 26 नवंबर को संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाने का सराहनीय फैसला किया है। सब अवगत है कि 15 अगस्त, 1947 को देश की आज़ादी के बाद, देशहित में भारतीय परिवेश के अनुरूप नए संविधान की आवश्यकता थी। ऐसे में 29 अगस्त, 1947 को डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर को स्वतंत्र भारत के संविधान का प्रारूप तैयार करने के लिए प्रारूपण समिति का अध्यक्ष नियुव्त किया गया था। उनकी अध्यक्षता में समिति द्वारा प्रारूपित संविधान 26 नवंबर, 1949 को तत्कालीन संविधान सभा द्वारा भारत के संविधान के रूप में अपनाया गया, जिसे 26 जनवरी, 1950 से पूरे देश में लागू किया गया। आज के दिन मैं भारत के सच्चे सपूत और गरीब, शो­िात एवं पिछड़े वर्गों के मसीहा डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर को नमन करती हॅं। आज अगर मैं इस सदन में एक चुने हुए जनप्रतिनिधि के रूप में अपने विचार व्यव्त कर रही हॅं तो इसका पूरा श्रेय डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर को ही जाता है। जिनके प्रयास से ही हमें समानता के अवसर मिले। डॉ. बाबासाहेब में बेमिसाल संकल्पशव्ति, सामाजिक न्याय के प्रति अटूट प्रतिबद्धता और अपना लक्ष्य हासिल करने के लिए किसी भी तरह के अवरोध को पार करने का जज्बा था। समाज के शो­िात, पिछड़े वर्ग से आने के चलते उन्हें अनेक बार अपमान और क­ट सहना पड़ा। लेकिन वे इसके प्रभाव में अपने लक्ष्य से विमुख नहीं हुए और अपने देश और समाज को सुधारने के लिए उच्च शिक्षा हासिल की और जन कल्याण के लिए अपना जीवन समर्पित कर दिया। तमाम बाधाओं के बाद भी वे अपने उच्चतम उद्देश्य से नहीं डिगे। एक तेजस्वी वकील, विद्वान लेखक और बेहिचक अपनी राय व्यव्त करने वाले एक स्प­ट वव्ता के रूप में उनकी ख्याति आज भी प्रासंगिक है। भारतीय संविधान की रचना के लिए बनी मसौदा समिति के अध्यक्ष के रूप में आज भी हम उन्हें देश के संविधान की रचना का महान कार्य करने के लिए याद करते हैं। 

डॉ. अंबेडकर ने सामाजिक न्याय के आदर्शों तथा मूल्यों के प्रति पूरी प्रतिबद्धता की हिमायत करते हुए संविधान के माध्यम से समाज के शो­िात, वंचित वर्गों के उत्थान और कल्याण के साथ-साथ देश के सभी नागरिकों को समानता का अधिकार दिलाया। आज के दिन हमें संकल्प लेना चाहिए कि डॉ. अंबेडकर के सपनों के भारत का निर्माण करने का, जहां व्यव्ति को वर्ग के चश्मे से नहीं बल्कि समाज हित में उसके योगदान के आधार पर आंका जाए। सभी की समानता का भाव डॉ. बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर के दिल के सबसे करीब था। आज़ादी के इतने व­ााॉ बाद भी क्या आज हम समाज के वंचित वर्ग के लोगों को सुनिश्चित तरीके से सामाजिक, राजनैतिक और आर्थिक न्याय प्रदान कर रहे हैं? आज़ादी के लगभग 50 व­ााॉ तक केंद्र में किसी एक दल विशे­ा की सरकार रही है परंतु विडंबना ही है कि आज भी डॉ. अंबेडकर के सपने को पूरा करने के लिए काफी कुछ करना शे­ा है। पिछली सरकारों ने पिछड़े दलित वर्ग को सिर्फ वोट बैंक की तरह इस्तेमाल किया है। आंकड़े उठाकर देख लीजिए प्रगति अपने आप पता चल जाएगी। विकास की यात्रा में एक भी व्यव्ति वंचित न रह जाए,यह सुनिश्चित करना हम सब की जवाबदेही बनती है। गरीब से गरीब व्यव्ति को भी जब तक लाभ नहीं मिलता, तब तक कोई भी कानून या सुधार पर्याप्त नहीं है। हमें शिक्षा के अवसर बढ़ाने पर ज़ोर देना चाहिए, जिससे समाज के वंचित वर्ग के लोगों को स्वावलंबी बनने का सामर्थ्य मिलेगा। इसके अलावा हमें स्वरोज़गार एवं उद्यमिता को भी प्रोत्साहन देना चाहिए ताकि वे अपने चुने हुए क्षेत्र में अपने सपनों को साकार करने के लिए आत्मविश्वास के साथ आगे बढ़ सकें।

डॉ. अंबेडकर द्वारा प्रदत्त संविधान के मूल्यों को पूरा करने की हमारी प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाते हुए हमें एकजुट होकर बिना किसी राजनीतिक द्वे­ाभावना के रा­ट्र हित में हमारी सरकार द्वारा लिए जा रहे नीतिगत फैसलों का समर्थन करना चाहिए। वैसे भी पिछले कई सालों में आशानुरूप प्रगति और बदलाव नहीं हुआ है। विकास के मानकों पर हम अपने कई अन्य समकालीन रा­ट्रों से काफी पीछे खड़े हैं। आज जब संविधान निर्माता रा­ट्र पुरू­ा डॉ. अंबेडकर को सही सम्मान देते हुए हमारी सरकार द्वारा आज के दिन को संविधान दिवस के रूप में मनाने का फैसला लिया गया है, वो शायद पहले की सरकारों में भी हो सकता था। पर पार्टी विशे­ा की पिछली सरकारों में सिर्फ एक परिवार विशे­ा या उनके समर्थकों को ही रा­ट्र निर्माण का सारा श्रेय दिया जाता रहा है। ऐसे में डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर, सरदार बल्लभ भाई पटेल, नेता जी सुभा­ा चन्द्र बोस, लोकनायक जयप्रकाश नारायण, श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी, पंडित दीन दयाल उपाध्याय आदि महापुरू­ााो के योगदान को सम्मानित करने का एक बहुत ही सराहनीय कार्य हमारी सरकार ने किया है। संविधान दिवस के उपलक्ष्य में संविधान के प्रति हमारी प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाने के लिए एक सार्थक बहस करायी जा रही है। संसद भवन भी इस मौके पर रोशनी में जगमगा रहा है। इसी प्रकार साल दर साल हमारा देश संविधान प्रदत्त मूल्यों की प्राप्ति में अग्रसर हो और प्रगति पथ पर आगे बढ़ता रहे, ऐसी शुभकामनाओं के साथ मैं अपनी बात का समापन करना चाहती हॅं और ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम जी के शब्दों को उद्धृत करती हॅं।

SHRI KESINENI SRINIVAS (VIJAYAWADA) : On the midnight of 15th August, 1947, India became free and joined the comity of independent nations. Today, 26th November, 2015 is exactly 66 years from the day when the Constituent Assembly adapted, enacted and gave us the Constitution of India. The Constituent Assembly spent 114 days considering and debating the draft Constitution. The members of the Constituent Assembly were vigilant and scrutinized each and every word of the Constitution of India, which has been the centre piece of our democracy for over 6 decades now.

Today, we are discussing commitment to India's Constitution as part of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Birth Anniversary celebrations. Dr. Ambedkar, as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution, worked tirelessly for the idea of India that we hold dear to our hearts today-in Indian, where every citizen has equal rights, opportunities and justice.

Our Constitution resolved to establish India as a sovereign, socialist, secular and democratic republic with the aim of securing social, economic and political justice; Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality of status and of opportunity and a spirit of brotherhood among all citizens of the country.

The strength of our nation lies in the commitment of its people, parliament, governments and judiciary in upholding the cherished principles enshrined in the Constitution. There have been times, as it happens in life of every nation, when Constitutional principles have been under threat, but the firm belief and resolve of Indian people ensured that we stay true to our ethos of liberty, equality, fraternity and justice.

We as representatives of the people have the responsibility to be the guardians of India's values and Constitution. As societies evolve, there arises the need for reform and change. We as lawmakers have the duty to be alive to the changing goal posts of the Indian society and lead India towards growth, progress and brotherhood with all our energy.

In the India of 21st century, we must reinforce our commitment to our secular ethos. Secularism, not only means tolerating diverse religious and beliefs but also respecting the pluralism in our society. To build a harmonious India, we must respect each other, our individual freedom of choice and ensure that no Indian goes to sleep at night with a sense of hatred against any fellow citizen. This respect for diversity is the true hall mark of India.

When we talk about justice, we must ensure that our institutions are able to deliver social, economic and political justice. We must strengthen institutions of democracy.

The Parliament as the supreme legislative body must work harder and with a spirit of cooperation towards building a peaceful and prosperous India. We have inherited a rich legacy of erudite decision making from our forefathers, and we must not let it fritter away with disruptions. Parliament as an institutions is held high in the eyes of the people. To be held in high esteem Parliament must deliver on its words. The commitments made by Parliament to the people of Andhra Pradesh at the time of bifurcation of the state have not been delivered upon. This has led to a sense of betrayal in the hearts of people of Andhra Pradesh. It is important that Parliament and Government maintains its legitimacy in the eyes of the people by delivering on its promises to the people.

The judicial system must reform in order to ensure that jutice is fair and speedy. With over 31 million cases pending in courts across the country, people's faith in Justice is visibly shaken. We must debate as to how justice can be made quick, efficient accessible.

Federalism is the hall mark of the Indian republic. We see more and more powers and decision making authority being devolved to the state governments. It is a good sign that India is moving in the direction of cooperative federalism. Now, we must focus on empowering the third tier of governance namely the panchayats and the municipal bodies. Real decision making power should be devolved to the people at the grass roots.

The press is the watchdog of a healthy democracy. The Indian press has always been true to journalistic ethos and fearless in its reporting. However, we increasingly see a trend where the institution of press is being called names. This is a very dangerous trend. The institutions of executive, legislature, judiciary and the Press, each have a defined role to play in the success of our democracy. We must respect each institution and in turn each of these institutions must carry out their functions with a single purpose of upholding the truth. 

On this day, let us all re-dedicate ourselves to the principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity enshrined in our Constitution. I would like to conclude by quoting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on the need for the Indian in us to be above and beyond any other identity we may ascribe to.

He said, "I do not want that our loyalty as Indians should be in the slightest way affected by any competitive loyalty whether that loyalty arises out of our religion, out of our culture or out of our language. 

I want all people to be Indians first, Indian last and nothing else but Indians."
