श्री रवीन्द्र कुमार पाण्डेय (गिरिडीह) ः जुलाई, 2015 में बोकारो जिला के अंतर्गत बी.एण्ड के. के क्षेत्र क खासमहल परियोजना में दर्जनों ट्रकों में माओवादी उग्रवादियों द्वारा आग लगा दी गई। ट्रकों (डम्परों) में कोयला लदा हुआ था, जिसके कारण करोड़ों की क्षति हुई है। इस संबंध में अधोहस्ताक्षरी द्वारा मामले को दिनांक 04.08.2015 को नियम 377 के अंतर्गत उठाया गया है और संबंधित विभाग से उत्तर भी प्राप्त हुआ है, परंतु उत्तर संतोषजनक नहीं है। भारी संख्या में अर्द्धसैनिक बलों की तैनाती के पश्चात इस क्षेत्र में ऐसी घटनाओं की कई बार पुनरावृत्ति हुई है। घटना के समय समीप के सरकारी लोक उपक्रम द्वारा अग्निशामक उपलब्ध नहीं कराया गया और आज की तिथि तक घटनास्थल और प्रभावित क्षेत्र में अर्द्धसैनिक बलों की तैनाती नहीं की गई है और घटना में हुए संपत्ति के नुकसान का मुआवजा पीड़ित पक्ष को उपलब्ध नहीं कराया गया है।

अतः मेरा केंद्र सरकार से अनुरोध है कि प्रभावित क्षेत्र में पर्याप्त अर्द्धसैनिक बलों की तैनाती, आपात स्थिति से निपटने के लिए आवश्यक उपकरण (अग्निशामक) आदि उपलब्ध कराते हुए नक्सली हमले में हुई क्षति का मुआवजा प्रदान कराने की व्यवस्था की जाए।

Title: Need to increase the honorarium and salary of mid-day meal workers as per minimum wage regulations. 

SHRI D.K. SURESH (BANGALORE RURAL) : Mid Day Meal workers have been demanding hike in their salaries for quite some time. The current salary is Rs.1700 for head cook and Rs.1600 for assistant cook. These salaries are not as per minimum wage regulations. There are nearly 26 lakh mid day meal workers across the country, most of them are women.

Mid day meal workers work more than 6 hours a day for 5 days a week. These underpaid workers are the ones responsible for making the mid day meal programme successful. Unless these workers are paid adequately, the scheme meant to improve learning and school attendance will suffer.

Title: Need to appoint a full time Chairman of Rubber Board and also promote the cultivation and production of natural rubber in the Country. 

SHRI ANTO ANTONY (PATHANAMTHITTA) : I request the Government to kindly appoint a Chairman for the Rubber Board. The rubber sector is undergoing a difficult period due to the massive import of natural rubber and subsequent fall in prices. Due to the continuous, steady and steep fall in the prices, the growers are withdrawing from rubber cultivation. Most of them are not tapping the latex as the production cost exceeds the returns from the rubber cultivation. It resulted in 11 per cent drop in the production of natural rubber last month compared to October 2014. Main tapping season in the country spans during October to January, hence, fall in production in this season will affect the prospects of the rubber growers. This is the time to support the rubber growers in the country, otherwise rubber cultivation in the country will wither away in a short span of time. Title: Need to expedite the repair/re-carpeting of runway of Calicut International Airport and restore the Calicut-Delhi flight service of Air India.

Title: Need to constitute a Tapioca Board with its headquarters at Salem, Tamil Nadu. 

SHRI P.R. SUNDARAM(NAMAKKAL) : Tapioca is known as 'Cassava', 'Mandidca', a dry rainfed annual tuber crop. Now, it is cultivated in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kerala and Coastal parts of Andhra Pradesh. 

It is propagated through stem cutting. It can withstand arid and semi arid conditions in low marginal soils as single, inter, mixed crops. This is the main crop for the famers of the small, tiny fragmented lands in low elevated hilly regions. It also withstands disease and pest attack.

As a food stuff tuber tapioca is boiled and consumed directly. The tubers are also used as a raw material for extraction of starch and making sago (subudhana) from extracted starch.

Tapioca starch is very good source for ethanol production. It is also used in paper industry and textile industry. Tapioca Pearls commonly called sago is cooked and taken as food. For the reasons the 'MELINDA GATES FOUNDATION' of United States of America has identified that this crop 'Tapioca' will be the future crop for the third world country.

Due to several reasons the price of Tapioca has nosedived as a result of which Tapioca Farmers in Tamil Nadu, Puducheery, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh are facing huge losses. Central Government has formed Tea Board and Coffee Board for the Welfare of Tea and Coffee Farmers.

Hence, I urge upon the Central Government to constitute a Tapioca Board and save the Tapioca farmers. The Board can be set up in Salem as it is the trading centre for Tapioca products.

Title: Need to provide financial assistance to the people affected due to heavy rains in Tamil Nadu. 

DR. K. KAMARAJ (KALLAKURICHI) : The people of Tamil Nadu have experienced unprecedented and continuous heavy rains due to North East Monsoon during last month. The rains inundated Chennai city and many districts like Cuddalore, Kanchipuram, Thiruvallur, Villupuram and Nagapattinam. More than hundred people have lost their lives. Thousands of people lost their homes and cattle. More than one lakh acres of land and crops have been submerged with water. The essential infrastructure like highways, rural roads, railway tracks, bridges, canals and water bodies have been completely damaged. Electrical polls uprooted and cables were damaged and resulting in disruption of power supply to the Chennai city and hundreds of villages. 

The Tamil Nadu Government immediately initiated the precautionary and relief works. Thousands of people in the affected areas have been evacuated and provided with food, medicine and temporary shelters. The restoration of damaged infrastructure like roads, electricity, canals, lakes etc. are being repaired by the state machinery round the clock on a war footing. The State Government has ordered for the release of Rs.500 crore initially for relief works. 

The State Government has sought the financial assistance from the Central Government to alleviate the suffering of the people in the affected districts. The Central government should act pro-actively and immediately release adequate funds for providing financial assistance to affected farmers, 

compensation to families whose members died, their homes, cattle and properties destroyed and for repairing and relaying of the roads, bridges, canal bunds and water storage bodies. The Central Government should also come forward to waive the agricultural and farm loans obtained from the nationalised banks and state cooperative banks.

Title: Need to provide financial assistance to farmers in drought hit districts of Andhra Pradesh. 

SHRI KESINENI SRINIVAS(VIJAYAWADA) : I would like to bring to the notice of the Government that 196 Mandals in 7 out of 13 districts in the state of Andhra Pradesh have been hit by drought due to deficient rainfall. During South West Monsoon-(June 1, 2015 to September 30, 2015), the state received a rainfall of 519.7mm as against the normal rainfall of 549.1mm with a deficit of 5.4 per cent and the rainfall received during the previous year (2014) was 375.7mm with a deficit of 32 per cent for the corresponding period. 

The erratic rainfall, prolonged dry spells have led to significant yield loss in major crops. The drought in Andhra Pradesh is expected to dent the production of rain-fed crops such as pulses, whose prices have soared over the past month, alongside soyabean, cotton and coarse grains.

The drought in its second year is leading to reduced farm incomes and farm distress. The State government has taken a number of measures like provision of easy credit to aid the farmers. However, much more is needed. I request the Government of India and Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare to provide financial assistance to farmers in the drought hit regions of the State.

title: Further discussion on the situation arising out of incidents of intolerance in the country initiated by Shri Mohammad Salim on the 30th November, 2015 (Discussion concluded). 

HON. SPEAKER: Now, the House will take up discussion under Rule 193.

Shri P. Kumar.

सभी लोग समय का ध्यान रखें तथा अपनी बात संक्षेप में कहें।

SHRI P. KUMAR (TIRUCHIRAPPALLI): Madam Speaker, thank you for the opportunity given to me to speak on the issue of ‘Rising incidents of intolerance in the country’. 

For the first time in Independent India, people of all hues have openly expressed outrage on the culture of impatience or intolerance that is growing in our country presently. India is a large, heterogeneous and diverse country and also the largest democracy in the history of the world. More than a billion people need to live and work together in harmony and peace. With such a large population, even a ‘minority’ group in India has a population that is much larger than the population of many countries. The fact that such a diverse set of social, linguistic and religious groups are able to continue to live together peacefully should never be underestimated as a major historical achievement.

At the same time, the continued peaceful co-existence is something that cannot be taken for granted, nor can it be ensured by force or by harsh laws. It is the willing cooperation of all the people and the need for all the people living in this country to feel very much a part of the national mainstream which is very essential for this state of being to continue. We have to be very vigilant and watchful to ensure that this delicate balance is not upset or disturbed by hot-headed statements or by intemperate expressions of divisive opinions. 

A larger number of social groups live in this country. Their emotions and sentiments and sense of oneness with the idea of India need to be preserved and carefully nurtured. In that sense, tolerance is a two-way street, which has to be apparent in both what is spoken or expressed to begin with and in the manner in which one reacts or responds to the expressions of others. There has to be maturity and sensitivity that has to be displayed by everyone in public space, be they public servants, politicians, writers, artists, media persons or community leaders. There are times when this sense of balance and maturity appears to get somewhat skewed, leading to a sense of outrage from other sections of society.

Hence, maturity and restraint on all sides is something which is very essential to restore the sense of balance which is very essential in publicly asserting and voicing various views and opinions. We do hope that this debate helps to restore that sense of balance in the country.

Yet another crucial element is that in no case can violence be deemed to be the solution to any such problem of perception that arises.Whatever may be the provocation that is offered, resort to violence can never be condoned. It is the duty of the State to curb and put down violence firmly. The State machinery has to be geared up for this purpose. In some instances, the State machinery also has to act pre-emptively to prevent violence or unrest. Hence, opinions on sensitive issues need to be voiced with responsibility, maturity and restraint by all concerned. The Government needs to step in, in cases where some of this balance and restraint is lost.

It is an irony that those who have vowed to safeguard Constitutional rights are themselves challenging the Constitution with inflammatory statements and hate speeches instilling a fear in the minorities. 

There were articles in newspapers which suggested that there were isolated incidents, aberrations, and law and order problems. But the protests were hurting the image of India globally. What is more worrying is that such incidents may puncture India’s secular fabric.

It is more hurting to learn that this may have serious impacts on economic development of our country. In terms of our economy, top Indian business leaders state that if there is growing hostility towards minorities, there is a fear that there will be decreased attractiveness for foreign investors to put their money in India. This would jeopardize economic growth and investment flow into India. So, it will be pertinent for the Indian Parliament to send out a re-assuring message so that economically we do not suffer.

Recent developments in information and communication technology have also complicated the issue. With the use of social media, what are basically individual views can be disseminated on a very wide scale. Being individual views, they sometimes do tend to be expressed in an intemperate manner or without adequate restraint causing their own set of problems. This also sets off an “outrage” in the social media space. Unfortunately, the mainstream media tends to take a lot of notice of what the social media says although the social media often does not give adequate importance to the mainstream media. Hence, as a society, we need to be careful about how we adapt this new-found means of expressing views. 

Madam Speaker, Tamil Nadu, under the leadership of the hon. Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, has always been a haven of peace and tranquillity where communal harmony has always been preserved.

Yesterday, the hon. Member Shri Mahtab mentioned during his speech about the arrest of Shri Kovan in Tamil Nadu. He gave wrong information to the House… (Interruptions) Let me complete it. He gave wrong information to the House because Tamil Nadu Government is taking all steps to maintain law and order.… (Interruptions)

Sir, I have not completed my speech. After completion, you can respond. In this connection, I would like to say that Shri Kovan is instigating some persons by way of his activities to disturb peace in Tamil Nadu. That is why, the Tamil Nadu Government is taking action against him. This is the truth in the arrest of Shri Kovan.

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): Madam, I just want to clarify it. I was quoting Shri Jayanta Mahapatra, a poet of international acclaim who has written a letter to the hon. President of India. That was not my opinion nor was I giving any wrong information to the House. A large number of litterateurs of Odisha have condemned what Shri Jayanta Mahapatra has written in Odisha. I do not know what is happening in other parts of the country. As I said earlier, a large number of litterateurs, eminent personalities of Odisha have condemned this. He is a single member from Odisha who has written like this and has returned his Padma Shri Award. He is a Sahitya Akademi Award winner. He has come out in the Press saying: “I am not returning my Sahitya Akademi Award. I am returning my Padma Shri Award.” That has created more confusion. So, that was not my intention. श्री गजानन कीर्तिकर (मुम्बई उत्तर पश्चिम): अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं आपका आभार प्रकट करता हूं कि आपने मुझे चर्चा में भाग लेने का अवसर दिया।

महोदया, भारत में असहिष्णुता पर चर्चा करना जितना आवश्यक है, उससे कहीं अधिक इस पर गम्भीरता से सोच-विचार कर असहिष्णुता को समाप्त करने के लिए उपाय करना, चर्चा से भी ज्यादा महत्वपूर्ण बन गया है। असहिष्णुता एक ऐसी स्थिति है, जिस पर बहुत से वादी और प्रतिवादी आज की चर्चा में अपनी बात रख चुके हैं। भारत सरकार तथा देश की सभी न्यायपालिका स्वाभाविक रूप से असहिष्णुता रोकने के सभी प्रयास करती हैं। आज भी बहुत सारे कानून सारे देश में कार्य़ान्वित हैं, जैसे एट्रासिटी कायदा, मानवाधिकार कायदा, डोमैस्टिक वायलेंस आदि कायदे हैं, जो आज भी इस देश में हर स्टेट में जारी हैं। 

समाज के पत्रकारों, साहित्यिक, फिल्मी कलाकारों, राजकीय और सामाजिक नेताओं को अपनी बातें सावधानी से रखनी चाहिए। सामाजिक उत्तंडवाद फैलाने वालों को अपनी जुबान पर रोक लगानी चाहिए। असहिष्णुता फैलाने में यही लोग कारणीभूत होते हैं। बहुत सी जातियों, धर्मों और भाषाओं से समृद्ध हमारे भारत देश में हरेक समुदाय और पंथ की अपनी श्रद्धा रहती है और इसके खिलाफ आपत्तिजनक भावना भड़काने वाले और समाज में विध्वंस फैलाने का दुष्कार्य यही लोग करते हैं। सम्मान लौटाने का काम करने वाले और देश छोड़ने की भाषा बोलने वाले लोग देशवासियों का अपमान करते हैं। हमारी श्रद्धा पर अश्लीलता का भाष्य करने वालों पर रोक लगाना अत्यधिक जरूरी है। माननीय राजनाथ सिंह जी ने ऐलान किया था कि इलाज बताइये, मैं उनसे अनुरोध करता हूं कि ऐसे लोगों पर कड़ी नजर रखकर उन पर रोक लगाने और कायदे से कार्रवाई करने की जरूरत है। 

महोदया, हिंदू, देवी-देवताओं की उपासना पूजा-अर्चना करने के विरुद्ध बोलने वाला क्या अपराधी या दोषी नहीं होता है। कोई वक्ता देश की परम्परा, धर्म या रुढ़ि के विरुद्ध बोलकर हिन्दुओं की भावनाओं को ठेस और दुख पहुंचाता है। लेकिन ऐसे वक्ताओं के विरुद्ध बोलना क्या असहिष्णुता फैलाना होता है? 

जादू-टोटका आदि इस प्रकार की चीजों का विरोध करना स्वागतयोग्य है, परंतु विरोध करते समय कभी-कभी किसी धर्म का अपमान या उनकी भावनाओं को दुख पहुंचता है, ऐसे समय पर दुख पहुंचाने वाले का विरोध करना क्या असहिष्णुता होती है? पाकिस्तानी खिलाड़ियों और गायकों के लिए रेड कारपेट बिछाया जाता है, उनका स्वागत किया जाता है। पाकिस्तानी लेखकों की किताबों का प्रकाशन हिंदुस्तान में धूमधाम से किया जाता है। लेकिन इनका विरोध करने पर असहिष्णुता याद आती है। पिछड़ी आदिवासी जनता का औषधोपचार करने के बहाने उनका धर्मांतरण करना जायज है, परंतु धर्मांतरण करने वाले का विरोध करना क्या असहिष्णुता होती है? गोहत्या बंदी लागू होते हुए भी गोहत्या करने वालों के विरुद्ध कोई कार्यवाही करना क्या असहिष्णुता बन जाती है?

डा.बाबासाहेब अम्बेडकर जी के विरुद्ध बोलने वाले के चेहरे पर कालिख लगाई जाती है। अब कालिख लगाने वाला अपराधी है या डा.बाबासाहेब अम्बेडकर जी के विरुद्ध अपशब्द बोलने वाला अपराधी है। 

अध्यक्ष महोदया, मैं महाराष्ट्र की गौरवशाली बातें आपके सामने रखना चाहता हूं। महाराष्ट्र में सामाजिक अभिसरन बहुत अच्छे ढंग से चल रहा है। छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज, डा.बाबासाहेब अंबेडकर, राजश्री साहू महाराज, महात्मा ज्योतिबा फुले, अहिल्यादेवी होलकर जैसे महापुरुषों तथा ज्ञानेश्वर महाराज, तुकाराम महाराज, संत गाडगेबाबा जैसे संतों के विचारों से प्रभावित होकर महाराष्ट्र में सहिष्णुता का निर्माण हुआ है। 

हाल ही में सऊदी अरब, यमन, इजिप्ट, फ्रांस में हुई घटना क्या दर्शाती है, कौन असहिष्णुता फैलाते हैं, इसका भी विचार होना चाहिए। सहिष्णुता हिंदुस्तानियों के स्वभाव का एक हिस्सा बन गया है। परंतु कोई घटना या दुर्घटना होती है तो उसका क्या कारण है, इसका भी विचार होना अति आवश्यक है। ऐसे लोगों के विरुद्ध कार्रवाई होनी चाहिए, परंतु उनके विरुद्ध कार्रवाई क्यों नहीं होती है, मैं समझता हूं कि उससे असहिष्णुता रुक जायेगी। राजकीय लाभ के लिए सरकार के विरुद्ध जनता का मन कलुषित करने के लिए वर्तमान में कुछ देश विरोधी शक्तियां देश में जातिवाद का विष फैला रही हैं। 

महोदया, मेरा सरकार से अनुरोध है कि यदि ऐसी घातक घटनाएं होती हैं तो उनके विरुद्ध कठोर कार्रवाई होनी चाहिए। परंतु ऐसी घटनाओं के लिए मुख्य रूप से जवाबदार दोषियों पर भी कार्रवाई होनी चाहिए। व्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता, भाषण की स्वतंत्रता इसका अर्थ किसी धर्म की प्रथा या परम्परा पर टीका-टिप्पणी करना नहीं है। ऐसे समाज विरोधी कार्य करने वालों के विरुद्ध भी कड़ी कानूनी कार्रवाई होनी चाहिए, ऐसी मांग करके मैं अपना भाषण समाप्त करता हूं। धन्यवाद।

असहन और सहन के बारे में यह चर्चा जो आज चल रही है, दूसरे लोगों ने जो बात की, दूसरों के माफिक धर्म, मजहब के बारे में मैं नहीं जाना चाहता। तेलंगाना राज्य में हमारे जो मुख्यमंत्री के.सी.आर. जी हैं, अब राज्य का गठन होने के बाद डेढ़ साल हो रहा है। तेलंगाना के अन्दर एक गंगा-जमुनी तहजीब से हम चल रहे हैं। हम मानते हैं कि तेलंगाना में हिन्दू और मुस्लिम इतने सदियों से साथ मिलकर रह रहे हैं। हर त्यौहार या जो भी खुशी का मौका है, हर मौका हम लोग दोनों साथ मिलकर मनाते हैं। 

अगर दीवाली में ‘अली’ नहीं आए, तो दीवाली नहीं होती है। उसी तरीके से अगर रमज़ान में ‘राम’ न हो तो रमज़ान नहीं होगा। इस तरह से हम लोग दीवाली मनाते हैं और रमज़ान भी मनाते हैं। यह हम लोगों की गंगा-यमुना तहज़ीब है, जिसके तहत हम लोग आज तेलंगाना में साथ-साथ चल रहे हैं। 

हम लोगों को थोड़ी-सी असहमति है। हमने पहले ही दिन बताया था कि हमारा जो राज्य है, यह नया राज्य है। इसका थोड़ा पोषण कीजिए। हमें थोड़ी सहायता कीजिए। साठ सालों तक हमारे राज्य में दूसरे प्रदेश के लोगों ने जो रूलिंग किया था, तो हमारा पानी, हमारा इम्प्लॉयमेंट और हमारा जो पूरा कोष था, वह पूरा हम लोगों से लुट गया था। हम लोगों ने हर डिपार्टमेंट, हर मिनिस्ट्री से मांग की थी। हम ज्यादा कुछ नहीं मांगते हैं। हम दूसरे का हक़ भी छीनना नहीं चाहते हैं। तेलंगाना में पहले से यह भावना है कि हमारी जो चीज़ है, हम उसी के हद में रहना चाहते हैं। 

आंध्र प्रदेश रि-ऑरगेनाइजशन एक्ट के अंदर जो है, वह सब हमें दीजिए, जैसे हाईकोर्ट का बाइफरकेशन है, प्राणहिता चेवेल्ला के लिए स्पेशल प्रोजेक्ट है, एम्स के लिए बजट है इत्यादि। हाल ही में जो ड्रॉट उभर कर आया है, तो बहुत सालों के बाद हमारे तेलंगाना क्षेत्र में आज अकाल की परिस्थिति पैदा हुई है। 231 मंडल आज अकालग्रस्त है। इसके लिए हमने इम्मीडेटली 500 करोड़ रुपए का रिलीफ मांगा है। वहां कॉटन फार्मर्स आंदोलन कर रहे हैं। उनके द्वारा प्रोडय़ूस किए हुए कॉटन का प्रॉपर एम.एस.पी. प्राइस नहीं मिल रहा है। वहां पर उसका प्रॉपर बाइंग यूनिट्स भी नहीं है। इसी तरीके से, छः मेट्रो सिटीज़ को जो 100 करोड़ रुपए सैंक्शन किए गए हैं।

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: Hon. Member, we are discussing about intolerance. 

श्री ए.पी. जितेन्द्र रेड्डी : नहीं सर, यह हमारी असहमति है, जिसे हम बताना चाह रहे हैं। मैंने पहले से ही बताया है कि मैं मज़हब और धर्म के ऊपर नहीं जा रहा हूं। हमारा जो नया राज्य बना है, इसके आइटम्स के ऊपर FRBM to be raised by 0.5 per cent. हमने अरुण जेटली जी को एक पत्र भी लिखा है। डेढ़ सालों से हमारे सारे एम.पी., हमारे चीफ मिनिस्टर, हर आदमी दिल्ली में प्रदर्शन कर रहे हैं।  

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: You can raise these things on some other occasion. You have the right to raise these things but on some other occasion. 

श्री ए.पी. जितेन्द्र रेड्डी : सर, यह हमारी असहमति है। The subject is intolerance. इसलिए हम इनटॉलरेंस के ऊपर हम यह बात बता रहे हैं। मैंनें टॉलरेंस के ऊपर बता दिया। अभी हमारे एम.पी. आए हुए हैं। आंध्र प्रदेश स्टेट रि-ऑरगेनाइजेशन एक्ट में लिखा हुआ है कि there will be a wagon factory which will be built in Kazipet near Warangal. आज उन्होंने बोला कि इसे नहीं करेंगे। वहां स्टेट गवर्नमेंट ने उसके लिए लैंड खरीदी है। स्टेट गवर्नमेंट ने ऑलरेडी इसके लिए सेंट्रल गवर्नमेंट को बता दिया है। Today, they are saying no, we will not give you this wagon factory. यह जो हमारी असहमति है, हम उसके ऊपर बात कर रहे हैं। हमसे जो टॉलरेट नहीं हो रहा है, हम उसके ऊपर बात कर रहे हैं।

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: You have forgotten the Home Minister. You are only looking at the Finance Minister. That is the problem.

SHRI A.P. JITHENDER REDDY: Not only to them, but also we are having many problems. एमपीलैड्स की असहमति का नहीं है, मेरी वह प्राब्लम नहीं है। ...(व्यवधान) What I am saying is, my State is a newly born State and we are trying to build up. We have been going around all the Ministries. We have met all the Ministers and we have told them our problems. But even then we are not waiting for anybody to come. We have said we will build our own State. Our Chief Minister has, from day one, solved the problem of electricity. Today we are giving 24/7 power. 

Regarding drinking water, we have already asked the Panchayati Raj Minister to provide us funds for that but till date nothing has been given. But our Chief Minister is not waiting for that. We are not tolerating all that. We are not subjecting ourselves to wait for any person to come and give it to us. Already a Watergrid programme has been taken up. The same way we have met Uma Bharti Ji also. We have asked her to give us funds for our water resources programmes. We have not got anything. Even then we have already started our Kakatiya Mission and we are restoring all the lakes and ponds. Even for the irrigation projects, especially for the Pranahita Chevella, nothing was given. They have promised that a national project will be given to every State. Even today they have not given. However, we are going ahead with our works. So, seeing all the progress which is being done in the State also, we have been requesting the hon. Finance Minister. We have been going to the Home Minister and requesting him for the bifurcation of the High Court. Nothing has happened. Till date the division of the offices is still pending. So, what I am saying is, this is intolerance. 

Regarding the other subject, I am not telling here that my people are trying to go. यहाँ पर नहीं हो रहा है तो मैं दूसरे देश में जाकर उन लोगों को बसने के लिए नहीं कह रहा हूँ। मेरे मुख्यमंत्री जी सबका आदर कर रहे हैं और बोल रहे हैं कि इधर-उधर क्यों जाते हो, हमारे पास आकर बसो। दूसरे देश में क्यों जाते हो, हर चीज हम यहाँ पर देने वाले हैं। इस पूरी चीज के लिए मैं आपको यही बात बताना चाह रहा हूँ कि हमारा जो इनटॉलरेंस है, यह जो हमसे वादा किया और जो आइटम्स हैं, इन आइटम्स के ऊपर आप हमारा भरपूर सहयोग कीजिए। जो आपने वादा किया है, मैं कोई नया नहीं पूछ रहा हूँ, हमको जरूरत भी नहीं है, किसी की प्रॉपर्टी की जरूरत नहीं है, किसी का कुछ छीनने का भी हमारा इरादा नहीं है। मैं आपको पहली बात बताता हूँ, इनटालरेंस की बात जो बोल रहे हैं, on the first day of Parliament, an Ordinance was passed in this House and seven Mandals from Telangana have been taken away from us against the Adivasis. The Adivasis have come crying. They say we want to be in Telangana. All their villages have been submerged. So, that is intolerance. But even then also, we are not saying anything. We will tolerate everything. We are ready to tolerate everything. But whatever has been promised by the Government should be fulfilled. If that is given, there will be no intolerance at all from our side. Till date also we are tolerating whatever you are saying. 

Sir, you have seen till date we have not disturbed the House. We have not forced adjournment of the House. We ourselves have taken the complete pains on our legs and we have stood there. We, all our 11 MPs, stood there for hours and hours together. But the Government has not even bothered about it. We have tolerated ourselves. So, my request is, it should not be intolerable. Let it not come to an intolerable level. Again, on behalf of my Telangana people, on behalf of my Chief Minister and on behalf of all the MPs, I request the Government to submit to us whatever has been promised in the Act and whatever is required for Telangana. Then it will be tolerable. If not, it will be intolerable. Thank you very much.

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: Hon. Members, those who are interested to lay their written speeches, can lay them on the Table of the House. 

The ongoing discussion is on the situation arising out of incidents of intolerance in the country raised by Shri Md. Salim on 31st November. Therefore, the hon. Members are requested to raise the points only related to the discussion.

SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE (GULBARGA): Sir, I want to bring to your kind notice that this notice stands in the name of S/Shri P. Karunakaran and K.C. Venugopal and the agenda also came in that way. Shri Mohammad Salim initiated the discussion because he authorized him to. 

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: But, authorization request was accepted.

… (Interruptions)

SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE : He was authorized to speak on behalf of Shri P. Karunakaran. So, in the agenda it should not go like that. It should go in the name of Shri P. Karunakaran and Shri K.C. Venugopal. 

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: Shri P. Karunakaran relinquished his chance and authorized Md. Salim to speak.

… (Interruptions)

SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL (ALAPPUZHA): I have also given the notice. My name is there in the list. … (Interruptions)

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: That is alright. But I spoke only the name who initiated the debate. You also say that it was started by Md. Salim. Yesterday, you also spoke in the same way. 

… (Interruptions)

SHRI K.C. VENUGOPAL: My name is there in the list itself.… (Interruptions)

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: OK. Whatever you raised can be added. There is no problem in it. 

Now, Shri Varaprasad Rao.

SHRI VARAPRASAD RAO VELAGAPALLI (TIRUPATI): Thank you very much, Sir. I may be permitted to speak from this seat. 

HON. DEPUTY SPEAKER: OK, you can speak from there.

SHRI VARAPRASAD RAO VELAGAPALLI: Sir, India is known for its secularity and democracy all over the world. In fact, several countries of late are looking up to India for its vibrant democracy and true secularism. What is happening of late in the last eight months is a little disturbing and people like us request the people at the helm of affairs to arrest this kind of trend so that whatever the name India has in the world could be continued. 

First, it started with Gharvapsi. India has already more than hundred crore of Hindus who are extremely poor and thousands of temples are in a very dilapidated condition where poojas and archnas are not being done. If they are really interested in the Hindu religion and want to protect it, instead of getting into this kind of controversy they may focus on the renovation of temples and revival of poojas and archnas in temples.

I want to share here my personal experience when I was an IAS officer in Tamil Nadu. Madam, Jayalalitha, initially tried with anti-conversion law, but people resisted it. She immediately withdrew the anti-conversion law and respected the sentiments of the people. Then, she has taken up renovation of temples, conducted poojas and appointed the archikas annadhanam in several temples. Thereby she has helped the Hinduism to come up. If they really want to do service to the Hinduism, that kind of steps should be taken even at the higher level. 

Then, the issue of beef eating came up. For centuries people have been eating of their own choice. Ours is a secular and democratic country. No Government, however majority it has, presuming that it has 545 seats, has the right to tinker with the basic structure of the Constitution. In fact, one thing can be appreciated when hon. Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju said: ‘I have every right to eat beef and he challenged it if anybody could stop him.’ 

That means eating is a personal choice. In the incidents of lynching which took place at Dadri and other incidents which happened in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir, all the three people belonged to the minorities. Nobody at the helm of affairs could condemn that. At least in one incident of Dadri, it is clearly established that a BJP functionary was behind it. This is not my view. … (Interruptions) Let me complete.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI KIREN RIJIJU): Sir, the hon. Member took my name. So, I would like to clarify.

I did not challenge anybody. I just made a statement in front of the civil society in Mizoram, which is dominated by one particular community, that eating is a personal habit and nobody will come and force you at home as to what to eat and what not to eat. So, in the media, it came out as if I have gone out of the way and made a challenge to the people that ‘come and stop me’. That wrong impression was created.

Secondly, he made a statement about Dadri incident. He cannot make a conclusive remark here that a BJP member was involved. Till the report comes from the UP Government, how can he make a statement that a BJP member was involved there? … (Interruptions) No. But he cannot make a wrong factual statement on the floor of the House. … (Interruptions)

SHRI VARAPRASAD RAO VELAGAPALLI: Hon. Minister must also appreciate that I am only saying what has appeared in the newspapers. If that is the case, you can as well condemn that. If you find that no BJP functionary is involved, you can as well say that and your image will go up. That is all I can say. 

I am not against BJP or any Government. Ours is a very small party and extremely political neutral. We have no comments. What all we want to say is that India all along has been like this. The present BJP Government has to take a golden leaf from the past BJP Government where Vajpayee had said against the Gujarat riots ‘it is a blot on the democracy’ when the party in power at the Centre was BJP and the party in power in Gujarat was also BJP. You could say that. We want that kind of people here so that the entire comity of nations will admire India. I am not talking politics here. Why can we not pick up a golden leaf from the book of Vajpayee’s life? 

Sir, the incidents of killing of the rationalist Kalburgi, Dhabolkar and Govind Pansare are unfortunate and highly condemnable. Again here, what I have seen in the newspaper is – for people like us, we will not be talking politics here – that Bajrang Dal people are behind all the three incidents. The fourth rationalist was also cautioned that if he does not mend his way, he will also meet the same fate as all the other three who have been killed. … (Interruptions) If that is the case, perhaps it is right. … (Interruptions) We do not deny it. Then, why are these kinds of things going on? Why do you not say against them? That is all I want to say. 

Now, I come to returning of awards. People in a democratic country have different ways of expressing their anguish because we have lot of freedom. All along we have been enjoying it. It is not that anybody has given us this freedom; it is enshrined in the Constitution. It is unprecedented that more than 45 Sahitya Academy awardees and Padamshree awardees have returned their awards. They should not humiliate them by saying that those people are trying to pay their own patronage because after all, they got their awards with much hard work. Just as we work for politics life-long, these writers also have dedicated their lives to entertain the people and create awareness. So, instead of worrying that 50 people have returned their awards, still criticizing them is very unfortunate. When people like Noble Prize Award winner Prof. Amartya Sen said that : “It is unfortunate to live in a place like this because in the past India was extremely peaceful and tolerant, and presently it is becoming intolerant”. He has no politics, and what all we need is an eye-opener. The people have given a wonderful verdict and you have a lot of things to do like development and other things instead of getting into these smaller kinds of things.

Again, the political intolerance and statements that several MPs and Ministers are making are not required and is not a healthy trend in a democratic country, which could be avoided. By making such kind of statements, in fact, deliberately, some of the people at the helm of affairs are trying to wake up the sleeping rivals. So, that could have been avoided by the people at the top. For example, I can again mention that the Congress Vice-President does not do his homework or there is no sign of revival of the Congress or the Left Party is losing its relevance. All these kinds of political intolerance, if really that happen, all the more happy because you could continue for more years. So, that kind of hurting the sentiments of other political parties could be avoided.

Now, a good trend has taken place after 18 months and controversies like ‘Ghar Vapsi’ and so many others. Now, the hon. Prime Minister has chosen to invite the important Opposition Leaders. It is a very good trend. Now, it has been realised that instead of majority rule the broader consensus is advisable. It is a very good trend, and I hope that for the rest of the term the Government will continue that way. Thereafter, we will have a very smooth running of the Parliament, and thereby the Parliament could really contribute for country’s development where really pending issues are there like poverty eradication. We have promised this in several ways in several things. The House is for all, and in the last 18 months, at least, in my Constituency, I did not see even a single house being constructed. Is this the kind of development that we look up to?

I was one of the persons who strongly believed that the BJP is one of the disciplined Parties, and they may live up to the expectations as it was in the past. In the future also they can live up to the expectations and the people would be deciding about it. Recently, the Pakistan Poet, Fahmida Riaz, stated that तुम बिल्कुल हम जैसे निकले। You turned out to be just like us, which means she is speaking from the Pakistan soil and had the guts to say this. This means that they were all holding India in very high esteem. After seeing 18 months incidents she could say that you turned out to be just like us. It is really an eye-opener for us. Let us not give that kind of impression to the rest of the world. 

Some of the earlier Speakers were telling as to all that is happening in a State is a State subject like law and order, etc. Many of us cannot buy that argument for the simple reason that the Central Government, all said and done, is mighty. It has the IAS officers at every State. Presently, the people are highly aware of this. Even if the BJP, to some extent, may not have very big presence in Andhra Pradesh, yet the BJP at the Centre gives a voice at the lower level. Therefore, to make the present democracy a more secular country, the Government could say and advise their party leaders, party functionaries and the Ministers not to give any provocative statements. When a person like the hon. Minister Shri V.K. Singh, who held a very high esteemed post of the Chief of the Indian Army, is giving such kind of comments every now and then, insulting human beings, comparing human beings with dogs is extremely unfortunate. … (Interruptions)

SHRIMATI KIRRON KHER (CHANDIGARH): He did not do that. … (Interruptions)

SHRI VARAPRASAD RAO VELAGAPALLI: Perhaps, you should check up. People like us will not talk politics here. We are not talking any politics here. It is very unfortunate. And comparing some of the human beings as dogs is extremely unfortunate. That kind of statements could be avoided. Therefore, people have given the verdict only to rule within the ambit of the Constitution, not beyond that. 

With these words, I thank the Chair for giving me the opportunity and also my Party for giving me the opportunity. 

*DR. SUBHASH RAMRAO BHAMRE (DHULE) : I am clueless why I read these days about India becoming intolerant. I feel that India is not any intolerant nation. I think that this is merely the propaganda by some section of media. The truth of the matter in my opinion is that India is not getting any intolerant but getting more nosier and insensitive. 

The average Indian is neither very tolerant nor intolerant but mostly indifferent to the matters of caste or community, unless of course it impacts his immediate or everyday life. Thus, any average Indian, while upholding his own belief in his personal life and hourbouring some vague stereotype about people of other caste or communities, generally do not indulge in riots everyday or go on a violent killing spree.

Right from the days of partisan and its bloody aftermath, major and minor communal clashes and caste conflagration were a periodical phenomenon in India. But even then most of these skirmishes were strictly localised and had personal rivalries or basic livelihood issues than any fanatical communal frenzy for their origin. The general public never approved of such hostilities.

Even in the recent period, according to data from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), there has been 823 cases of communal violence in 2013, 644 in 2014 and 633 this year up to October. It appears that there has not been any spurt in these incidents in the recent past and the position has been nearly the same or more under the UPA rule.

So, the fact of the cases seems to be that India has remained just as tolerant or intolerant all along. But what makes the present situation more appalling is the spread of news channels and most importantly, their deafening decibel levels. 

Particularly, the role played by the social media which seems to lack both authenticity or accountability in both fomenting trouble and in equally strident backlash to events has over dramatised the whole scenario and made it appear as though the country is getting intolerant by the day. The threat to secular fabric of India is more from irresponsible electronic media and social media. 

Our visionary late President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam too realised that Indian media is too negative. Why are we in India so embarrassed to recognise our own strength, our achievement. We are such a great nation. We have so many amazing success stories but we refuse to acknowledge them. Why ? And when it comes to negative propaganda against India in the world, our media tops the list. This is manufactured dissent. And all the people who have wasted interest are trying to derail Mr. Modi's agenda for development. 

*SHRI P.C. MOHAN (BANGALORE CENTRAL) : This subject of intolerance is not at all a new incident in this country. There were so many such incidents happened in this country. During the partition, when Pakistan was created, there was a hue and cry of muslim population migrating to the territory of Pakistan but it was the tolerant Hindu population in the country which helped the Muslims, who did not go to Pakistan territory to stay and strive here. Therefore, the perception being created that Hindus are intolerant is totally misleading.

It was during the Congress Rule that thousands of Sikhs were butchered by the Congress goons, who were behind the massacre. Even now, the main Congress leaders who were behind the massacre are not punished. How the opposition could explain this act? Thousands of Kashmiri Pandits were driven out of their homes leaving all their land and wealth. They were not allowed to return to their houses. 

In 2010, a college professor, Shri T.J.Joseph was assaulted and his hand chopped off by popular Front of India when the Left was in power in Kerala. Shri K.T. Jayakrishnan, a teacher was barbarously hacked to death by the Marxists in the class room while he was teaching primary school children.

Shri T.P. Chandrashekaran was also brutally murdered by the Marxists when he rebelled against the Communist Leadership. During all these incidents nobody talked of intolerance, no intellectual returned their awards, neither the Congress men nor the Communists showed any acts of sympathy to the victims.

It was during the emergency the state sponsored acts of intolerance reached its peak. Lakhs of citizens who agitated against the black rules were put behind bars and tortured. Many Members of Parliament and leaders were arrested under MISA and released only after one and half years of torture.

Now, even small incidents here and there are being highlighted to show the Modi led NDA Government in poor light to put hazards in the steps of development.
